### ⚠️ Tooling trap that cost six false positives — read before testing any button
The Browser pane is often **hidden**, which throttles the page. Symptoms: screenshots fail
("not compositing frames"), `javascript_tool` times out at 30s, synthetic clicks appear to do nothing,
and `fetch` instrumentation is silently bypassed (the app wraps `window.fetch` itself).
**A "button does nothing" observation is NOT a finding until the server confirms it.** Six were
disproved this way: theme toggle, `+ Add Transaction`, Finance showing ₹0, `POST /library/parties`
"hanging", `Save Employee`, and task-progress "not saving". Reliable techniques:
- fire-and-poll (`window.__x = ...` then read it in a later call) instead of awaiting in one call
- verify writes by querying the API, never by reading the UI
- React `onBlur` needs a **`focusout`** event; a synthetic `blur` does not bubble

### Browser environment state at handoff (2026-07-26, end of session)
The Browser pane degraded badly near the end of the session: a trivial three-endpoint parallel `GET`
issued from the page did not resolve in **35+ seconds**, having responded in ~1s minutes earlier.
While in that state the project **Transaction** page rendered `Loading…` with `TOTAL IN ₹0` /
`MARGIN ₹0`, despite having correctly rendered ₹80,000 and three rows earlier in the same session.

**That observation is recorded as UNVERIFIED and was deliberately NOT filed as a finding.** It is
most likely the same hidden-pane throttling described above. A new session should re-open
`/c/{cid}/p/{pid}/transaction` **with the Browser pane visible** and confirm it renders the three
bills and a non-zero margin before drawing any conclusion.

## 🗺️ REMEDIATION GAP MAP — every `invoice_type` branch in the backend

R2-036, R2-041 and R2-043 are the same root cause: the invoice_type remediation introduced the
canonical constants and updated **some** call sites. This is the measured scope of what it missed —
every backend file that branches on `invoice_type`, and whether it accounts for the settlement
(`payment_in`/`payment_out`/`i_paid`/`i_received`) and movement (`material_transfer`/`material_return`)
buckets at all:

| File | `invoice_type` branches | Settlement-aware? | Known findings here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routers/billing.py` | 6 | ❌ **NO** | — (ZATCA gate, terms, match resolution) |
| `routers/reports.py` | 5 | ❌ **NO** | R2-039, R2-041 |
| `routers/tally.py` | 2 | ❌ **NO** | **R2-043** (wrong voucher types → external system) |
| `routers/bi_export.py` | 2 | ❌ **NO** | — |
| `routers/budget.py` | 2 | ❌ **NO** | R2-036 (`:146`, `:160`) |
| `routers/projects.py` | 2 | ❌ **NO** | R2-021 (`_project_cash`) |
| `routers/subcon_performance.py` | 2 | ❌ **NO** | — |
| `routers/budgeting.py` | 1 | ❌ **NO** | — |
| `routers/finance.py` | 14 | ⚠️ partial | **R2-043 cont.** — `:306-316` still binary despite the file importing the constants |
| `routers/analytics.py` | 10 | ✅ yes | R2-036 (`:223`, `:439` — unfiltered *sums*, separate from the branches) |

**Read this as:** 8 of 10 files (22 branches) treat `invoice_type` as if only `sale`/`purchase`/
`subcon` exist. Every one of them silently mishandles the six types the Transaction page can actually
create. `finance.py` is marked *partial* deliberately — it imports and uses the constants in places
yet still has a binary revenue/else ledger classification at `:306`, so **file-level "aware" does not
mean every branch is correct.**

**Recommended approach:** rather than patching the named findings one at a time, walk all 46 branches
against the four buckets in `constants.py` and decide the correct behaviour for each. Add a test that
creates one bill of **every** canonical type and asserts each aggregate/classifier handles all twelve —
that single test would have caught R2-036, R2-041 and R2-043 together.

## ⚖️ DECISIONS REQUIRED BEFORE FIXING — do not let an implementer guess these

Most findings have an obvious fix. These do not: they encode business or accounting policy, and
picking the wrong option produces code that is confidently wrong. **Answer these first, then hand the
answers to whoever implements.**

### D1 — What is "Cash In" supposed to mean? *(blocks R2-021, R2-042)*
The project dashboard's CASH IN shows billed value, not cash received (proven: a real ₹50,000 receipt
moved it by ₹0). Two coherent options:
- **(a) Make it genuinely cash** — drive from `Bill.paid_amount`. The correct calculation already
  exists unused at `dashboard/page.tsx:246`. **Requires R2-042 fixed first**, otherwise `paid_amount`
  is always 0 and the card would read ₹0 for everyone.
- **(b) Keep it accrual and rename** to "Billed In / Billed Out", leaving NET CASH POSITION as the
  cash-aware figure (that card is already correct).
**Also decide:** margin basis. Transaction tab uses ex-GST subtotals (₹80,000); the dashboard uses
GST-inclusive accrual (₹94,400). Pick one — ex-GST is conventional — and apply it to both.

### D2 — Should payroll pay a full month when there is NO attendance data? *(blocks R2-033)*
Today, zero attendance silently pays full pro-rated days, displayed identically to measured
attendance. Options:
- **(a) Keep the fallback** (sensible for companies not using the attendance module) **but flag it** —
  return `attendance_source: "recorded" | "assumed"` and badge assumed rows plus a run-level warning.
- **(b) Zero attendance means zero pay**, with an explicit override per employee.
- **(c) Company setting** choosing between (a) and (b).
**Context:** this compounds with R2-014 — if the offline queue is destroyed, payroll silently pays
those days anyway. Whichever option is chosen, R2-014 must be fixed regardless.

### D3 — Should settlement types be `Bill` rows at all? *(underlies R2-043, R2-021, R2-036)*
`payment_in` / `payment_out` / `i_paid` / `i_received` currently create `Bill` records **and** there is
a separate `Payment` table. That duality is the root of several findings: Tally exports the same
receipt two different ways, and every aggregation must remember to exclude settlement types.
- **(a) Keep both** — then every bill aggregation and the Tally exporter must classify all four
  buckets explicitly, forever.
- **(b) Stop creating Bills for settlement types** — the Transaction page's Payment In/Out routes to
  `Payment` instead. Cleaner long-term; needs a migration for existing rows.
**This is the highest-leverage architectural decision in this report.**

### D4 — GST place of supply: derive it, or keep the documented assumption? *(blocks R2-041)*
`_gst_split` always splits 50/50 CGST/SGST and can never emit IGST. The data to derive place of supply
exists (`Project.state`, party address, company GSTIN state prefix).
- **(a) Derive it properly** — correct for inter-state supply, required for accurate filing.
- **(b) Keep the assumption** but surface an on-screen caveat and remove the misleading always-zero
  IGST column.
**Not a code preference — it determines whether the GSTR-1 export is filable as-is.**

### D5 — BOQ line items: build manual entry, or stay Excel-only? *(blocks R2-030)*
There is no endpoint or UI to add a single BOQ line; the only path is an Excel import.
- **(a) Add `POST /boq-documents/{id}/items` + inline row** (recommended — BOQ lines change constantly)
- **(b) Accept Excel-only** and remove the implication that lines can be managed in-app.

### D6 — Is the demo OTP path live in production? *(blocks R2-024 — a 2-minute env check)*
Confirm whether `OTP_DEMO_ALLOWLIST` / `OTP_DEMO_CODE` are set on Render. If **unset**, the hardcoded
`+919876543210` / `123456` in the client bundle are inert and R2-024 is cosmetic. If **set**, the demo
login is reachable from the production frontend. Delete the "Create Demo Request" button either way.

### ROUTE COVERAGE (measured, not estimated)
The console contains **95 `page.tsx` routes**. After the extended sweep, **~55 were opened in a real
browser**, including every company-level module, every top-level page (`dashboard`, `projects`,
`analytics`, `enterprise`, `settings`, `reports`, `cost-codes`, `materials`) and the major
project-level pages.

**Why the remaining ~40 are lower risk than the raw number suggests:** many project-level routes
render the *same component* as their company-level counterpart, verified by comparing rendered output
(e.g. `/p/{pid}/hr` is identical to `/d/hr` — so R2-013 and R2-019 apply to both; `/p/{pid}/drawings`
is identical to `/d/drawings` — R2-006 and R2-009 apply to both; likewise statutory, production,
three-way, equipment, planning, quality, subcon, procurement, billing). Where a shared component was
confirmed, the finding was extended to cover both routes rather than the route being re-audited.

**Genuinely not opened:** `/p/{pid}` variants of todo, chat, custom-fields, depreciation, labour,
towers, wastage, budgeting, face-recognition, and a handful of dynamic `reports/[slug]` pages beyond
the two sampled (`po-summary`, `dpr`). These are the residual gap.

**An honest caveat on what page-load screening catches.** The rapid sweep reliably surfaces
fabricated data, error boundaries, dead controls and internal labels. It does **not** reliably catch
wrong-number bugs — R2-021 (cash that isn't cash), R2-025 (sign-inverted rollup) and R2-026
(hardcoded "3") were each found by *comparing two screens against each other*, not by loading one.
Any of the ~40 unopened routes could hold a similar defect.

**Coverage note:** Phase 1 remains partial by design — signup, login with correct/incorrect
credentials, OTP expiry and OAuth consent require entering credentials, which the auditor does not
do on the founder's behalf. Those items need founder execution. Logout/re-login was deferred and
not run, since it would have ended the audit session.

**Modules verified clean (no findings):** CRM, Library, Finance (main), Payroll, Procurement (page
load), Subcontractor, Statutory, Settings (10 sections), 3-Way Matching, Equipment, BOQ, Task/Gantt,
Material Stock, Towers, Wastage, MOM, Chat, Tally Sync, project-level Documents.

## AUDITOR TOOLING CAVEAT (not an application defect)
Pixel-coordinate clicks are unreliable while the Browser pane is hidden — the page stops compositing
frames (screenshots fail with "the Browser pane is not displayed"), and synthetic mouse events do not
consistently land. `+ Add Transaction` appeared dead under coordinate clicking but opened correctly
when the click was dispatched on the element. **This was auditor tooling, not a bug, and is NOT
logged as a finding.** For remaining phases the founder should display the Browser pane so true
pixel clicks and screenshots work. Findings derived from DOM structure (e.g. R2-001) are unaffected.

## FINDINGS

### FINDING R2-001 — "Material (Pending)" dashboard card is not clickable (dead card)
- **Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (no data loss; misleading affordance on the main landing page)
- **Where:** company home / Project Hub, pending-summary card row
  (`frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/home/`)
- **Evidence:** `Approval (Pending)` → anchor `/c/{cid}/d/payment-approval`;
  `To Do (Pending)` → anchor `/c/{cid}/d/todo`; `Material (Pending)` → `closest('a') === null`.
- **Impact:** the card looks identical to two siblings that navigate, so clicking it silently does
  nothing. Users chasing pending material indents get no response and no feedback.
- **Suggested fix:** wrap the card in a link to the material/procurement pending view, matching its
  siblings. Confirm the correct destination route first (`/d/procurement` vs a project-scoped
  material route) rather than guessing.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only, per audit rules (zero code changes during testing).

- **Where (exhaustive — verified by a precise emoji-presentation scan of all of `frontend/src`):**
  - `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:332` `📝` (U+1F4DD), `:344` `✅` (U+2705), `:356` `💬` (U+1F4AC)
  - `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/reports/[slug]/page.tsx:780` `⬆️` (U+2B06) — the report
    **Export** button, seen rendering live as "⬆️ Export" on the PO Summary report
- **Method note:** a naive scan of the emoji unicode ranges returns 126 hits across the codebase, but
  the overwhelming majority are legitimate text glyphs (`✓` U+2713, arrows, en/em dashes) that are
  *not* emoji. Filtering to characters in U+1F300–1FAFF plus those carrying an explicit
  emoji-presentation selector (U+FE0F) gives the true count: **4 hits in 2 files.**
- **Impact:** the emoji purge (commit `ea2b890`, recorded as "0 emoji left in `app/c/**`") swept the
  page tree under `app/c` but missed `components/` entirely, and missed the dynamic report route.
  The "0 emoji" claim is inaccurate — the single most-rendered component in the console still has three.
- **Suggested fix:** replace all four with the existing stroke-icon component (the icon set was
  extended to 105 icons in `d6f8cde` for exactly this purpose).
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-003 — Delete Logs entity filter: 2 options can never match, 21 logged types unlisted
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (audit-trail feature silently returns nothing for two filters)
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/delete-logs/page.tsx:18-27` (`ENTITY_TYPES`)
- **Evidence:**
  - UI offers: `project, task, lead, workorder, material, payment, timesheet, party`
  - Backend actually writes (from every `log_deletion(...)` call site): `approval_rule, asset_type,
    chat_group_member, cost_code, crm_lead, deduction, drawing_pin, holiday, leave_template,
    library_todo, location, material, material_category, mom, party, payment, payment_request,
    progress, project, project_member, project_party, rate, retention, salary_template, task,
    timesheet, todo, tower, workforce`
  - **`lead` is never written** — the backend logs `crm_lead` (`crm.py`). Filtering by "lead" returns
    zero rows forever.
  - **`workorder` is never written at all** — no call site emits it. Also returns zero forever.
  - 21 entity types that ARE logged have no filter option, so those deletions cannot be filtered for.
- **Impact:** two filters are permanently dead, and a user auditing deleted CRM leads gets an empty
  result that looks like "nothing was deleted" rather than "wrong filter value". For an audit-trail
  feature this is misleading in the worst direction.
- **Suggested fix:** derive `ENTITY_TYPES` from the actual set the backend emits (ideally exported
  from a shared constant, the same pattern adopted for `invoice_type`), rather than a hand-typed list.
  At minimum change `lead` → `crm_lead` and remove `workorder`.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-004 — Concrete calculator silently inflates quantities by 5% (undisclosed wastage)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — material takeoff figures don't match the formula the UI states
- **Where:** Concrete Volume calculator, `/c/{cid}/d/reports/calculators` (Concrete Vol tab);
  backend `ConcreteCalcRequest.wastage_pct` defaults to `5.0` (`backend/app/routers/calculators.py`)
- **Reproduction (defaults, M20, 5m × 3m × 0.15m):**
  - Wet volume shown: `2.250 m³` ✓ (5 × 3 × 0.15)
  - UI states the dry factor is **1.54** — label reads `DRY MIX MATERIALS (1.54 FACTOR)` and the
    reference note says "Dry-to-Wet volume expansion factor: 1.54"
  - By that stated formula: dry = 2.25 × 1.54 = 3.465 m³; M20 is 1:1.5:3 (5.5 parts), so
    sand = 3.465 × 1.5/5.5 = **0.945 m³**, aggregate = 3.465 × 3/5.5 = **1.890 m³**
  - **UI actually shows sand 0.99 m³, aggregate 1.98 m³, cement 20 bags**
  - Those match `dry = 2.25 × 1.54 × 1.05 = 3.638 m³` exactly: sand 0.992, aggregate 1.984,
    cement 0.6615 m³ → 19.05 bags → 20 rounded up. **A 5% wastage multiplier is being applied.**
- **Evidence it is undisclosed:** the string "wastage"/"waste" does not appear anywhere on the page,
  and there is no wastage input control (5 inputs only: length, width, thickness, cement rate,
  sand rate).
- **Why this is a defect and not a convention:** the **Bricks** calculator on the same screen *does*
  disclose its buffer — "Includes 10% cutting wastage buffer". So disclosure is the established
  pattern and Concrete is inconsistent with it.
- **Impact:** a QS or engineer verifying the takeoff by hand against the stated 1.54 factor gets a
  mismatch and would reasonably conclude the tool is wrong. Users also cannot switch the allowance
  off for a pure theoretical quantity, or raise it for a difficult pour.
- **Suggested fix:** either surface the allowance the way Bricks does ("Includes 5% wastage
  allowance") and ideally expose `wastage_pct` as an input, or set it to 0 so the output matches the
  formula the UI advertises. Audit the other 9 calculators for the same disclosure gap — this was
  found by checking two of eleven.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-004 (cont.) — CONFIRMED SYSTEMIC: Plaster calculator hides a 10% allowance too
- **Reproduction (defaults, 50 m² wall × 12 mm):**
  - Wet volume shown `0.600 m³` ✓ (50 × 0.012)
  - UI shows CEMENT BAGS `5.1`, SAND `0.70 m³`
  - Pure stated formula (dry = wet × 1.33, mix 1:4 → 5 parts): cement = 0.6 × 1.33 / 5 = 0.1596 m³
    → 4.6 bags; sand = 0.638 m³. **Does not match the screen.**
  - With the backend's default 10% wastage: dry = 0.6 × 1.33 × 1.10 = 0.8778 m³ → cement =
    0.17556 m³ → 0.17556 × 1440 / 50 = **5.06 bags ✓ (shows 5.1)**; sand = 0.702 → **✓ (shows 0.70)**
  - The string "wastage"/"waste"/"buffer" appears **nowhere** on the Plaster screen, and there is no
    wastage input (2 inputs only: wall area, thickness).
- **Assessment:** the gap is not isolated to Concrete. Two of the three calculators checked apply an
  undisclosed allowance (Concrete 5%, Plaster 10%) while the third (Bricks) discloses its 10%.

#### R2-004 (final scope — resolved from source, all 11 calculators)
Wastage is applied by **7** calculators. Cross-referencing the applied allowance against whether the
UI exposes a control and whether it discloses the allowance in text:

| Calculator | Allowance applied | UI input to change it | Disclosed on screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Steel (Col/1-Way/2-Way) | 5% | ✅ yes (line 581) | via the input itself |
| Bricks | 10% | ❌ no | ✅ "Includes 10% cutting wastage buffer" |
| **Concrete** | **5%** | ❌ no | ❌ **no** |
| **RMC Mixer** | **5%** | ❌ no | ❌ **no** |
| **Tile** | **10%** | ❌ no | ❌ **no** |
| **Plaster** | **10%** | ❌ no | ❌ **no** |
| **Waterproofing** | **5%** | ❌ no | ❌ **no** |

- **Evidence:** seven `useState` wastage values exist (lines 43, 75, 91, 118, 139, 145, 151) and all
  feed the computations, but **only `setSteelWastage` is ever bound to an input** (line 581). The
  other six are fixed constants the user cannot see or change.
- **Net:** **5 of 11 calculators silently inflate material quantities with no disclosure and no way
  to adjust or disable the allowance.** Bricks discloses but still can't be adjusted. Only Steel is
  fully transparent.

### FINDING R2-010 — Console calculators never call the backend; the math is duplicated
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (architecture / drift risk, and it nullifies prior hardening work)
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/reports/calculators/page.tsx`
- **Evidence:** the string `apis/v3/calculators` appears **0 times** in the page. Every calculator is
  computed locally in `useMemo` blocks, e.g. `dryVol = wetVol * 1.33 * (1 + plasterWastage/100)`
  (line 329), `dryMortarVol = mortarVol * 1.33` (line 287), paint at lines 310-312. There are
  therefore **two independent implementations of every calculator**: `backend/app/routers/
  calculators.py` and this page.
- **Consequence 1 — prior hardening protects nobody in the console.** Commit `e2646c6` added Pydantic
  `gt=0` validators, `mix_ratio` format validation (converting a 500 into a clean 422), and the
  `/brickwork`, `/plastering`, `/flooring` route aliases. **None of that is reachable from the console
  UI**, because the console never issues those requests. The validation only protects direct API
  consumers.
- **Consequence 2 — silent drift.** Nothing keeps the two implementations in sync. They currently
  agree on the cases verified here (Concrete 1.54×1.05, Plaster 1.33×1.10, Paint 1.10/1.05 — all
  identical on both sides), so **no divergence exists today**; the risk is that any future change to
  one side goes unnoticed on the other, and there is no test comparing them.
- **Suggested fix:** either have the console call the API (making it the single source of truth), or
  extract the formulas into one shared module consumed by both, or add contract tests asserting the
  two produce identical output for a fixed input matrix. Do not leave two hand-maintained copies.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-010 (cont.) — quantified: 14 calculator endpoints have zero callers
A route-usage scan over all **414** backend routes confirms the calculator module is entirely
orphaned. These 14 endpoints are never referenced anywhere in `frontend/src`:
`/calculators/steel`, `/concrete`, `/rmc`, `/house-cost`, `/brick`, `/brickwork`, `/paint`, `/tile`,
`/flooring`, `/plaster`, `/plastering`, `/waterproofing`, `/billing`, `/split-rate`.
This independently corroborates the earlier finding (`grep -c "apis/v3/calculators"` in the console
calculator page = **0**) and puts a number on the dead surface: **all of the Pydantic validation,
the `gt=0` guards, the `mix_ratio` parsing fix and the three route aliases added in `e2646c6` protect
14 endpoints that nothing calls.**

**Scan caveat — the headline number is NOT reportable.** The same scan flagged **67** of 414 routes as
unreferenced, but that figure is inflated by dynamic URL construction: e.g.
`library/page.tsx:160` builds `` `${apiHost}/apis/v3/library/${type}` ``, so every `library/*` route it
flagged is in fact called. Only the calculator subset was independently verified. **Do not cite "67
orphaned routes" — it is an upper bound containing known false positives.** A proper orphan audit
needs to resolve template literals, which this scan does not do.

### FINDING R2-011 — `party_type`: 6 of 9 dropdown options return 422 and fail silently
### ⚠️ SECOND INSTANCE OF THE `invoice_type` BUG CLASS — LIVE IN PRODUCTION
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — two-thirds of a core dropdown is dead, and the failure is invisible
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/p/{pid}/party` → **+ New Party**;
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/party/page.tsx:24` (`PARTY_TYPES`, bound to the
  form `<select>` at line 269, POSTed to `/library/parties` at line 233)
  vs `backend/app/routers/library.py:24` (`PartyCreate.party_type` pattern)
- **PROVEN IN THE BROWSER:** opened + New Party, entered name `ZZ QA Investor Test`, selected type
  **Investor**, clicked **Create Party**. Instrumented `window.fetch` captured the response:
  **HTTP 422**. The modal **closed as though it had succeeded**, the party was **not created**, and
  **no error was displayed anywhere**.
- **The mismatch:**
  - UI offers: `Client, Staff, Investor, Worker, Labour Contractor, Material Supplier,
    Equipment Supplier, Other Vendor, Contractor`
  - Backend allows (anchored, case-insensitive): `Client|Supplier|Vendor|Subcontractor|Contractor|
    Staff|Party|Architect|Consultant|Other`
  - ✅ valid: `Client`, `Staff`, `Contractor` (3 of 9)
  - ❌ **422:** `Investor`, `Worker`, `Labour Contractor`, `Material Supplier`, `Equipment Supplier`,
    `Other Vendor` (6 of 9). Note the regex is anchored, so `Labour Contractor` does **not** satisfy
    `Contractor`, and `Material Supplier` does not satisfy `Supplier`.
- **Origin:** introduced by commit `5b51a4c` ("add pattern regex validation to party_type field in
  PartyCreate") — part of the **same hardening batch that produced the `invoice_type` outage**. The
  identical root cause: a hand-typed regex allowlist derived from the field's *comments and backend
  usage* rather than from the values the live UI actually sends.
- **Auditor disclosure — this was previously cleared in error.** Earlier in this engagement I
  reviewed all 9 patterns from that batch and reported that only `invoice_type` was broken and the
  other 8 were safe. That conclusion was wrong for `party_type`. My check grepped for literal
  `party_type = "..."` / `party_type: "..."` assignments, which returned only valid values
  (`Client`, `Staff`, `Supplier`, `Vendor`, `Subcontractor`). It did not catch a `<select>`
  populated from a module-level const array. **Grepping literal assignments is not sufficient to
  verify a discriminator field** — every option list feeding the field must be enumerated.
- **Impact:** a user classifying a party as an Investor, Worker, Labour Contractor, Material
  Supplier, Equipment Supplier or Other Vendor loses the record entirely, with the UI signalling
  success. Given parties underpin billing, procurement and subcontractor flows, this is a
  significant data-entry failure.
- **Suggested fix:** the same remedy applied to `invoice_type` — one shared canonical constant
  driving both the regex and the dropdown, so they cannot drift. Decide deliberately whether the
  richer UI vocabulary (Labour Contractor, Material Supplier, Equipment Supplier…) should become
  canonical, or whether the UI should be narrowed to the backend's set; the former looks more useful
  and preserves data already displayed to users. **Also surface 422s in this form** — the silent
  close is what let this go unnoticed.
- **Remaining risk:** the other 7 patterns from commit batch `c851e64..0c05726` were cleared by the
  same insufficient method. **All of them should be re-verified by enumerating every dropdown,
  const array and default that feeds each field**, not by grepping literal assignments.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

---

## RE-VERIFICATION OF THE REMAINING 4 PATTERNS (done properly)

Prompted by R2-011, every remaining pattern from batch `c851e64..0c05726` was re-checked by
**enumerating every frontend source that can feed the field** — dropdown option lists, module-level
const arrays, `useState` defaults, and computed variables traced to their possible values — rather
than grepping literal assignments.

| Field | Backend pattern | Every frontend feed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payment_method` | `(?i)^(Cash\|Bank Transfer\|Bank\|Cheque\|UPI\|Online)$` | one site only: `finance/page.tsx:532` hardcoded `"Cash"` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `payment_type` | `^(in\|out\|transfer)$` | `finance/page.tsx:520` — ternary yielding only `"in"` / `"out"` | ✅ **SAFE** (`transfer` never used) |
| `opening_balance_type` | `^(pay\|receive)$` | `finance/page.tsx:247, 1020` defaults + `:1496/:1497` toggle buttons → only `"pay"` / `"receive"` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `opening_balance_direction` | `^(will_pay\|will_receive)$` | `party/page.tsx:225, 302` defaults + two `<select>`s at `:280, :336` → only `will_receive` / `will_pay` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `category` (drawings) | `^(2D Layout\|3D Layout\|Production File)$` | **none** — the only `/apis/v3/drawings` call is a GET (`:107`); the strings "2D Layout"/"3D Layout"/"Production File" appear nowhere in `frontend/src` | ✅ no 422 risk (orphaned endpoint — see R2-006) |

**Conclusion:** `party_type` (R2-011) was the only additional broken pattern. The other four are
genuinely safe, now confirmed by exhaustive feed enumeration rather than the earlier grep.

**Near-miss worth noting:** `payment_method` looked risky at first — `finance/page.tsx:4045` offers a
Cash/Bank/**UPI**/Cheque select. It turned out to bind to `prPayment.mode`, which is POSTed as
`payment_mode` to `/finance/payment-requests/pay/{id}` — a different, unpatterned field. Had that
select fed `payment_method`, every option would still have been valid anyway.

### FINDING R2-012 — "Payment Method" radio group is dead (selection silently discarded)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — a labelled required-looking input in a financial form captures nothing
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/finance/page.tsx:3396-3410`
- **Evidence:** the group renders `["Cash", "Bank Transfer", "Cheque"]` under a **"Payment Method"**
  label, but each `<input type="radio">` has only `name="paymentMethod"`, `defaultChecked` and a
  className — **no `value`, no `checked`, no `onChange`**, and no state binding. Grepping the file,
  the identifier `paymentMethod` appears **exactly once**: as that `name` attribute. Nothing reads it.
  The only `FormData` in the file (line 381) belongs to an unrelated upload handler.
- **Impact:** a user selecting "Bank Transfer" or "Cheque" has their choice silently discarded; the
  record is saved with whatever the caller hardcodes. In a finance module the payment method is a
  reconciliation-relevant field, so this is a quiet data-quality loss rather than a cosmetic issue.
- **Suggested fix:** bind the group to state and include it in the submit payload (the backend
  already accepts `payment_method` and all three labels are within its allowlist), or remove the
  control if the method is genuinely not captured at this step.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-013 — HR module: three flows report "success" while saving nothing
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the UI affirmatively tells the user data was saved when no request is made
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/hr/page.tsx`
- This is worse than a silent failure (R2-006/R2-007): those fail quietly, these **actively assert
  success**. All three show a green confirmation toast and close the dialog.

**1. Employee Details → Save (line 2009) — payroll-relevant, saves nothing**
```js
onClick={() => {
  triggerLocalToast("Details updated successfully");
  setShowDetailsDrawer(false);
}}
```
  - No API call, no state read. The form's fields are **uncontrolled** — `Salary Amount (₹)*`
    (`defaultValue={selectedEmpDetail.grossMonthly}`, line 1938), working hours (`:1960`), OT rate
    (`:1972`) and `Designation` (`:1983`) all use `defaultValue` with **no `onChange`**, so their
    edited values are never captured anywhere.
  - A user changes an employee's monthly salary, clicks Save, is told "Details updated successfully",
    and nothing is persisted or even held in memory.

**2. Add Workforce → Save (line 1852) — saves nothing, not even locally**
```js
onClick={() => {
  if (!workforceForm.workerType) return;
  triggerLocalToast("Workforce added successfully");
  setShowWorkforceDrawer(false);
}}
```
  - Validates one field, then reports success. No API call and no local state update, so the record
    does not appear even in the current session.

**3. Add Holiday → Save Holiday (line 1750) — local-only, lost on refresh**
  - Builds `{ id: "H-" + Date.now(), ... }`, calls `setHolidays([...holidays, newH])` and toasts
    "Holiday added successfully". **No API call.** The holiday shows in the list until the page is
    reloaded, then disappears.
  - Note the backend supports this properly — `hr.py` has holiday endpoints and `log_deletion(...,
    "holiday", ...)` exists — so the wiring is simply absent on the client.

- **Impact:** holidays feed attendance and payroll calculations, and employee salary/designation are
  payroll-critical. A user has no way to know the data was discarded; the interface states the
  opposite. This is the most misleading failure mode found in the audit.
- **Contrast (verified working):** `saveBreakup` in `payroll-attendance/page.tsx:970` does it
  correctly — `await jput('/hr/payroll-profiles/{id}', ...)` then `toast(...)` then `reload()`. That
  is the pattern the three handlers above should follow.
- **Also noted at this location:** the Workforce drawer contains hardcoded cost-code options, e.g.
  `<option value="C-509">C-509 (MEP Rough-Ins)</option>` (line 1845) — fabricated reference data of
  the same class as R2-008/R2-009.
- **Suggested fix:** wire all three to their real endpoints, make the Employee Details inputs
  controlled, and only toast success after a confirmed 2xx response.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-014 — 🔴 CRITICAL: "Sync Offline Queue" DELETES offline attendance punches
### The offline punch feature destroys data and reports success
- **Severity:** **CRITICAL** — irreversible loss of payroll-relevant records, with a false success
  confirmation. This is the most serious defect found in the audit.
- **Where — TWO independent copies of the same defect:**
  - `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/attendance/page.tsx:476-483` (`flushQueue`), button
    "Sync Offline Queue (N)" at line 676
  - `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/attendance/page.tsx:472-479` (`flushQueue`),
    button at line 672 — **identical code, identical bug**
  Both share the same localStorage key `siteflow-punch-queue` and both `persistQueue`
  implementations write the cleared array back to it (`:391` and `:387` respectively), so the queue
  is destroyed from either screen and neither page can recover what the other wiped.
- **The code:**
```js
const flushQueue = () => {
  if (queuedPunches.length === 0) { setSyncMessage("No queued punches to sync"); return; }
  persistQueue([]);                                                    // ← wipes the queue
  setSyncMessage(`Synced ${queuedPunches.length} queued punches successfully`);
};                                                                     // ← no network call at all
```
  and `persistQueue` (line 391) is what makes it irreversible:
```js
const persistQueue = (entries) => {
  setQueuedPunches(entries);
  window.localStorage.setItem(PUNCH_QUEUE_KEY, JSON.stringify(entries));  // "siteflow-punch-queue"
};
```
- **What happens:** `flushQueue` clears both React state **and the localStorage key**, then reports
  `Synced N queued punches successfully`. **It issues no HTTP request whatsoever.** Every queued
  punch is permanently destroyed and the user is told they were synced.
- **How punches reach the queue (both legitimate offline paths):**
  1. `!navigator.onLine` → punch queued, "Punch in queued offline" (line 440-444)
  2. the online POST to `/apis/v3/hr/attendance/punch` throws → "Server connection lost. Saved
     offline." → punch queued (line 469-471)
  The online path itself is correct (proper `res.ok` handling with an error branch). The defect is
  solely in the flush.
- **Real-world impact:** a site supervisor captures attendance on-site without connectivity — the
  advertised PWA capability ("Ready for offline punch capture" appears in Settings; the marketing
  site promotes a GPS-geofenced offline PWA) — returns to signal, taps **Sync Offline Queue (12)**,
  and receives "Synced 12 queued punches successfully". All 12 punches are gone. They were never
  transmitted, and because localStorage is overwritten there is **no recovery path**. Attendance
  drives payroll, so the downstream effect is unpaid or under-recorded worker hours with no audit
  trail of the loss.
- **Why nothing catches it:** no network request is made, so there is no failed call to log, no
  console error, and no server-side trace. The only symptom is attendance silently missing later.
- **Suggested fix:** `flushQueue` must POST each queued punch to `/apis/v3/hr/attendance/punch`,
  remove entries **only** on a confirmed 2xx, retain any that fail, and report actual counts
  ("Synced 10 of 12; 2 failed and remain queued"). Until fixed, consider disabling the button or
  relabelling it, because today it is a delete button labelled "Sync".
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

---

- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/home/page.tsx:545-548` — the `+` button in the

### FINDING R2-016 — Task progress saves without checking the response, then shows it as saved
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — corrupts schedule forecasting, and the page explicitly advertises those
  figures as computed rather than estimated
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/task/page.tsx:109` (`updateProgress`)
- **The code:**
```js
const updateProgress = async (id, value) => {
  setSavingId(id);
  try {
    await fetch(getApi(`/planning/tasks/${id}`), { method: "PUT", ... body: { progress: ... } });
    setTasks((ts) => ts.map((t) => t.id === id ? { ...t, progress: clamp(value,0,100) } : t));
  } finally { setSavingId(null); }
};
```
- **Two problems:** the response is never inspected (no `res.ok`), and the local state is updated
  **optimistically with no refetch**. A 422/500 therefore leaves the new progress rendered on screen
  as though it saved; it silently reverts only when the user next reloads.
- **Why it matters here specifically:** the Tasks & Schedule page states *"Delay and Forecast End are
  computed live from start/end dates and actual progress — no estimates faked."* Those derived
  figures, the Gantt bars and the S-curve are all driven by `progress`. A silently-failed update
  yields confidently wrong schedule forecasting.
- **Triage context (why the other 21 candidates were not filed):** a scan for mutating handlers that
  never inspect the response returned 22 candidates. Most were the declaration-matcher grabbing
  mid-function variables (`res`, `body`, `apiHost`, `formData`). Of the genuinely-named handlers,
  `removeProject` (`projects:155`), `onStatusChange` (`p/[project_id]/layout.tsx:78`) and
  `savePartyMapping` / `saveLedgerMappings` / `saveCostCentreMapping` (`finance:834/848/867`) all
  **refetch from the server** immediately afterwards (`load()` / `fetchTallyData()`), so a failed
  write self-corrects on the next render. They lack an error message but do not display false state,
  so they are noted here rather than filed as findings. `updateProgress` is the one that both skips
  the check *and* renders optimistic state without refetching.
- **Suggested fix:** check `res.ok`, surface a failure, and either refetch or roll the optimistic
  update back.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-016 — LIVE TEST RESULT: latent, not manifest (auditor correction)
Tested end-to-end with seeded data. Created WBS task *"ZZ QA Task - Foundation"* (2026-07-01 → 07-06),
set progress via the Gantt input, then re-read the record from the API:
- Setting progress to **75** through the UI **persisted correctly** (`progressOnServer: 75`), and the
  **Forecast End** column recomputed from "Insufficient data" to **2026-08-03**. Delay showed
  "19d behind", which is correct for an end date of 07-06 against a current date of 07-26.
- **The happy path works.** R2-016 remains a valid code smell — the response is never checked and the
  optimistic update would survive a failure — but it does **not** currently produce wrong data.
  Severity stays MEDIUM as a latent risk, not an active defect.
- **Auditor note:** an earlier attempt appeared to show progress silently failing to save. That was a
  test artifact — the input is uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) with an **`onBlur`** handler, and a
  synthetic `blur` event does not bubble, so React (which delegates `onBlur` via `focusout`) never
  ran the handler. Dispatching `focusout` instead made it work. **The application was never at
  fault**; this is recorded so the finding is not misread as confirmed data loss.

### FINDING R2-031 — Task status never derives from progress, and can't be changed from the Gantt
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — the schedule displays self-contradictory data
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/planning.py:486-505` (`update_task`);
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/task/page.tsx:192-194`
- **Observed live:** after setting *"ZZ QA Task - Foundation"* to **75% progress**, the API and the
  Gantt both still report `status: "not_started"`. The row reads:
  `ZZ QA Task - Foundation | 2026-07-01 → 2026-07-06 | 75 | 19d behind | 2026-08-03 | not_started`
  — a task that is three-quarters complete, 19 days late, with a computed forecast end date, labelled
  **not started**.
- **Cause:** `update_task` applies `status` only when explicitly supplied and `progress` only when
  supplied; **there is no derivation between them**. Meanwhile the Gantt row exposes **only** a
  progress input — there is no status control anywhere in that view (verified: the row contains one
  `<input type=number>` and zero buttons).
- **Impact:** status is effectively write-once at creation. Any status filter, status rollup, or
  "active tasks" count is wrong for every task whose progress has moved. The 14-Day Lookahead and
  Milestones views both key off status.
- **Suggested fix:** derive status server-side on progress change (`0` → not_started, `0<p<100` →
  in_progress, `100` → completed) unless explicitly overridden, or expose a status control in the row.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-017 — 🔴 The main "Dashboard" shows 4 fabricated projects and hides the real one
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the primary sidebar destination displays fictional data instead of the
  user's own
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/dashboard` — the **"Dashboard"** link in the sidebar;
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/dashboard/page.tsx:188` (initial state) and `:124-135` (merge)
- **Observed live in the browser on the founder's company:** the page renders
  **Metro Terminal (Phase 2)**, **Bypass Highway Flyover**, **Alpha Premium Residences** and
  **Prestige Commercial Hub**, together with fabricated attributes including key personnel
  **"Yash Desai"** and customer **"Prestige Group"**. The company's actual project, **"Zoho Test
  Project", does not appear at all** (`/Zoho Test Project/.test(bodyText) === false`).
- **Root cause:**
  1. `const [projects, setProjects] = useState<any[]>([ …4 hardcoded project objects… ])` (line 188)
     — the fabricated set is the **initial state**, so it paints before any request resolves and
     persists if the fetch fails or returns nothing usable.
  2. Lines 124-135 then `merge` fetched projects against a `defaultMatch` table keyed on the demo
     UUIDs `d0000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000000{1,2,3}` — the seed ids created by
     `auto_seed_database()` in `backend/app/main.py`. Real rows whose ids don't match get none of
     those attributes, while the hardcoded entries survive.
- **Contrast:** `/c/{cid}/d/home` (Project Hub) queries the same data and correctly shows only
  "Zoho Test Project". So the app has two dashboard surfaces and the one wired into the sidebar is
  the fabricated one.
- **Impact:** the first screen a user lands on presents four projects that do not exist, attributes
  invented for them, and omits their real work. Any figure derived from that list on this page is
  meaningless. It also re-introduces a real third-party developer brand ("Prestige Group") and an
  invented individual's name, both of which the earlier content-integrity audit set out to remove.
- **Related hardcoded demo data found in the same sweep** (same class as R2-008/R2-009):
  - `reports/dpr/page.tsx:131-133` — project filter offers the three demo project names as options
  - `reports/item-wise-sales/page.tsx:76` — same, "Metro Terminal"
  - `hr/page.tsx:928` — static caption "Radius: 500m • Site: Metro Terminal Phase 2, Mumbai"
- **Suggested fix:** initialise `projects` to `[]`, render a genuine loading/empty state, delete the
  `defaultMatch` merge entirely, and replace the hardcoded filter options with values derived from
  the company's real projects.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-019 — HR Holidays feature is entirely disconnected from the backend
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — holidays drive attendance and payroll; none of this feature reaches the server
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/hr/page.tsx:141` (seed), `:1473` (delete), `:1757` (add)
- **Evidence:** `setHolidays` has **exactly three references in the file** and **none of them is a
  fetch**:
  1. `useState<any[]>([{ id: "H-01", holidayName: "Diwali", date: "2026-07-04", day: "Saturday" }])`
     — a single fabricated holiday, hardcoded as the initial state
  2. `setHolidays(holidays.filter(x => x.id !== h.id))` — Delete removes it locally only
  3. `setHolidays([...holidays, newH])` — Add appends locally only (this is R2-013 #3)
- **Therefore the whole feature is local-only:** the list is never loaded from the server, additions
  are never persisted, and deletions are never persisted. Every page load resets to the same single
  fabricated entry.
- **The seed data is also factually wrong:** it lists **Diwali on 2026-07-04**. Diwali falls in
  October/November; 4 July is not Diwali in any year. (The same `2026-07-04` string appears as the
  dead date default in R2-018, suggesting a copy-paste placeholder.)
- **The backend supports this properly** — `hr.py` exposes holiday endpoints and `log_deletion(...,
  "holiday", ...)` exists — so this is purely missing client wiring.
- **Confirmed live in the browser:** HR → **Holidays** tab renders the "HOLIDAY CALENDAR" with the
  fabricated **Diwali** row present on the founder's real company.
- **Impact — and the page states it itself:** the tab's own description reads *"Create and manage your
  official company holiday calendar. **Employees will be auto-credited present on these dates.**"*
  So the fabricated 4 July "Diwali" entry is not cosmetic — by the product's own description it
  auto-credits attendance, which feeds payroll. A company cannot configure its real calendar at all,
  and cannot remove the fictional entry permanently (deletion is local-only and resets on reload).
- **Suggested fix:** load, create and delete against the existing endpoints; remove the seed.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-020 — DPR measurement book is pre-filled with fabricated quantities
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — one click applies invented measurements into a Daily Progress Report
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/dpr/page.tsx:72` (seed), `:486` (Apply button)
- **Evidence:** the measurement-book modal opens pre-populated with two fabricated rows:
```js
{ description: "Main Floor 2 Slab section A", nos: 1, l: 15.0, w: 8.0, h: 0.15 },
{ description: "Beam drop grid B-C",          nos: 3, l: 6.0,  w: 0.3, h: 0.45 },
```
  and the modal's action button computes `nos × l × w × h` across the rows and writes the total into

```js
const total = mbRows.reduce((acc, r) => acc + (r.nos * r.l * r.w * r.h), 0);
setExecutedQty(total.toFixed(3));
```
- **Consequence:** a user who opens the measurement book and presses **"Apply to Executed Qty"**

  **`Open M.B. Sheet`** displays a computed total of **`20.430 m³`** with the **`Apply to Executed
  Qty`** button active — matching the figure predicted from the seeded rows exactly. This is a
  source-derived finding independently verified against the running application.

### FINDING R2-021 — Project dashboard: "Cash In" isn't cash, and Margin disagrees with the Transaction tab
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — mislabeled financial figures, and two screens report different margins for
  the same project
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/p/{pid}/dashboard`;
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/dashboard/page.tsx:230, 246, 334, 336` and
  `backend/app/routers/projects.py:109` (`_project_cash`)
- **Observed live** on "Zoho Test Project", whose only bills are one sale (₹1,00,000 + GST =
  ₹1,18,000) and two purchases (₹23,600 total) — **all three marked Unpaid, zero payments recorded**:

| Card shown | Value | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| **CASH IN** | **₹1,18,000** | **₹0** — nothing has been paid |
| **CASH OUT** | **₹23,600** | **₹0** — nothing has been paid |
| **NET MARGIN** | **₹94,400** | see basis conflict below |
| NET CASH POSITION | ₹94,400 | correct (0 cash + 1,18,000 receivable − 23,600 payable) |

- **Cause 1 — "cash" is actually accrual.** `_project_cash` (projects.py:109) sums
  `Bill.total_payable` for revenue/expense types and returns it as `cash_in`/`cash_out`. It never
  looks at `paid_amount`. The dashboard binds the header card directly to it
  (`<Card label="Cash In" value={fmtINR(project.cash_in ...)}`, line 334).
- **The correct calculation already exists in the same file and is not used for that card:**
  ```js
  const cashIn = sale.reduce((s, b) => s + (b.paid_amount || 0), 0);   // line 246 — correct, = ₹0
  ```
  It is used for `projectBalance`/`netCash` (which is why Net Cash Position is right) but not for the
  Cash In / Cash Out / Net Margin cards.
- **Cause 2 — two different margins for one project.** `margin0 = project.cash_in - project.cash_out`
  (line 230) is GST-**inclusive** accrual → **₹94,400**. The Transaction tab computes
  `margin = sales - expense` from **subtotals** (GST-**exclusive**) → **₹80,000** (verified earlier
  in this audit). Same project, same data, two figures, and neither screen states its basis.
- **Impact:** a user reading "CASH IN ₹1,18,000" concludes the project has received ₹1.18 lakh when
  it has received nothing — the exact figure someone checks before deciding whether they can pay a
  vendor. The ₹80,000 vs ₹94,400 split then makes it impossible to know which margin is authoritative.
- **Suggested fix:** rename `_project_cash` outputs to `billed_in`/`billed_out` (or compute from
  `paid_amount` if the cards are genuinely meant to be cash), point the Cash In/Out cards at the
  existing line-246 calculation, and standardise margin on one basis — ex-GST is the conventional
  choice — across both screens.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-021 — CONFIRMED BY EXPERIMENT: a real ₹50,000 receipt moves nothing
Rather than argue from source, a payment was recorded and the effect measured.

**Action:** `POST /finance/payments` → **201**, `{payment_type: "in", amount: 50000,
payment_method: "Bank Transfer", reference: "ZZ-QA-PAY-001"}` against the project.

**Result — project dashboard, before vs after:**

| Card | Before | After receiving ₹50,000 |
|---|---|---|
| CASH IN | ₹1,18,000.00 | **₹1,18,000.00 — unchanged** |
| CASH OUT | ₹23,600.00 | ₹23,600.00 — unchanged |
| NET CASH POSITION | ₹94,400.00 | **₹94,400.00 — unchanged** |

**The payment was definitely stored.** `GET /finance/transactions/{cid}` returns
`in_total: 50000`, 4 transactions, and the reference `ZZ-QA-PAY-001` is present.

**So the two modules disagree about the same company's cash:**

| Screen | "Cash in" | Actually derived from |
|---|---|---|
| Finance → Transactions | **₹50,000** | real `Payment` records ✓ |
| Project dashboard | **₹1,18,000** | `SUM(Bill.total_payable)` for sale types ✗ |

A ₹68,000 discrepancy between two screens that both present the figure as cash. This upgrades the
finding from "mislabelled" to "**contradicts the product's own cash ledger**": `_project_cash`
ignores the `Payment` table entirely, so no amount of money actually received will ever move the
project dashboard's cash cards.

**Additional observation (not separately filed):** the same transactions response reports
`cash_balance: 0` and `company_balance: 0` despite `in_total: 50000`. That may be correct if those
figures require a configured bank/cash account, so it is noted rather than asserted as a defect.

**Second experiment — R2-021 is independent of R2-042.** A further ₹40,000 payment was recorded
*with* `party_company_user_id`, which correctly settled the invoice
(`ZZ-QA-AUDIT-001 → paid 40,000, status "Partially Paid"` — verified). The dashboard afterwards:
**CASH IN still ₹1,18,000.00, unchanged.** So even once payments settle properly, the cash cards
remain pure accrual sums. Fixing R2-042 will not fix R2-021; both changes are required.

**Correctly behaving, for the record:** `NET CASH POSITION` stayed at ₹94,400 across both payments,
which is **arithmetically right** — it is `paid + receivable − payable`, and moving money from
"receivable" to "paid" leaves the net position unchanged. That card is sound; only CASH IN / CASH OUT
are mislabelled.

### FINDING R2-022 — Company-wide Finance data only loads if a project happens to be active
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — a company with no active project sees an entirely empty Finance module
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/finance/page.tsx:373-377`
```js
useEffect(() => {
  if (projectId) {        // projectId = activeProjectId, from ProjectContext
    fetchData();
  }
}, [projectId, companyId]);
```
- **The problem:** `fetchData()` loads **company-scoped** data — `finance/transactions/{companyId}`,
  `finance/parties/{companyId}`, `finance/payment-requests/{companyId}`, `finance/accounts/{companyId}`
  — but the effect that calls it is gated on a **project** being active. Only the first request inside
  it (`finance/pl?project_id=…`) is genuinely project-scoped and is separately guarded at line 297.
- **Consequence:** for a company with no projects, or a session where `activeProjectId` has not
  resolved (fresh login, `last_project_id` unset, project deleted), the Finance module renders
  Total Invoice ₹0 / Total Expense ₹0 / Company Balance ₹0, empty Parties, empty Payment Requests and
  "No Data Transaction" — with **no error and no loading state** — while the API would return real
  figures. Verified the API is healthy: `GET /apis/v3/finance/transactions/{cid}` → `200` with
  `{"total_invoice":118000.0,"total_expense":23600.0,...}`.
- **Auditor note — what this finding is NOT:** during testing the page initially displayed ₹0 and
  appeared broken. Re-checking after the context resolved showed the correct ₹1,18,000. **That first
  reading was a probe-timing artifact, not the defect,** and is recorded here so the finding is not
  misread as "Finance always shows zero". The defect is narrower: company data should not depend on
  a project being selected.
- **Suggested fix:** split the effect — call the company-scoped fetches on `companyId` alone, and
  keep only the P&L call gated on `projectId`.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-024 — 🔴 Production UI has a "Create Demo Request" button that calls the OTP auth endpoint with hardcoded demo credentials
- **Severity:** **HIGH** (security-adjacent + demo data in a financial module)
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/d/payment-approval` — button rendered at
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/payment-approval/page.tsx:187`, handler
  `handleCreateDemoRequest` at `:121`
- **Observed live:** the Payment Approvals screen — the module used to *authorize company payments* —
  renders a **"+ Create Demo Request"** button in production.
- **What the handler does:**
```js
const userRes = await fetch(`${apiHost}/apis/v3/auth/otp/verify`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ mobile: "+919876543210", code: "123456" }) // mock verify to get user
});
let userId = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000";
if (userRes.ok) { userId = (await userRes.json()).user.id; }
// then POSTs a payment request with party_company_user_id: userId
```
- **Why this matters:**
  1. A **production page invokes the authentication endpoint with hardcoded credentials** — the demo
     phone `+919876543210` and demo code `123456`. These are precisely the values configured as
     `OTP_DEMO_ALLOWLIST` and `OTP_DEMO_CODE` in `backend/app/config.py`, i.e. the dev/demo login
     bypass. The call carries no `Authorization` header — it is an unauthenticated auth attempt made
     by the app itself.
  2. If the demo allowlist is still populated in the production environment, this button confirms the
     bypass is reachable from the live frontend. **If it is not populated, the call fails and
     `userId` silently falls back to the all-zeros UUID**, creating a payment request attributed to a
     non-existent user.
  3. Either way it **writes a real payment request into the approvals queue** of a financial module.
- **Founder context (2026-07-26):** the demo number and code were deliberately created by the team to
  test the OTP flow. They are **known test credentials, not an unrecognised backdoor.** That removes
  the "unknown bypass" concern but not the exposure: because this handler lives in a client page,
  **`+919876543210` and `123456` are compiled into the production JavaScript bundle** and readable by
  anyone who opens devtools on the live site. If the allowlist is still populated on Render, any
  visitor can authenticate as that demo user.
- **Auditor note:** this was **not executed**. Invoking an authentication endpoint to obtain another
  identity is outside what the auditor will do on the founder's behalf.
- **SEVERITY REVISED DOWN after the Phase 1 code review.** The demo code is gated more tightly than
  first assumed (`auth.py:350-360`):
```python
provider_ready = sms.is_configured()          # True when SMS_PROVIDER_API_KEY is set
is_demo        = _is_demo_mobile(mobile)      # mobile in OTP_DEMO_ALLOWLIST
if not provider_ready and not is_demo: → 503
use_demo_code  = is_demo and not provider_ready
code = settings.OTP_DEMO_CODE if use_demo_code else _generate_otp_code()
```
  **The fixed code `123456` is only accepted when NO SMS provider is configured.** If `MSG91` /
  `SMS_PROVIDER_API_KEY` is set on Render, `provider_ready` is True, a real random OTP is generated
  and sent by SMS, and the hardcoded code will not authenticate anything.
  Additionally, `_is_demo_mobile()` routes the demo number into `_ensure_demo_company()` — a
  **separate shared demo tenant**, so it cannot reach a real company's data even when it does work.
- **So the actual question is narrow:** is `SMS_PROVIDER_API_KEY` set in production?
  - **If set** → the button is merely broken/pointless (the OTP call fails, `userId` falls back to
    the all-zeros UUID, and a payment request is created against a non-existent user). Low severity.
  - **If unset** → the demo login path is live, and `+919876543210` / `123456` are readable in the
    production JS bundle. That would be a real (if demo-tenant-scoped) exposure.
- **Action:** delete the button regardless — it writes junk into a financial approvals queue — and
  confirm `SMS_PROVIDER_API_KEY` is populated on Render.
- **Suggested fix:** delete the button and `handleCreateDemoRequest` outright. Separately, confirm the
  demo OTP allowlist is empty in production regardless of this button's fate.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-025 — 🔴 Enterprise Rollup "Net Balance" formula subtracts receivables (sign error)
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — a positive financial position is displayed as a large negative one
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/finance.py:895-897` (`/finance/enterprise-rollup/{company_id}`),
  rendered at `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/enterprise/page.tsx:111`
- **Observed live** on the founder's company:

| Card | Displayed |
|---|---|
| TO PAY | ₹23,600.00 |
| TO RECEIVE | ₹1,18,000.00 |
| **NET BALANCE** | **−₹1,41,600.00** |

  The correct net position is `1,18,000 − 23,600 = **+₹94,400**`. The screen is wrong by **₹2,36,000**
  and, more damagingly, **inverts the sign** — a company that is net owed money is presented as
  deeply in deficit.
- **The formula:**
```python
total_balance = round(
    totals["advance_paid"] + totals["advance_received"] - totals["to_pay"] - totals["to_receive"], 2
)
```
  With advances at zero this evaluates to `0 + 0 − 23,600 − 118,000 = −141,600`, exactly matching the
  screen — so this is confirmed as the source, not an inference.
- **The defect:** `to_receive` is money owed **to** the company (an asset) and must be **added**, not
  subtracted. The correct expression is `to_receive − to_pay` (plus whatever advance adjustment is
  intended).
- **Likely a second sign error in the same line:** `advance_paid` (cash the company has paid out —
  a receivable/asset) and `advance_received` (cash held on someone else's behalf — a liability) are
  **both added** with the same sign. They should oppose each other. This could not be verified live
  because both advances are ₹0 on this dataset, so it is flagged for review rather than asserted.
- **Impact:** the Enterprise Rollup is the consolidated multi-company financial view. Its headline
  number is not merely inaccurate but sign-inverted, and the error grows with transaction volume.
- **Suggested fix:** rewrite as `to_receive - to_pay` with explicitly-signed advance terms, and add a
  unit test asserting a known-good case (e.g. to_receive 118000, to_pay 23600 → +94400).
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-025 — SECOND MEASUREMENT ISOLATES THE FAULT TO THE FINAL LINE
Re-tested after ₹40,000 was settled against the ₹1,18,000 sales invoice:

| Card | Value | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| TO PAY | ₹23,600.00 | ✅ correct (both purchases still unpaid) |
| TO RECEIVE | ₹78,000.00 | ✅ **correct — fell by exactly the ₹40,000 settled** |
| **NET BALANCE** | **−₹1,01,600.00** | ❌ = −(78,000 + 23,600). Correct answer: **+₹54,400** |

**This is diagnostically useful:** the underlying party-balance engine is **sound** — `to_pay` and
`to_receive` both responded correctly to a real settlement, proving bills, payments and the FIFO
matching all feed it properly. The defect is isolated to the single aggregation line
(`finance.py:895-897`), which subtracts receivables instead of adding them. **It is a one-line fix,
not a rework of the balance logic.**

### FINDING R2-027 — 🔴 Face Recognition log endpoint 500s on every call; UI disguises it as "no data"
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the module is completely non-functional and the failure is invisible
- **Discovered by:** a **Sentry production alert** fired by the auditor merely opening the page.
  Event `8fae4420dca9418a8ea8112acecdc59f`, 2026-07-25 20:17:24 UTC, project `python-fastapi`,
  environment **production**:
  `AttributeError: type object 'FaceRecognitionLog' has no attribute 'created_at'`
  at `/app/app/routers/face_recognition.py`, line 82, in `list_logs`.

**Bug 1 — backend: the column does not exist.**
`backend/app/routers/face_recognition.py:82`
```python
return query.order_by(FaceRecognitionLog.created_at.desc()).limit(200).all()
```
The `FaceRecognitionLog` model (`backend/app/models.py:1736-1747`) declares `id, company_id,
project_id, employee_id, punch_type, face_verified, confidence_score, image_url, lat, lng,
is_within_geofence` — and then the class ends. **There is no `created_at`, and no timestamp column of
any kind.** So `GET /apis/v3/face/logs/{company_id}` raises `AttributeError` → HTTP 500 on *every*
request, for every company. This is not data-dependent.

**Design gap behind it:** an attendance *audit log* with no time column at all. The UI even renders a
**"Time"** header (`Time | Employee | Type | Verified | Confidence | Location`) for a field the model
cannot supply. Fixing the ordering alone is insufficient — the model needs a timestamp.

**Bug 2 — frontend: the 500 is swallowed and rendered as an empty state.**
`frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/face-recognition/page.tsx:49-53`
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: authHeaders() });
if (res.ok) setLogs(await res.json());     // 500 → condition false → nothing happens
} catch (e) { console.error("Failed to load face logs", e); }
```
There is no `else`. A 500 leaves `logs` empty, so the page displays **"No face recognition logs
found"** — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty log. Same anti-pattern as R2-006 / R2-007.

- **Impact:** face-recognition attendance auditing has never worked in production, and the interface
  reports the reassuring message that there is simply nothing to show.
- **Suggested fix:** add a timestamp column to `FaceRecognitionLog` (with a migration), order by it,
  and give the frontend an error branch that distinguishes "request failed" from "no records".

## ⚠️ METHOD NOTE — THIS FINDING EXPOSES A LIMIT OF THE BROWSER SWEEP
`/d/face-recognition` was visited during the sweep and **recorded as clean**. The probe returned
`err: false` and the page body read "No face recognition logs found" — a normal, healthy-looking
empty state. **The backend was returning 500 the entire time.**

It was caught only because Sentry emailed the founder about the exception the auditor's own page load
triggered.

**Implication for the rest of this report:** any route whose data-loading follows the
`if (res.ok) { ... }`-with-no-else pattern will look identical to an empty module in a page-load
screen. The clean bill of health given to low-data modules in this audit is therefore weaker evidence
than it appears. **The reliable way to close this class is to check Sentry for the production error
list, or add error branches, rather than to browse more pages.**

## RE-VERIFICATION — the 5 Sentry errors in `To Fix/Sentry` (fixed by a prior agent, commit `b1a9497`)

Independently re-checked against current code. **All five are genuinely fixed.** This was a real fix,
not a claimed one.

| # | Sentry error | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AttributeError: 'Project' object has no attribute 'start_date'` | ✅ **FIXED** | `Project` legitimately has no `start_date` (it uses `planned_start_date`/`actual_start_date`). No code references `project.start_date` / `p.start_date` / `p.customer_name` any longer. Remaining `.start_date` hits belong to `EquipmentDeployment` (`dep.start_date`) and to request payloads (`planning.py:445` uses `request.start_date`), both correct. |
| 2 | `HTTPException: Failed to create the Zoho Books bill … 13009 The account field cannot be empty` | ✅ **FIXED** | New helper `_default_expense_account_id()` (`zoho_books.py:207`) resolves an active expense account from the org's chart of accounts; **called at line 616** and applied to every line item, with an explicit 502 if no account exists. Helper is wired in, not just defined. |
| 3 | `HTTPException: Failed to update the Zoho Books vendor GST info … 8 Invalid Element gst_treatment` | ✅ **FIXED** | `gst_treatment` is now only included when applicable (`:287`), and there is an explicit retry-once-without-it path when Zoho rejects element code 8 (`:298-300`). Defensive and correct. |
| 4 | `NameError: name 'models' is not defined` | ❌ **NOT FIXED — STILL FIRING IN PRODUCTION** | See R2-028. Last seen **3 days ago** (i.e. *after* the `b1a9497` fix), 2 events, at `/apis/v3/billing/subcontractors`. **My first verification of this row was WRONG — see the correction note below.** |
| 5 | `RuntimeError: Directory 'static' does not exist` | ✅ **FIXED** | `os.makedirs("static/reports", exist_ok=True)` runs at `main.py:516`, **before** `app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(...))` at `:517`, and again inside the lifespan at `:481`. |

### 🔴 AUDITOR CORRECTION — row 4 was verified incorrectly the first time
My initial check for the `NameError` used this test:
```bash
grep -q "models\." "$f" && ! grep -qE "^from app\.models import|from app import models|import app\.models" "$f"
```
`billing.py` line 9 reads `from app.models import (Bill, Project, ...)`, which **matched the pattern**,
so the file was cleared. But `from app.models import X` imports *names* — **it does not bind the name
`models`**. The test was checking for the wrong thing and produced a false "fixed".

The live Sentry feed contradicted the verdict (error still firing 3 days ago, *after* the fix commit),
which prompted a correct re-scan:
```python
binds = r'^\s*(from\s+app\s+import\s+[^\n]*\bmodels\b|import\s+app\.models\s+as\s+models|from\s+app\s+import\s+models)'
```
That returns exactly one offending file — `routers/billing.py` — with 4 unbound uses. See R2-028.

**Lesson for this report:** a source scan that "finds nothing" is only as good as its pattern. Where
production telemetry exists, it outranks a grep.

### FINDING R2-029 — Zoho vendor duplicate (3062) remediation re-runs the query that already failed
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — latent; not currently firing, but the guard cannot resolve the case it was
  written for. Blocks Zoho bill push for affected vendors.
- **Sentry:** `PYTHON-FASTAPI-6`, 3 events, first/last seen ~Jul 14-15 2026, endpoint
  `/apis/v3/integrations/zoho-books/companies/{company_id}/push-bill/{bill_id}`
  `HTTPException: Failed to create the Zoho Books vendor contact: {"code":3062,"message":"A vendor
  with the name \"upadhyayprateek574\", already exists…"}`
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/zoho_books.py` — `_search_vendor` (`:232`), `_find_or_create_vendor`
  (`:265-317`)

**What the captured Sentry locals prove:**
```
contact_payload : {contact_name: "upadhyayprateek574", contact_type: "vendor", email: "…@gmail.com"}
contacts        : []            ← the lookup returned NOTHING
→ Zoho replies 3062 "a vendor with that name already exists"
```
Breadcrumbs show **two** GET calls to `zohoapis.in/books/v3/contacts` before the failing POST — i.e.
both the by-email and the by-name searches ran, and **both returned `[]`** — while Zoho simultaneously
insists the name is taken.

**Why the existing guard is ineffective.** Commit `d6de15c` added:
```python
if resp.status_code not in (200, 201):
    dup = _search_vendor(access_token, organization_id, name=name)   # ← identical to the search
    if dup: return dup                                               #   that already returned []
    raise HTTPException(502, …)
```
The fallback re-issues **the same by-name query that had just returned `[]`** moments earlier in the
same function. Given direct evidence that this query does not find the contact Zoho considers a
duplicate, the fallback will also return `None` and the 502 is raised anyway. The fix would only help
if the duplicate were findable by name — which the telemetry shows it is not.

**Most likely root cause:** `_search_vendor` always filters `contact_type: "vendor"`, but Zoho Books
enforces contact-name uniqueness **across all contact types**. If "upadhyayprateek574" already exists
as a **customer** (plausible — it is the founder's own name/email, likely created as a customer during
earlier testing), the vendor-filtered search can never see it, while creation is always rejected.

**Timeline note (why this is latent, not active):** the last event was Jul 14 09:20:54 UTC; `d6de15c`
landed 14:52 IST the same day — ~88 seconds later. It has not recurred, but there is no evidence the
guard works, only that the code path has not been exercised since.

**Suggested fix:** on a non-2xx create, re-search **without** the `contact_type` filter (or use Zoho's
`search_text` / `contact_name_contains`), and if a contact is found with the wrong type, either reuse
its `contact_id` or convert it. Also log the Zoho error code so a genuine 3062 is distinguishable from
other failures.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-032 — "Total Monthly CTC" double-counts employee PF and hardcodes 24%
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — systematically overstates payroll cost; the figure a company budgets from
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/hr/page.tsx:808`
```js
{ label: "Total Monthly CTC",
  val: fmt(employees.reduce((a, e) => a + e.grossMonthly + e.basic * 0.24, 0)) }
```
- **Found by seeding data.** With two seeded employees (basic ₹18,000, HRA ₹3,600, other ₹1,800 →
  gross **₹23,400** each, confirmed in the table), the header reads **TOTAL MONTHLY CTC ₹55,440**.
  - Screen: `2 × (23,400 + 18,000 × 0.24)` = `2 × 27,720` = **₹55,440** ✓ matches the formula exactly
  - Correct: CTC = gross **+ employer** contribution only = `23,400 + 18,000 × 0.12` = ₹25,560 each
    → **₹51,120**
  - **Overstated by ₹2,160 per employee per month** (12% of basic).
- **Defect 1 — employee PF is not a company cost.** The `0.24` is PF employee 12% + PF employer 12%.
  The employee's 12% is *deducted from* their gross pay; it is already inside `grossMonthly`. Adding
  it again counts the same rupees twice. Only the employer's 12% belongs in CTC.
- **Defect 2 — the rate is hardcoded.** `StaffEmployee` carries per-employee `pf_employee_pct` and
  `pf_employer_pct` (defaults 12/12, but settable — the create form exposes them). The dashboard
  ignores both and applies a flat 24% to every employee, so anyone with PF disabled or on a different
  rate is still charged 24% of basic.
- **Defect 3 (flagged, not verified) — no PF wage ceiling.** Indian statutory PF is normally computed
  on basic capped at ₹15,000/month. The formula applies 24% to uncapped basic, so high earners are
  overstated further. Not confirmed against the company's PF settings, so listed for review.
- **Impact:** scales linearly with headcount — at 100 employees on this salary the figure is
  overstated by ~₹2.16 lakh/month (~₹26 lakh/year). This is the number shown on the HR landing screen
  and the natural input to hiring and budget decisions.
- **Suggested fix:** `gross + basic * (e.pf_employer_pct/100)`, using the per-employee rate, with the
  statutory ceiling applied if the company's settings call for it.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

---

### FINDING R2-033 — Payroll pays a full pro-rated month when there is NO attendance data, shown as if measured
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — real money computed from an assumption, presented to the payroll approver
  as recorded attendance
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/hr.py:647-677` (`compute_payroll`)
```python
days_present = float(att_count + approved_leave_days) if (att_count + approved_leave_days) > 0 else default_days
#                                                                                                  ↑ full month,
#   or, for a mid-month joiner: (month_end - joining_date).days
```
- **Reproduced live end-to-end.** Seeded employee *"ZZ QA Employee One"* (basic ₹18,000, HRA ₹3,600,
  other ₹1,800 → gross ₹23,400; date of joining 2026-07-25). **No attendance record was ever created
  and no leave was requested.** Ran HR → Payroll Runs → Compute Payroll for 2026-07, 26 working days:

| Figure | Value | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| Days | **7 / 26** | = days from 25 Jul to month end — a *fallback*, not attendance |
| Gross | ₹6,300.00 | 23,400 × 7/26 ✓ arithmetically correct |
| PF (emp) | ₹581.54 | 18,000 × 7/26 × 12% ✓ correct |
| Net pay | ₹11,436.92 (2 emps) | 12,600 − 1,163.08 ✓ correct |

  **Every calculation is right. The input is invented.**
- **The defect is not the arithmetic — it is that the payslip cannot be distinguished from a real
  one.** The UI renders "7/26" in a **DAYS** column beside GROSS / PF / NET, with the run marked
  **finalized**. Nothing on screen indicates that attendance was absent and a default was substituted.
  A payroll approver has no way to tell "7 days attended" from "no attendance data, assumed 7 days".
- **Why this matters for this product specifically:** GPS-geofenced attendance is a headline feature
  (`Geofence: Active`, face-recognition audit trail, offline punch capture). A company adopting it to
  stop paying for unworked days will, if punches are missing for any reason — device offline, module
  not rolled out, or **R2-014 silently deleting the offline queue** — pay those days in full anyway.
  R2-014 and this finding compound: punches get destroyed, then payroll quietly assumes full attendance.
- **This may be an intentional fallback** for companies not using the attendance module. If so it is
  a defensible policy but an undisclosed one, and the display makes it indistinguishable from
  measured data.
- **Suggested fix:** keep the fallback if desired, but flag it — return a per-line
  `attendance_source: "recorded" | "assumed"` and render assumed rows distinctly (badge/warning), and
  surface a run-level warning such as "N employees had no attendance; full days assumed". Consider a
  company setting to make zero attendance mean zero pay.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-034 — RA Bills cannot be submitted: subcontractor dropdown never populates; WOs show "Unassigned"
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the subcontractor billing chain is unusable end-to-end
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/billing/page.tsx` — subcontractor loader at `:221`,
  dropdown at `:848-851`, work-order name map built at `:225` and consumed by `fetchWorkOrders(nameMap)`
- **Reproduced live after seeding real data:**
  1. Created subcontractor **"ZZ QA Subcon Co"** (`POST /billing/subcontractors` → 201) and work order
     **ZZ-QA-WO-001** for ₹150,000 (`POST /billing/work-orders` → 201).
  2. `GET /billing/subcontractors?company_id={cid}` → **200, count 1, `["ZZ QA Subcon Co"]`**
     (verified twice, directly against production).
  3. `GET /billing/work-orders?project_id={pid}` → **200**, and the row carries
     **`subcontractor_name: "ZZ QA Subcon Co"`**.
  4. **In the UI, after a full page reload:** the **Submit RA Bill** modal's SUBCONTRACTOR select
     contains only `"Select subcontractor"` — the seeded subcontractor is absent. The field is
     required, so **no RA bill can be submitted at all**.
  5. The **Work Orders** tab *does* list `ZZ-QA-WO-001 | ₹150,000 | ACTIVE` correctly, but its
     **Subcontractor column reads "Unassigned"** — despite the API supplying the name in the very
     same response.
- **Mechanism (partly confirmed):** the page does not use the `subcontractor_name` the work-orders
  endpoint already returns. It instead builds its own `nameMap` from a *separate* subcontractors
  fetch (`:221-226`) and passes it into `fetchWorkOrders(nameMap)`. That fetch is wrapped in
  `if (res.ok)` with no `else`, so any failure leaves both `subcontractors` (the dropdown source) and
  `nameMap` (the WO name source) empty — producing exactly the two symptoms observed together.
  Confirmed that calling these endpoints with undefined params returns **422**, which that guard
  would swallow silently.
- **What is NOT proven:** the precise reason the page's own fetch yields nothing while an identical
  direct request succeeds. `companyId` comes from `useParams()` and should be valid on this route.
  The loader effect is keyed on `[projectId]` (which is `activeProjectId` from context, resolving
  asynchronously), so a first run with an unresolved value that never re-runs is the leading
  hypothesis — **stated as a hypothesis, not a conclusion.**
- **Impact:** subcontractor RA billing — retention, TDS, pre/post-tax deduction ordering, the whole
  module — cannot be exercised by a user. Work orders also misattribute to "Unassigned".
- **Suggested fix:** use the `subcontractor_name` already present in the work-orders response instead
  of a client-side name map; add an `else` branch that surfaces the failure; and key the loader on
  `[companyId, projectId]` so it re-runs once the project context resolves.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.
