### FINDING R2-035 — 🔴 Project progress ignores task progress entirely; buckets by status instead
### Compounds with R2-031: a project can be 100% built and still report 0%
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the headline completion figure for every project can be permanently 0%
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/projects.py:71-106`
```python
_TASK_PROGRESS = {"not_started": 0.0, "start": 0.1, "ongoing": 0.5, "completed": 1.0}
...
earned = sum((t.duration_days or 0) * _TASK_PROGRESS.get(t.status, 0.0) for t in tasks)
return round(earned / total_dur * 100, 1)
```
- **The `Task.progress` column is never read.** Confirmed: `.progress` does not appear anywhere in
  `projects.py`. Project completion is derived **solely from `t.status`**, quantised to four values
  (0%, 10%, 50%, 100%).
- **Reproduced live:** project *"Zoho Test Project"* has exactly one task, *"ZZ QA Task - Foundation"*,
  set to **progress = 75** (verified on the server). The project dashboard reports **PROGRESS 0%**,
  because that task's `status` is still `not_started` and `_TASK_PROGRESS["not_started"] = 0.0`.
- **The compounding failure with R2-031:** the Gantt exposes **only** a progress input and no status
  control, and `update_task` never derives status from progress. So the only completion signal a user
  can actually enter is the one the rollup ignores. **A user can set every task in a project to 100%
  progress and the project will still report 0% complete, forever.**
- **Two further consequences:**
  1. Even when status *is* set, progress is quantised — a task 90% done that is still `ongoing`
     contributes 50%, and one barely begun contributes the same 50%.
  2. The value feeds the project dashboard PROGRESS card, the `/projects` list Progress column, and
     the home Project Portfolio — so all three understate delivery.
- **Suggested fix:** use `t.progress` for the earned-value calculation
  (`earned = Σ duration_days × (progress/100)`), falling back to the status map only when `progress`
  is null. Fixing R2-031 alone is not sufficient — this function must read the progress field.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-036 — 🔴 Analytics "Spend" counts sales invoices as expenditure
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — budget variance and burn rate are inflated by revenue
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/analytics.py:223`
```python
project_spend = sum(_to_float(bill.total_payable) for bill in bills_by_project.get(project.id, []))
```
  **Every bill is summed regardless of `invoice_type`** — sales invoices included.
- **Reproduced live:** the project holds one **sale** of ₹1,18,000 and two **purchases** totalling
  ₹23,600. The Analytics dashboard reports **BUDGET VARIANCE Rs -1,41,600**, subtitled
  **"Spend 1,41,600 vs budget 0"**. That is `118,000 + 23,600` — the company's own **revenue counted
  as money spent**. Correct spend is ₹23,600.
- **This is the same defect family as R2-025** (Enterprise Rollup subtracting receivables) and
  R2-021 (accrual labelled as cash): financial aggregates that ignore the revenue/expense
  distinction. Note the identical figure ₹1,41,600 appears in both R2-025 and here from two
  independent code paths.
- **Downstream:** `burn_rate_pct` (`:258`) and `budget_variance` (`:259`) are both derived from
  `total_spend`, so both are wrong by the value of all sales invoices.
- **The fix already exists in the codebase:** `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES` in `backend/app/constants.py`
  was introduced during the invoice_type remediation for exactly this purpose. This call site was
  missed — filter with `bill.invoice_type in EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES`.

#### R2-036 (cont.) — SYSTEMIC: five call sites sum bills as cost with no `invoice_type` filter
A scripted sweep for bill aggregations (`sum(... total_payable ...)`) lacking an `invoice_type`
filter returned 8 candidates; after inspecting each, **5 are confirmed instances of this defect**:

| File / line | Expression | What it feeds |
|---|---|---|
| `analytics.py:223` | `project_spend = sum(bill.total_payable …)` | Budget Variance, Burn Rate (**verified live: ₹1,41,600**) |
| `analytics.py:439` | `spend = sum(b.total_payable for b in Bill.filter(project_id))` | project Health determination |
| `budget.py:146` | `actual = sum(b.total_payable …)` after `Bill.filter(project_id)` | budget "actual" figure |
| `budget.py:160` | same | budget "actual" figure |
| `towers.py:178` | `total_billed = sum(b.total_payable …)` | **Consolidated P&L by Tower** → Billed column |
| `towers.py:200` | same | tower P&L |

In every case the query is `db.query(Bill).filter(Bill.project_id == …)` with **no type restriction**,
so sales invoices, purchases, subcon bills and expenses are added together and presented as cost
(or, in `towers.py`, as "billed" value).

**Ruled out (checked, not defects):** `subcon_performance.py:255` — the enclosing query does filter
`Bill.invoice_type == "subcon"` a few lines above, outside the scan window. `finance.py:1156` —
aggregates `Payment.paid_amount`, not bills.

**Note on scope:** the project Budget page's headline **TOTAL ACTUAL ₹23,600 was observed correct**
(purchases only), because that card is served by the separately-filtered queries at `budget.py:83/92`.
The unfiltered sums at `:146/:160` therefore feed a different surface (cost-code / variance views)
that was not exercised with data during this audit — flagged from source, **not** confirmed on screen.

- **Suggested fix:** apply `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES` (or the appropriate bucket) at all five sites, and
  add a regression test asserting a project with one sale and one purchase reports spend equal to the
  purchase only.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-037 — "Material Wastage" reports 100% for material that simply hasn't been issued yet
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — an alarming KPI that is wrong by construction
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/analytics.py:330-333`
```python
ordered_qty  = sum(_to_float(item.quantity) for item in purchase_order_items)
consumed_qty = sum(_to_float(tx.qty) for tx in material_transactions)
wastage_qty  = max(ordered_qty - consumed_qty, 0.0)
wastage_pct  = round((wastage_qty / ordered_qty) * 100, 2) if ordered_qty else 0.0
```
- **Reproduced live:** one PO exists (100 bags of cement) and **no material has been issued**. The
  Analytics dashboard reports **MATERIAL WASTAGE 100%**, captioned "Ordered vs consumed from
  procurement".
- **The defect:** material ordered but not yet consumed is **stock in hand**, not waste. The formula
  treats every un-issued unit as wasted, so a company shows 100% wastage immediately after raising a
  PO — the normal state before goods are received and issued. The figure only becomes meaningful once
  consumption catches up, and can never distinguish "not used yet" from "actually wasted".
- **Note:** a dedicated Wastage module already exists (`/d/wastage`, "Track scrap, offcuts, damage and
  theft on site") with its own records. This KPI ignores that data entirely and infers waste by
  subtraction instead.
- **Suggested fix:** compute wastage from the wastage records, or at minimum compare consumed against
  *received* (GRN) quantities rather than ordered, and suppress the metric when consumption data is
  absent.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

- **Severity:** LOW (consistency)
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/analytics` — BUDGET VARIANCE card renders **`Rs -1,41,600`**
- Every other financial surface audited (project dashboard, transactions, budget, enterprise rollup,
  payroll, HR) renders `₹`. This card also omits the decimal places used elsewhere and does not appear

### FINDING R2-039 — 🔴 Reports ship 91 hardcoded-empty columns across 21 builders (incl. Balance Due)
- **Severity:** **HIGH** (functional incompleteness) — reports promise columns they never populate,
  including receivables figures
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/reports.py` — 91 occurrences of `"Column Name": ""` spread across
  **21** `_rep_*` builder functions
- **Reproduced live** on `/c/{cid}/reports/company-sales` with a real ₹1,18,000 sales invoice:

| Column | Rendered | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice Date | `2026-07-25T00:00:00+00:00` | a formatted date |
| Total Amount | `118000` | ₹1,18,000.00 |
| Retention Amount | *(blank)* | 0 |
| Post Tax Deduction | *(blank)* | 0 |
| **Net Amount** | *(blank)* | 1,18,000 |
| **Payment Received** | *(blank)* | 0 |
| **Balance Due** | *(blank)* | 1,18,000 |
| Notes / Creator / Settlement Amounts / Payment Dates / Reference Numbers | *(blank)* | — |

  **11 of 19 columns in this one report are literal `""` in the source.**
- **The data exists.** `Bill.paid_amount` gives Payment Received; `total_payable - paid_amount` gives
  Balance Due; `TransactionDeduction` rows carry retention and post-tax deductions. Nothing is being
  computed and discarded — the fields were simply never wired.
- **Worst-affected builders:** `_rep_company_sales` (11), `_rep_material_received_used` (11),
  `_rep_po_item` (8), `_rep_task_attendance` (7), `_rep_task_measurement_book` (6),
  `_rep_gstr2_purchase` (6), `_rep_dpr` (5), `_rep_po_summary` (5), `_rep_item_wise_sales` (5).
- **Why this matters beyond cosmetics:** `Balance Due` on a company sales report is the receivables
  number — the reason the report is run. `_rep_gstr2_purchase` is a **statutory GST filing** report
  with 6 empty columns. These are exported to Excel/PDF and handed to accountants.
- **Two formatting defects in the same path:** dates emit raw ISO-8601 timestamps
  (`2026-07-25T00:00:00+00:00`) rather than formatted dates, and amounts emit bare integers
  (`118000`) with no currency symbol or separators — unlike every other screen in the product, which
  uses `fmtINR` and respects `currency_decimal_places`.
- **Suggested fix:** populate the columns from data already loaded in each builder, and route dates
  and amounts through shared formatters. Where a column genuinely has no source, remove it from the
  header rather than emitting an empty cell.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-040 — "Export as Excel" writes a CSV file with a `.xlsx` extension
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — the file is not an Excel workbook and Excel warns the user on open
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/reports/[slug]/page.tsx:735-746` (`handleExportSelect`)
```js
const csvContent = [headers.join(","), ...dataRows.map(...)].join("\n");
const blob = new Blob([csvContent], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8;" });
...
const extension = format === "xlsx" ? "xlsx" : "csv";
link.setAttribute("download", meta.title... + `_export.${extension}`);
```
- **The defect:** the **CSV and Excel menu items run identical code**. Both produce comma-separated
  text with MIME type `text/csv`; only the filename extension differs. Choosing **Export as Excel**
  therefore downloads a CSV named `..._export.xlsx`. Excel opens it with a *"The file format and
  extension don't match"* security warning, and it is not a real workbook — no sheets, no typing, no
  formatting. Anything consuming it as `.xlsx` programmatically (openpyxl, pandas `read_excel`) will
  fail outright.
- **Related, same handler:** **Export as PDF** does not produce a PDF. It opens a print window with
  generated HTML and toasts *"Exported PDF print preview generated!"* (`:730`). That is a browser
  print dialog, not a file export — defensible behaviour, but the label and toast overstate it.
- **Context:** this is the export path for the entire ~40-report catalogue, and per **R2-039** the
  rows it exports have up to 11 blank columns.
- **Suggested fix:** either generate a genuine workbook (e.g. SheetJS, already a common dep) for the
  Excel option, or rename the menu item to "Export as CSV (Excel-compatible)" and drop the `.xlsx`
  extension. Do not ship a mislabelled file.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.
- **Auditor note — what was NOT verified:** clicking **Export as CSV** in the browser produced no
  observable blob via an intercepted `URL.createObjectURL`, and no console error. Source shows the
  path does call `createObjectURL` (`:741`), so this is most likely the same hidden-pane interaction
  limitation that produced six earlier false positives in this audit, **not** a broken export.
  **CSV export is therefore recorded as UNVERIFIED, not as a defect.** The `.xlsx` mislabelling above
  is asserted from source and does not depend on that interaction.

### FINDING R2-041 — GSTR-1/GSTR-2 can never produce IGST; tax is always split 50/50 CGST/SGST
- **Severity:** **HIGH** (statutory/compliance) — an inter-state supply filed as intra-state is a
  reporting error that attracts notices and interest
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/reports.py:1000-1008` (`_gst_split`), used by `_rep_gstr1_sales`
  (`:1011`) and the GSTR-2 purchase builder
```python
def _gst_split(tax_amount):
    """Clearly-labeled standard assumption: no place-of-supply data available,
    so split the tax equally into CGST and SGST, IGST/UTGST = 0."""
    half = tax / 2.0
    return half, half, 0.0, 0.0
```
- **Verified live** on `/reports/gstr1-sales` with a real ₹1,18,000 invoice (₹100,000 taxable + 18%):
  `Invoice Amount 118000 | Tax Amount 18000 | CGST 9000 | SGST 9000 | IGST 0`.
  The arithmetic is correct **for an intra-state supply** — and that is the only outcome the function
  can ever produce.
- **The defect:** the split is unconditional. There is no place-of-supply comparison, so
  **IGST is structurally unreachable** — the column exists and is always `0`. Any inter-state sale
  is reported as CGST+SGST, which is the wrong head of tax on a statutory return.
- **The data to do this properly is present:** `Project.state`, `LibraryParty.address`, and the
  company's own GSTIN (whose first two digits encode the state) are all stored. Place of supply is
  derivable; the function simply doesn't attempt it.
- **Credit where due:** unlike most findings in this audit, the assumption is **explicitly documented
  in the code** rather than silently wrong. The gap is that the assumption is invisible **to the
  person filing** — the report renders an IGST column of zeros with no caveat, and it is exported to
  Excel/PDF for an accountant.
- **Two related gaps observed in the same report:**
  1. **No "Taxable Value" column.** GSTR-1 B2B requires taxable value and tax separately; the report
     shows only `Invoice Amount` (₹118,000, tax-inclusive) and `Tax Amount`. A filer must derive
     ₹100,000 by subtraction, and could easily report ₹118,000 as taxable value.
  2. **Party GST renders blank**, so rows cannot be filed as B2B. In this instance the test party
     genuinely has no GSTIN, so this is noted as a data-completeness observation rather than a defect.
- **Suggested fix:** derive place of supply from the company GSTIN state vs the party/project state,
  emit IGST when they differ, add a Taxable Value column, and surface an on-screen caveat whenever the
  split is assumed rather than determined.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-042 — 🔴 Payments recorded in the UI can never settle an invoice (no party sent)
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — invoices remain "Unpaid" forever no matter how much is paid against them
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/finance/page.tsx:524-537` (payment POST body) vs
  `backend/app/routers/finance.py:136` (settlement guard)
- **The backend has working FIFO auto-settlement** — on `POST /finance/payments` it matches the
  payment against that party's outstanding bills and updates `paid_amount` / `status`:
```python
# FIFO Auto-Settlement Logic against Outstanding Bills
if party_uuid:                       # ← only runs when a party is supplied
    target_inv_type = list(REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES) if req.payment_type == "in" else list(EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES)
    query = db.query(Bill).filter(Bill.party_company_user_id == party_uuid, Bill.status != "Paid")
```
- **The frontend never sends a party.** The payload contains `company_id, project_id, payment_type,
  amount, payment_method, reference_number, description, payment_date` — **`party_company_user_id` is
  absent**. `party_uuid` is therefore always `None`, so **the settlement block never executes for any
  payment created through the UI.**
- **Observed live.** After recording a ₹50,000 payment-in against the project, all three bills remain:

| Invoice | Type | Total | Paid | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZZ-QA-AUDIT-001 | sale | 118,000 | **0** | **Unpaid** |
| ZTEST-001 | purchase | 11,800 | 0 | Unpaid |
| TALLY-001 | purchase | 11,800 | 0 | Unpaid |

  The payment exists (`in_total: 50000`) but is orphaned — attached to no party and no bill.
- **Consequences that cascade through the product:**
  - Receivables/payables never reduce; every invoice ages as unpaid indefinitely.
  - `Balance Due` / `Payment Received` in reports stay empty (compounding **R2-039**).
  - Party ledgers and `to_pay`/`to_receive` in the Enterprise Rollup (**R2-025**) never reflect
    settlement.
  - The project dashboard's `paid_amount`-based `cashIn` (the *correct* calculation sitting unused at
    `dashboard/page.tsx:246`) would read ₹0 even if it were wired up — so **R2-021 cannot be fixed by
    switching to `paid_amount` until this is fixed too.**
- **Second defect in the same payload — confirms R2-012:** `payment_method` is hardcoded to
  `"Cash"`. Every payment is stored as Cash regardless of what the user picks, which is exactly what
  the unwired "Payment Method" radio group (R2-012) implied. Bank/cheque/UPI reconciliation is
  impossible.
- **Suggested fix:** add a party selector to the payment form and send `party_company_user_id` (the
  backend logic is already correct and needs no change), and bind `payment_method` to the radio group.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-043 — 🔴 Tally export pushes receipts and transfers into Tally as PURCHASE vouchers
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — writes incorrect voucher types into the customer's external accounting system
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/tally.py:548-553` (bill selection) and `:202-212` (classification)
- **The selection has no type filter:**
```python
bills = db.query(Bill).filter(
    Bill.company_id == comp_uuid,
    Bill.status != "Cancelled",
    Bill.tally_synced == False,
    Bill.invoice_date >= conn.sync_window_start_date,
).all()          # ← every invoice_type is included
```
- **The classification is binary:**
```python
if b.invoice_type in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES:   # sale, material_sale
    vchtype = "Sales"
else:
    vchtype = "Purchase"                       # ← catch-all for EVERYTHING else
```
- **Consequence.** Under the 12-value canonical vocabulary established during the invoice_type
  remediation, the `else` branch swallows the settlement and movement types, all of which are created
  as `Bill` rows by the Transaction page:

| Bill `invoice_type` | Exported to Tally as | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| `payment_in` | **Purchase** ❌ | Receipt voucher |
| `i_received` | **Purchase** ❌ | Receipt voucher |
| `payment_out` | **Purchase** ❌ | Payment voucher |
| `i_paid` | **Purchase** ❌ | Payment voucher |
| `material_transfer` | **Purchase** ❌ | Stock Journal / not a purchase |
| `material_return` | **Purchase** ❌ | Debit Note / Rejection Out |
| `purchase`, `subcon`, `expense`, `equipment` | Purchase ✅ | correct |
| `sale`, `material_sale` | Sales ✅ | correct |

- **Compounding — the same money can post twice.** Cash received has two routes in this product:
  the Transaction page (creates a `Bill` with `invoice_type='payment_in'`) and Finance → payments
  (creates a `Payment` row). The exporter queries **both** — `bills` at `:548` and `payments` at
  `:554` — so a receipt entered as a transaction posts as a *Purchase voucher* while a receipt entered
  as a payment posts as a *Receipt voucher*. The same economic event is typed differently depending
  on which screen the user used, and a company using both screens will overstate purchases.
- **Why this is worse than an internal display bug:** every other financial finding in this report
  produces a wrong number on a SiteFlow screen. This one writes wrong entries into **Tally**, the
  customer's system of record, where they must then be found and reversed by an accountant.
- **Note:** `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES` is already imported in this file (`:16`) but never used — the
  `else` branch was left as a catch-all when the constants were introduced.
- **Suggested fix:** classify explicitly against all four buckets — `REVENUE → Sales`,
  `EXPENSE → Purchase`, `SETTLEMENT → Receipt/Payment by direction`, `MOVEMENT → Stock Journal or
  excluded — and either skip settlement-type bills entirely (since `Payment` rows already cover them)
  or de-duplicate the two sources.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

#### R2-043 (cont.) — the same catch-all also corrupts the internal Finance ledger
`backend/app/routers/finance.py:306-316` repeats the pattern on the company ledger:
```python
is_receipt  = obj.invoice_type in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES          # payment_in → False
debit       = amount if is_receipt else 0.0
credit      = 0.0 if is_receipt else amount
running_balance += amount if is_receipt else -amount
category    = "Client Invoice" if REVENUE else ("Subcon Invoice" if subcon else "Material Bill")
ledger_head = "Revenue"        if REVENUE else ("Subcon Cost"    if subcon else "Material Cost")
```
A `payment_in` bill (money **received**) is therefore posted as a **credit**, **subtracted** from the
running balance, and labelled **"Material Bill" / "Material Cost"**. The sign of the entry is
inverted and the ledger head is wrong — inside SiteFlow's own ledger, not just the Tally export.

#### R2-043 (cont. 2) — THIRD instance: the Party Ledger report
`backend/app/routers/reports.py:628-639` repeats it again, in a report that is exported and handed to
parties and accountants:
```python
is_receipt = obj.invoice_type in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES
if is_receipt:  txn_type="Sale Invoice";   party_type="Client"; debit  = amount; running += amount
else:           txn_type="Purchase Bill";  party_type="Vendor"; credit = amount; running -= amount
```
A `payment_in` bill — money **received from a client** — is rendered in the party ledger as a
**"Purchase Bill"** from a **"Vendor"**, posted as a **credit**, with the running balance moving
**down** instead of up. Four attributes wrong on one row, in the document a client may be shown to
reconcile their account.

**Scope of the constants refactor, measured:** `analytics.py` *was* updated correctly and even
handles settlement explicitly (`:579` uses `SETTLEMENT_INVOICE_TYPES`). Three separate ledger/export
classifiers were left binary — `tally.py:202` (external accounting), `finance.py:306` (internal
ledger), `reports.py:628` (party ledger report) — all three written as
`if invoice_type in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES: … else: <treat as purchase>`. So the remediation covered
some call sites and not others, consistent with R2-036 (5 unfiltered aggregation sites), R2-041 (GST
split) and R2-044 (bare `"sale"` gates).
**Any fix should sweep every `invoice_type` branch in the backend, not just the ones named here.**

**Cleared in the same file (checked, correct):** `reports.py:83` (`== "subcon"` — a single canonical
type, correct), `:748` and `:1013` (`in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES`), `:1044` (`in EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES`).

### FINDING R2-044 — `billing.py` gates use bare `"sale"` where a bucket is meant (ZATCA + 3-way match)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — one compliance gap, one control applied to the wrong records
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/billing.py:430`, `:543`, `:730`

**(a) ZATCA e-invoicing excludes material sales** — `:430`
```python
if bill.invoice_type != "sale":
    raise HTTPException(400, "ZATCA e-invoicing applies to sale (simplified tax) invoices")
```
`material_sale` is a revenue invoice — a taxable supply — but is **blocked from generating a ZATCA
e-invoice**. Under Saudi ZATCA rules a taxable supply requires an e-invoice regardless of whether the
line items are services or materials. Should test `in REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES`.

**(b) 3-way matching is applied to settlement and movement bills** — `:543`, `:730`
```python
if invoice_type == "sale":       # 3-way matching is a purchase-side control; ignore for sale invoices
    return None
...
if bill.invoice_type == "sale":  # Sale invoices are exempt from 3-way matching
    bill.match_id = None
```
Only literal `"sale"` is exempted. So `material_sale`, and every settlement type
(`payment_in`, `payment_out`, `i_paid`, `i_received`) and movement type
(`material_transfer`, `material_return`), fall into the **purchase-side** branch and are subjected to
PO↔GRN↔Invoice three-way matching — a control that is meaningless for a receipt or an internal
transfer. The stated intent in the comments ("purchase-side control") is correct; the implementation
tests one string instead of the bucket.

**Not defects (checked):** `:376` is a user-supplied filter passthrough; `:474` is the PDF label map,
which correctly enumerates all eight recognition/movement types and raises 400 on anything else;
`:643` selects the terms template and defaulting non-subcon to "invoice" is reasonable.

- **Suggested fix:** `REVENUE_INVOICE_TYPES` for the ZATCA gate; exempt
  `REVENUE ∪ SETTLEMENT ∪ MOVEMENT` from three-way matching.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

---

### FINDING R2-045 — BI export silently omits "Other Expense" and "Equipment Expense" bills
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — actual cost is understated in the external BI/analytics feed
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/bi_export.py:255-275`
- The export builds four budget-vs-actual pairs, each sourced separately:

| Category | Actual sourced from | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Material | `Bill.invoice_type == "purchase"` | `purchase` only |
| Subcon | `Bill.invoice_type == "subcon"` | `subcon` only |
| Labour | `PayrollLineItem.net_payable` | payroll, not bills |
| Equipment | deployment hourly cost + fuel | **not bills at all** |

- **The gap:** bills of type **`expense`** (Other Expense) and **`equipment`** (Equipment Expense) —
  both canonical, both creatable from the Transaction page — are counted in **none** of the four
  categories. `equipment_actual` is derived from equipment *deployments and fuel*, explicitly not from
  equipment-type bills (the code comment says it "mirrors finance.get_project_pl").
- **Consequence:** a company that records Other Expense or Equipment Expense transactions sees those
  costs in the SiteFlow UI but **nowhere in the BI export**, so total actual cost — and therefore every
  variance and margin computed downstream in the BI tool — is understated by their full value.
- **Contrast:** `finance.get_project_pl` was corrected during the invoice_type remediation to use
  `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES` (which includes `expense` and `equipment`). The BI export was not updated to
  match, so the two now disagree about the same project's cost.
- **Suggested fix:** add the missing types to the appropriate categories (or add an "Other" cost line),
  and reconcile against `get_project_pl` so the BI feed and the in-app P&L agree.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

**Cleared in the same sweep (checked, correct):** `subcon_performance.py:250` (`== "subcon"` — a single
canonical type, correct for a subcontractor scorecard) and `budgeting.py:291`
(`in BILLING_TYPES`, which was correctly repointed to `{"sale", "material_sale"}` during the
remediation).

## METHOD NOTE — how the fake-success class was enumerated (and its limits)

A scripted scan over every `.tsx` under `frontend/src/app/c` looked for inline `onClick={() =>` bodies
that emit a success message (`toast`/`triggerLocalToast`/`setMessage`/`setSuccess`/`setSyncMessage`/
`alert` containing success|saved|added|updated|created|recorded|submitted|approved|sent) **without**
any `fetch(` / `await` / `jpost` / `jput` / `jdel` / `jpatch` in the handler body.

**Result: exactly 4 hits** — `hr/page.tsx:1747, 1853, 2010` (R2-013) and `home/page.tsx:546` (R2-015).

**Known limits of this scan — do not read it as proof the class is exhausted:**
- It only inspects **inline arrow handlers**. `flushQueue` (R2-014, the CRITICAL one) is a *named*
  function and was **not** caught by it — that was found by reading the attendance module directly.
  Other named handlers could hide the same defect.
- It uses a 16-line window, so a success call further from the handler opening is missed.
- It cannot detect handlers that call an API but ignore the response (R2-006/R2-007 class), which is
  a separate pattern found via the `"using local only"` search.
- An earlier, looser version of this heuristic returned **273** candidates, nearly all false
  positives (Cancel buttons, modal openers, toggles). That number is recorded only to make clear it
  was rejected rather than reported.

### A second scan that was run and DISCARDED
A scan for "rendered list state never populated from the network" (looking for a `useState` array
that is `.map()`-rendered whose setter never appears within 12 lines of a `fetch`/`await`/`.json()`)
returned **23 candidates**. On verification it was almost entirely false positives — the window was
too narrow, because these pages commonly transform the response through a long `.map()` between the
fetch and the setter. Confirmed fed-from-server despite being flagged:
`quality:137/138/140` (`setChecklists(currentChecklists)` after a checked `clRes.ok`),
`hr:137` (`setEmployees(mapped)`), `payroll-attendance:294` (`setDeductions(b.deductions ?? [])`),
`settings:744` (`setBTypes(settings.construction_types ?? [])`).

**The scan is not evidence of anything and its output is not reported as findings.** The three
genuinely disconnected surfaces (R2-017 dashboard projects, R2-019 HR holidays, R2-020 DPR
measurement book) were each confirmed by reading every reference to the setter individually, which
is the only method that held up.

### FINDING R2-005 — Plaster calculator shows brick reference notes, no plaster guidance
- **Severity:** LOW (content correctness / usefulness)
- **Where:** Plaster tab, `/c/{cid}/d/reports/calculators`, "ENGINEERING & TAKEOFF REFERENCE NOTES"
- **Evidence:** with Plaster active the notes read: "Modular Brick dimensions: 190 x 90 x 90 mm.
  Traditional Brick: 230 x 110 x 75 mm." / "Standard mortar joint thickness is 10 mm." / "Mortar
  volume constitutes ~30% of total brick wall volume." The word "plaster" does not appear.
- **Not a stale-state bug:** verified deterministic — navigating Bricks → Plaster → Paint → Plaster
  reproduces the same brick notes every time, and Paint correctly shows paint-specific notes. So the
  notes block is mis-assigned content, not a React state leak.
- **Impact:** the panel gives no plaster guidance at all (dry factor 1.33, 1:4 mix, standard 12 mm
  internal / 15–20 mm external thickness) — precisely the reference a user needs to sanity-check the
  output, which matters more given R2-004's hidden allowance.
- **Note:** the Paint notes block also carries an unrelated tile line ("Tile quantities account for
  grout width additions"), suggesting the notes are grouped per category rather than per calculator.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-006 — Drawings module cannot create a first drawing; failure is silent
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — an entire module is unusable from a cold start, and it fails with no
  feedback whatsoever
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/d/drawings`; handler in
  `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/drawings/page.tsx` (~line 262)
- **Action performed (real UI):** opened Drawings on a project with no drawings. Empty state reads
  *"No drawings found for this project. Use "Upload New Revision" to add the first one."* Clicked
  **↑ Upload New Revision**, entered Version Code `V1`, clicked **Publish V1**.
- **Observed:** nothing happens. Modal stays open, no drawing is created, list still shows
  "No drawings found", and **no error is surfaced to the user**. No console error captured either.
- **Root cause (source-confirmed):**
  1. The modal can only create a *revision*: its fields are Version Code and Release Notes. There is
     **no drawing name, no category, and no file input at all** — despite the button saying "Upload".
     It also states "Current revision will be automatically archived as Superseded" when no current
     revision exists.
  2. The handler POSTs to `/apis/v3/drawings/${activeDrawingId}/revisions`. With zero drawings,
     `activeDrawingId` is null, so the request cannot succeed.
  3. `POST /apis/v3/drawings` — the endpoint that actually creates a drawing, backed by
     `DrawingCreateRequest` (`backend/app/routers/drawings.py:57`) — **has no frontend caller
     anywhere in the codebase.** (This is the same orphaned endpoint noted during the invoice_type
     remediation; its consequence is now identified.)
  4. The failure is deliberately swallowed:
     ```js
     if (!res.ok) throw new Error("Failed to publish revision");
     } catch (err) { console.error("Revision publish error, using local only:", err); }
     setDrawings(prev => prev.map(...))   // runs regardless of failure
     ```
     The catch only logs, and the local state update executes unconditionally afterwards.
- **Impact:** no user can ever add a drawing through the UI. The empty state actively instructs them
  to do something impossible, and the app gives zero indication anything went wrong.
- **Suggested fix:** wire a real "New Drawing" flow calling `POST /apis/v3/drawings` (name, category
  from the 3 allowed values, file_url), and surface fetch failures to the user instead of
  `console.error` + optimistic local state.
- **Related:** this is the same silent-failure anti-pattern previously found in `handleToggleLock`
  in this file (fixed during the invoice_type remediation). **The pattern still exists here**, which
  suggests the earlier fix was applied to one call site rather than swept across the file. Every
  mutation handler in this module should be audited for it.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

### FINDING R2-007 — Purchase Order vendor is never saved; UI shows a fabricated vendor instead
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — POs are persisted with no vendor, and the UI actively misrepresents that
- **Where:** `/c/{cid}/d/procurement`, `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/procurement/page.tsx`
- **Action performed (real UI, empirically proven):** clicked `+ Purchase Order`, set PO No.
  `ZZ-QA-PO-001`, saved. PO appeared in the list showing vendor **"Shree Cement Traders"**, total
  ₹48,380 (100 × ₹410 + 18% GST — arithmetic correct). **Reloaded the page.** The PO persisted, but
  the vendor column now reads a generic **"Vendor"**. The vendor was never stored.
- **Root cause (source-confirmed):**
  - The PO create modal has **no vendor selector at all** (fields: PO number, item name, qty, rate).
  - `newPOVendor` is initialised to the hardcoded string `"Shree Cement Traders"` (line 239) and only
    written into the local object (`vendor: newPOVendor`, line 337).
  - The POST body sends `company_id, project_id, po_number, po_date, items, terms` — **`vendor_id` is
    never sent.**
  - The backend fully supports it: `POCreateRequest.vendor_id` (procurement.py:63), stored at
    line 433, resolved to a vendor name at line 918, and `PurchaseOrder.vendor_id` exists on the
    model (models.py:419, FK → company_team).
  - On reload the loader substitutes the literal placeholder `vendor: "Vendor"` (line 160).
- **Impact:** every PO created through the UI is vendorless in the database — unusable as a
  procurement record, and it breaks vendor-linked reporting (PO Summary, Vendor Performance,
  three-way match). Worse, the user is shown a specific vendor name at creation time, so there is no
  indication anything was dropped.
- **Suggested fix:** add a vendor selector bound to the company's parties and send `vendor_id`. The
  backend needs no change. Remove the hardcoded default.
- **Not yet fixed** — reported only.

- **Severity:** **HIGH** (integrity) — fabricated document counts and stock imagery on an empty project
- **Where — BOTH drawings routes (confirmed live on each):**

  - `/c/{cid}/p/{pid}/drawings` → **Project Files** tab — same phantom folders, same 3 Unsplash images

- **Observed (rendered live):**

# ROUND 3 — CONTINUATION SWEEP (2026-07-26, new session)

**Scope of this continuation:** complete the sweep the Round 2 handoff left open — the ~40 unopened
routes, edit/delete flows, approval workflows, cross-linking integrity, and the remaining systematic
source scans. Findings are numbered **R2-046 onward** to preserve the existing sequence.

Two scans were *invalidated during this session and corrected before reporting* (see the METHOD
NOTES in each section) — the raw output of a scan is never reported as a finding here.

## 🧭 NAVIGATION REACHABILITY — measured, whole-console

The single largest structural defect found this round. It also explains why Round 2 had "~40
unopened routes": **most of them cannot be reached by clicking anything.**

### The complete set of navigation sources in the console
| Source | File | Destinations offered |
|---|---|---|
| Main sidebar | `components/Sidebar.tsx:80-211, 324-348` | **16** |
| Project tab bar | `app/c/[company_id]/p/[project_id]/layout.tsx:9-23` (`TABS`) | **13** |
| Company home cards | `d/home/page.tsx:342, 372, 502, 540` | 3 (payment-approval, todo, planning/gantt) |
| Projects page | `projects/page.tsx:197, 211, 307` | 3 |
| Procurement page | `d/procurement/page.tsx:581` | 1 (vendor-performance) |
| Library / project dashboard | `d/library/page.tsx`, `p/[pid]/dashboard/page.tsx` | 2 (materials, cost-codes) |
| **Help article body text** | `d/help/helpContent.tsx` | **14** (see R2-048) |

`app/c/[company_id]/layout.tsx:71-89` also mentions nearly every route, but it is a **page-title
lookup** (`if (pathname.includes("/d/finance")) return "Finance"`), not navigation. It renders no

### FINDING R2-046 — 🔴 28 project-level routes have zero inbound links (unreachable by clicking)
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — entire built, maintained modules are inaccessible to users
- **Evidence:** for each project module, a search for any project-scoped link
  (a `p/${...}/<name>` template or a `slug: "<name>"` nav entry), excluding the module's own page:

  **Reachable — the 13 entries in `TABS`:** dashboard, boq, party, transaction, todo, task,
  attendance, material, subcon, files, mom, equipment, quality.

  **Unreachable — 0 inbound links anywhere in `frontend/src`:**
  `billing`, `budgeting`, `budgeting/boq`, `chat`, `crm`, `custom-fields`, `depreciation`, `dpr`,
  `drawings`, `face-recognition`, `finance`, `hr`, `labour`, `planning`, `planning/gantt`,
  `procurement`, `procurement/rfq`, `procurement/vendor-performance`, `production`, `reports`,
  `reports/calculators`, `safety`, `statutory`, `subcon/scorecards`,
  `subcon/work-orders/amendments`, `three-way`, `towers`, `wastage`.
- **Impact:** 28 routes ship in the production bundle, render, hold real logic, and are maintained —
  and no user can navigate to them. Several are modules the marketing site advertises (DPR, drawings,
  labour, statutory). They can only be reached by typing a URL containing two UUIDs.
- **Cross-reference:** this is *why* Round 2 could not open ~40 routes. It is not an audit coverage

Every static `href` / `router.push` / `router.replace` target in `frontend/src` (all 120 app routes,
template literals normalized to a wildcard segment) resolves to a real route. **Zero broken links.**
The navigation defect is one of omission, not of wrong targets.

that mangled `[param]` segments). Both were fixed and the corrected run returns 1 hit, itself a
dynamic tab construction (`p/[project_id]/layout.tsx:75`) that resolves correctly. **No broken-link
finding exists — do not re-derive one from the uncorrected output.**

## 🔐 TENANT ISOLATION — swept, and it is solid

### ✅ Verified good — no IDOR across the router surface
Every endpoint taking a non-`company_id` path parameter was checked for a company or project guard
(`get_company_membership`, `verify_company_access`, `verify_project_access`,
`verify_project_in_company`, `require_permission`). **Exactly one endpoint has no guard:**
`auth.py:804 GET /resolve-company/{slug}` — intentionally public (pre-login company lookup).
Everything else is guarded, most via the `verify_project_access` dependency.

**Method note — this scan was wrong on its first run and is reported only after correction.** The
first pass omitted `verify_project_access` from the guard list and reported **31 unguarded
endpoints**. Spot-reading `projects.py:309` and `towers.py:67` showed both carry
`Depends(verify_project_access)`. The corrected list collapses 31 false positives to 1 intentional
case. **Do not cite the uncorrected figure.**

### FINDING R2-049 — 🔴 Equipment code uniqueness is global, not per company (cross-tenant)
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — multi-tenancy violation: cross-tenant denial of service and information
  disclosure
- **Where:** `backend/app/models.py:919` — `code = Column(String(100), unique=True, nullable=False)`
  on `Equipment`; enforced at `backend/app/routers/equipment.py:117`:
```py
existing = db.query(Equipment).filter(Equipment.code == payload.code).first()
if existing:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Equipment code already exists")
```
- **The defect:** the query has **no `company_id` filter**, and the DB constraint is global. Every
  other duplicate guard in the codebase is company-scoped — `billing.py:303` (WO number),
  `billing.py:571` (invoice number), `procurement.py:278` (indent), `procurement.py:405` (PO),
  `procurement.py:591` (GRN) and `finance.py:120` (payment reference) all filter by company.
  Equipment is the sole exception.
- **Impact, three ways:**
  1. **Cross-tenant DoS.** Company B cannot register equipment with a code Company A already used.
     Equipment codes are short and conventional (`EXC-01`, `JCB-01`, `CRANE-1`, `TM-02`), so
     collisions are near-certain as tenant count grows, and the first tenant to register a code
     squats it platform-wide.
  2. **Cross-tenant information disclosure.** The 400 confirms that *some other company* owns that
     code — an oracle for probing another tenant's fleet numbering.
  3. **Inexplicable failure.** The message says "Equipment code already exists" while the user's own
     fleet list shows no such code.
- **Suggested fix:** filter by `payload.company_id` at `:117`, and replace the column-level
  `unique=True` with `UniqueConstraint("company_id", "code")` plus a migration. Check for existing
  cross-tenant duplicates before applying the constraint.

## ✅ APPROVAL WORKFLOWS — untested in Round 2, swept here, and they are broken

### FINDING R2-050 — 🔴 Indent and PO approvals mark themselves approved regardless of the server
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — an authorization control that displays "approved" whether or not the
  server agreed
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/procurement/page.tsx`
  — `handleApproveIndent` (`:307-323`) and `handleApprovePO` (`:386-402`)
- **The code (both identical in shape):**
```js
const handleApproveIndent = async (id) => {
  try {
    await fetch(`${apiHost}/apis/v3/procurement/indents/${id}/approve`, { method: "POST", ... });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("Indent approve error:", err);      // <- swallowed
  }
  setIndents(prev => prev.map(ind =>                  // <- runs unconditionally, outside the try
    ind.id === id ? { ...ind, status: "approved" } : ind));
};
```
  `handleApprovePO` does the same, setting `{ approvalFlag: "approved", status: "sent" }`.
- **Why this is worse than the other unchecked mutations:** the state update sits **after** the
  `catch`, so it executes on *every* path — network failure, 403, 422, 500. The response is never
  inspected. A user without approval permission clicks Approve, the server correctly refuses, and
  the UI shows the indent as **approved** and the PO as **approved and sent**.
- **Impact:** the approval control cannot be trusted as a record of what was approved. A PO displayed
  as "sent" may never have been approved server-side. Until the page is reloaded there is no signal
  that anything failed, and the console error is invisible to the user.
- **Suggested fix:** check `res.ok`, surface the server's message on failure, and re-read the list
  from the server rather than patching local state. **Re-test RBAC after fixing** — the entire point
  of an approval gate is that a rejection is visible.

### FINDING R2-051 — 🔴 GRN creation sends placeholder item IDs and falls back to "local only"
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — goods-receipt records are either rejected or written with meaningless
  line references, and inventory moves locally either way
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/procurement/page.tsx:456-472`
- **Two separate defects in one handler:**
  1. **Placeholder foreign keys transmitted as real data:**
```js
items: receivedItems.map((item, idx) => ({ po_item_id: `placeholder-${idx}`, received_qty: item.qty }))
```
     `po_item_id` is sent as the literal string `placeholder-0`, `placeholder-1`, … The real PO item
     IDs are never looked up. Depending on backend validation this either 422s every GRN or stores
     line items that reference nothing.
  2. **The failure is designed to be invisible:**
```js
} catch (err) {
  console.error("GRN create error, using local only:", err);
}
setInventory(prev => ...)          // <- inventory updated regardless
```
     The comment states the intent outright. Stock levels move in the UI whether or not the GRN
     persisted; the response is never checked, so even a 422 from defect (1) lands here silently.
- **Impact:** goods receipt is the point where a PO becomes a liability and stock becomes real. A GRN
  that appears to succeed but was rejected leaves the PO unreceived, the stock figure wrong until
  reload, and no error anywhere. Combined with R2-050 (PO shown as "sent" when it was not), the whole
  procure-to-pay chain can display a state the database does not hold.
- **Also at this location — fabricated data of the R2-008 class:**
  - `:440` `receivedBy: "Amit K (Site Engineer)"` — a hardcoded invented person credited as the
    receiver on every GRN
  - `:380` the PO line-item form defaults to `{ name: "UltraTech Cement", qty: 100, unit: "bags",
    rate: 410 }` — a real third-party brand and an invented rate pre-filled into a financial form
  - `:303` / `:382` document numbers generated as `IND-2026-0${indents.length + 4}` and
    `PO-2026-0${pos.length + 43}` — magic offsets 4 and 43 over the length of the *currently loaded*
    list. They collide on reload, break past 10 records (`PO-2026-053`), and bear no relation to any
    server sequence. The backend already generates and validates these numbers
    (`procurement.py:278, 405`).
- **Suggested fix:** resolve real `po_item_id` values from the selected PO, check `res.ok`, refresh
  inventory from the server, delete the hardcoded receiver and brand defaults, and take document
  numbers from the backend.

## 💸 PAYMENT REQUESTS — schema-level defects

### FINDING R2-052 — 🔴 `PaymentRequest.party_company_user_id` points at `users`, not `company_team`
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — payment requests are impossible for any party without a platform login,
  and the party name stored is the wrong entity
- **Where:** `backend/app/models.py:1507`
```py
# PaymentRequest
party_company_user_id = Column(UUID, ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False)
```
  compared with the **same column name** on four other tables (`models.py:578, 618, 633, 1152`):
```py
party_company_user_id = Column(UUID, ForeignKey("company_team.id"), nullable=False)
```
- **The frontend already compensates, which proves the inconsistency is live:**
  `p/[project_id]/transaction/page.tsx` sends `member.company_team_id` to `/billing/bills`,
  `/billing/debit-notes` and `/billing/credit-notes` (`:499, :530, :543`) but `member.user_id` to
  `/finance/payment-requests/{cid}` (`:555`). One field name, two meanings, and every caller must
  remember which.
- **Consequence 1 — external parties cannot receive a payment request.** `CompanyTeam.user_id`
  (`models.py:263`) is nullable and `CompanyTeam.library_party_id` (`:266`) exists precisely so a
  vendor with no login can be a party. For such a party `member.user_id` is null, and the schema
  field is a required non-optional UUID (`finance.py:512`) → **422**. Payment requests are therefore
  unavailable for exactly the counterparties they are most needed for.
- **Consequence 2 — the wrong name is stored.** `finance.py:1106-1107`:
```py
user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == data.party_company_user_id).first()
party_name = user.name if user else "Unknown Party"
```
  The **login user's** name is written to `party_name`, not the party's. Where no user matches, the
  request is stored as the literal string **"Unknown Party"** instead of being rejected.
- **Suggested fix:** repoint the FK at `company_team.id` to match every sibling table, resolve
  `party_name` from the library party, and migrate existing rows. If the FK must stay for now,
  **rename the column** so the two meanings cannot be confused — a silent mis-join between `users`
  and `company_team` is exactly what this invites.
- **Cross-reference:** same failure class as **R2-042** (payments never settle because the frontend
  omits `party_company_user_id`). Fix them together.

### FINDING R2-053 — Payment request `details` is required by the API but supplied from "Ship To"
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — a payment request cannot be created unless an unrelated field is filled in
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/finance.py:515` (`details: str` — required, no default) vs
  `backend/app/models.py:1512` (`details = Column(String, nullable=True)` — optional) vs
  `frontend/.../p/[project_id]/transaction/page.tsx:557` (`details: shipTo || null`)
- **Evidence:** the modal's **Ship To** input is the only source for `details`. Leaving it blank
  sends `null` into a required `str` → **422**. Schema and model disagree on whether the field is
  optional, and the UI labels it as something else entirely.
- **Mitigating:** unlike R2-050/R2-051 this error *is* surfaced — the modal shows
  `Save failed (422): ...` (`transaction/page.tsx:565-569`). It fails loudly but inexplicably: the
  user is told the save failed with no indication that "Ship To" is the cause.
- **Suggested fix:** make `details` `Optional[str] = None` to match the model, or give the
  payment-request branch its own labelled, required "Details" field rather than borrowing Ship To.

### FINDING R2-054 — `request_no` is generated by counting rows, so numbers repeat after a deletion
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — duplicate document numbers in a finance module
- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/finance.py:1110-1112`
```py
count = db.query(PaymentRequest).filter(PaymentRequest.company_id == company_id).count()
request_no = f"PR-{count + 1}"
```
- **Evidence:** `request_no` has **no unique constraint** (`models.py:1516` —
  `Column(String(50), nullable=True)`) and **no duplicate guard**, unlike invoice numbers
  (`billing.py:571`), PO numbers (`procurement.py:405`) and payment references (`finance.py:120`),
  all of which are explicitly checked. Delete PR-2 of three and the next create counts 2 and emits
  **PR-3**, which already exists. Two concurrent creates also both read the same count.
- **Impact:** duplicated payment-request numbers in the approval queue and in the party ledger export
  (`reports.py:516`), with no way to tell the rows apart.
- **Suggested fix:** derive from the highest existing number rather than the row count, or use a
  per-company sequence, and add the same duplicate guard the sibling documents already have.

## 🔁 UNCHECKED MUTATIONS — full sweep of every write in the console

Round 2 filed R2-016 as a single instance. This is the complete measured set: every `fetch` with
method `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` in `frontend/src`, classified by whether the response is
inspected.

**Verified individually — these DO check their response and are correct (not findings):**
`p/[project_id]/transaction/page.tsx:493, 524, 537, 550` (all four branches share one
`if (res.ok) ... else setErr("Save failed (...)")` at `:565`), `d/library/page.tsx:199`,
`app/login/page.tsx:90`, `d/planning/gantt/page.tsx:344`. Four further scan hits
(`d/labour:83`, `settings:437`, `settings:492`, `ProjectSettingsModal:78`) are **GET** requests
inside `Promise.all` blocks that the scan window mis-attributed to a later POST — **false positives,
not findings.**

### FINDING R2-055 — 16 confirmed unchecked writes, covering every edit and delete flow
- **Severity:** **HIGH** in aggregate — this is the entire untested "edit/delete flows" surface from
  the Round 2 handoff, and none of it reports failure
- **Confirmed sites (response never inspected, no error path to the user):**

  | File | Line | Op | What silently fails |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `projects/page.tsx` | 157 | DELETE | **Delete a project** |
  | `projects/page.tsx` | 840 | PUT | Edit project |
  | `projects/page.tsx` | 880 | DELETE | Delete project location |
  | `projects/page.tsx` | 148 | POST | Pin / unpin project |
  | `components/ProjectSettingsModal.tsx` | 87 | PUT | Edit project settings |
  | `components/ProjectSettingsModal.tsx` | 123 | DELETE | Delete location |
  | `p/[project_id]/layout.tsx` | 82 | PUT | **Change project status** (sets local state at `:87`) |
  | `p/[project_id]/party/page.tsx` | 81 | DELETE | Remove a party from the project |
  | `p/[project_id]/party/page.tsx` | 90 | PUT | Edit project party |
  | `p/[project_id]/todo/page.tsx` | 64 | PUT | Toggle / edit a to-do |
  | `p/[project_id]/todo/page.tsx` | 73 | DELETE | Delete a to-do |
  | `p/[project_id]/boq/page.tsx` | 250 | POST | **BOQ Excel import** — the only way to add BOQ lines (see R2-030) |
  | `d/finance/page.tsx` | 1002 | POST | Create work order |
  | `d/finance/page.tsx` | 837, 850, 855, 874 | POST | Tally party / ledger / cost-centre mappings |
  | `d/subcon/scorecards/page.tsx` | 56 | POST | Recompute subcontractor scorecards |
  | `d/attendance/page.tsx` 504 · `p/[pid]/attendance/page.tsx` 500 | | POST | **Subcontractor crew attendance** |

- **Two severity tiers within this list:**
  - **Self-correcting but silent** — `projects/page.tsx` and `ProjectSettingsModal` call `load()`
    afterwards, so the UI eventually re-reads the truth from the server. The defect is that a failed
    delete or edit produces **no message at all**: an RBAC rejection is indistinguishable from a
    click that did nothing.
  - **Actively wrong** — `p/[project_id]/layout.tsx:82` writes the new status into local state at
    `:87` regardless, and the attendance handler below alerts success.
- **The worst of the group — subcontractor crew attendance** (`d/attendance/page.tsx:486-516`):
```js
for (const row of subconRows) {
  if (row.count <= 0) continue;
  await fetch(`${getApiHost()}/apis/v3/subcon/attendance`, { method: "POST", ... });   // no res.ok
}
alert(`Subcontractor crew attendance saved for ${selectedSubcon.name}!`);
```
  A loop of unchecked POSTs followed by an unconditional success alert. If row 3 of 8 is rejected,
  the user is told the whole crew's attendance was saved. This is **the same data class as R2-014**
  (the CRITICAL offline-queue defect) and it feeds subcontractor billing and labour cost. Present in
  both the company and project copies of the page.
- **Suggested fix:** one shared `mutate()` helper that throws on non-2xx, with a single error
  surface. The pattern already exists and is correct in two files —
  `d/payroll-attendance/page.tsx:94-121` (`jget`/`jpost`/`jput`/`jdel`, each
  `if (!r.ok) throw new Error(await r.text())`) and `d/crm/page.tsx:100`. It is simply not used
  anywhere else. **Adopt those helpers console-wide rather than patching 16 call sites.**

### FINDING R2-056 — the correct helper throws, but callers have no catch, so failures are silent
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Where:** `d/payroll-attendance/page.tsx:960-980`
```js
const createDesignation = async (name) => { await jpost(`/hr/designations/${companyId}`, { name }); reload(); toast("Designation added"); };
const createLeaveTemplate = async (name) => { await jpost(`/hr/leave-templates/${companyId}`, { name }); reload(); toast("Leave template added"); };
```
- **Evidence:** `jpost` correctly throws on non-2xx, but neither caller has a `try/catch` and neither
  is awaited by a handler that catches. On failure the promise rejects unhandled: no toast, no error,
  nothing visible happens. Better than a false success — the toast is correctly skipped — but from
  the user's point of view it is a dead button. `saveBreakup` at `:970` has the same gap.
- **Contrast:** `openDrawer` at `:946` does it correctly with `try/catch/finally`.
- **Suggested fix:** wrap in `try/catch` and surface the thrown message.

### FINDING R2-057 — Gantt predecessor failures are all reported as "Link loop detected"
- **Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM — misleading error attribution
- **Where:** `d/planning/gantt/page.tsx:352-359`
```js
if (res.ok) { setSuccess("Task link recorded successfully!"); ... }
else { setError("Link loop detected. Predecessor rejected."); }
```
- **Evidence:** the response *is* checked (good), but every non-2xx is reported as a dependency
  cycle. A 401 (expired session), 403 (no `planning:edit` permission), 404 (task deleted in another
  tab) or 500 all tell the user their schedule contains a loop that does not exist.
- **Suggested fix:** read `res.status` and the server's `detail`; reserve the loop message for the
  400 the backend actually raises for a cycle (`planning.py:565`).

## 🎭 FABRICATED / FALLBACK DATA — second sweep (console TSX)

Round 2 found five instances (R2-008, R2-009, R2-017, R2-019, R2-020) by browsing. This is the
systematic source sweep of the same class, and it found a further seven, four of them in pages
Round 2 recorded as **"renders clean"** — because the fabricated content only appears on an error
path or an empty result, which an audit of a populated, working environment never triggers.

### FINDING R2-058 — 🔴 "Create Demo Request" authenticates with hardcoded OTP credentials from the production console
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — supersedes and escalates R2-024, which described the demo credentials as
  inert strings in the bundle. They are not inert: a production page **calls the auth endpoint with
  them**.
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/payment-approval/page.tsx:121-158`
  (`handleCreateDemoRequest`), bound to a "Create Demo Request" button on the Payment Approval page
- **The code:**
```js
const userRes = await fetch(`${apiHost}/apis/v3/auth/otp/verify`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ mobile: "+919876543210", code: "123456" })   // mock verify to get user
});
let userId = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000";
if (userRes.ok) { const uData = await userRes.json(); userId = uData.user.id; }
```
  followed by a POST creating a payment request of **₹45,000** with the invented narrative
  `"Steel structures delivery invoice ST-1092"` (`:142-148`).
- **Three distinct defects:**
  1. **An authenticated console page performs an unauthenticated OTP verification** against the demo
     number. Note the request deliberately carries **no `Authorization` header** — it is a real login
     attempt, not a data fetch. If `OTP_DEMO_ALLOWLIST`/`OTP_DEMO_CODE` are set on Render (**this is
     exactly what decision D6 asks**), this returns a genuine session for the demo account and the
     resulting `user.id` is attached to a financial record in the founder's real company.
  2. **The failure path writes a null-UUID foreign key.** When the OTP call fails, `userId` stays
     `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` and the payment request is created with that as
     `party_company_user_id`. Combined with **R2-052** (that column is a non-null FK to `users.id`)
     this is a foreign-key violation — a 500, or a corrupt row if the constraint is not enforced.
  3. **Fabricated financial data in the founder's real books.** A ₹45,000 payment request with an
     invented invoice narrative enters the live approval queue. Neither POST surfaces an error:
     both use `if (res.ok) { ... }` with no `else`.
- **Impact:** this is the R2-024 concern made concrete, plus a fabricated-data injection path, plus
  a null-FK write, on the page that governs payment approvals.
- **Suggested fix:** **delete `handleCreateDemoRequest` and its button entirely.** Round 2 already
  recommended removing this button under R2-024; that recommendation now has a second, independent
  reason. Answer D6 regardless, since the demo OTP path's production status affects more than this
  page.

### FINDING R2-059 — Payment approve / reject / mark-paid fails silently
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — the most permission-sensitive action in the product gives no feedback when
  the server refuses it
- **Where:** `d/payment-approval/page.tsx:101-119` (`handleUpdateStatus`)
```js
const res = await fetch(`${apiHost}/apis/v3/finance/payment-requests/approve/${requestId}`, {
  method: "PUT", ..., body: JSON.stringify({ status: action })
});
if (res.ok) {
  setToastMessage(`Payment request ${action.toLowerCase()} successfully!`);
  fetchData();
}
// no else
} catch (err) { console.error(err); }
```
- **Evidence:** `if (res.ok)` with **no `else`**, and the catch only logs. A 403 (user lacks
  `billing:approve`), a 400 from the approval-rule gate (`finance.py:1149` explicitly rejects
  recording payment before all levels sign off), or a 500 all produce **absolutely nothing** — no
  toast, no error, no state change. The button appears dead.
- **Why this matters beyond UX:** this is precisely the failure mode the Round 2 handoff flagged
  under R2-027 — *"any module using `if (res.ok) {...}` with no `else` looks identical to an empty
  module"*. Here it means an approver cannot distinguish "I am not authorized" from "the click did
  not register", on a financial approval.
- **Suggested fix:** add an `else` that reads the server's `detail` and shows it. The backend already
  returns useful messages for both refusal cases.

### FINDING R2-060 — 🔴 Attendance fabricates a GPS location when geolocation is denied or times out
- **Severity:** **HIGH** — invented location evidence, stored indistinguishably from a real fix, on a
  feature whose entire value proposition is location verification
- **Where — both copies:** `d/attendance/page.tsx:398-416` and
  `p/[project_id]/attendance/page.tsx:394-412` (`captureLocation`)
```js
const captureLocation = async () => {
  const fallback = { lat: "12.9716", lng: "77.5946", label: "Metro Geofence Yard" };
  if (typeof navigator === "undefined" || !navigator.geolocation) return fallback;
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(
      (position) => resolve({ lat: ..., lng: ..., label: isGpsSimulatedVerified ? "GPS coordinates verified" : "GPS coordinates (Off-site warning)" }),
      () => resolve(fallback),                       // <- permission denied, position unavailable, or timeout
      { enableHighAccuracy: true, timeout: 5000 }
    );
  });
};
```
- **What the fallback actually is:** `12.9716, 77.5946` is **Bangalore city centre**, labelled
  **"Metro Geofence Yard"** — a site name that does not exist in any customer's data.
- **When it fires:** the error callback catches *permission denied*, *position unavailable* **and**
  *timeout*. A 5-second high-accuracy timeout on a phone indoors or on a basement site is routine.
  The user is never told; the punch proceeds.
- **Impact:** the punch is recorded with plausible coordinates and a confident site label. Downstream
  nothing can distinguish it from a genuine fix, so the geofence audit trail silently contains
  fabricated positions. The marketing site sells GPS-geofenced attendance; the "Off-site warning"
  label on the *success* path shows the product does treat location as evidence.
- **Compounding:** R2-014 destroys queued offline punches and R2-055 does not check the subcontractor
  attendance POST. All three are in the same two files and all three degrade attendance silently.
- **Suggested fix:** on geolocation failure, either block the punch with an explicit message, or
  record it with `location: null` and a `location_source: "unavailable"` flag that the UI and reports
  display. **Never substitute coordinates.** Remove the hardcoded pair either way.

### FINDING R2-061 — Equipment page renders an invented fleet whenever a fetch fails
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (disclosed, but fabricated operational and cost data)
- **Where — both copies:** `d/equipment/page.tsx:131-146`, `p/[project_id]/equipment/page.tsx:129-144`
- **Evidence:** the `catch` sets `setError("Using demo data — backend connection unavailable")` and
  then populates three fabricated machines — `JCB Excavator 3DX` (`JCB-001`, ₹1,500/hr),
  `Concrete Mixer 10/7` (₹600/hr), `Crawler Crane Demag` (₹4,500/hr) — plus two deployments with
  invented meter readings ("Start reading: 435. Photo Proof: true") and a fuel log
  (45 L @ ₹92 = ₹4,140).
- **Better than R2-008 in one respect:** it *is* disclosed via the banner. Still fabricated fleet,
  hour rates, meter readings and fuel spend rendered inside the authenticated console, and the
  "Photo Proof: true" strings assert evidence that does not exist.
- **Note for Round 2's record:** Equipment was listed as "renders clean" in the Phase 10 sweep. It
  renders clean *when the API responds*. The fabricated branch is unreachable in a healthy
  environment, which is why page-load screening missed it — see the honest caveat in the Round 2
  coverage note.
- **Secondary:** the category `<select>` (`:827-830`) offers `Excavator / Concrete Mixer / Tower
  Crane / Generator` while the fallback rows use `Excavator / Mixer / Crane` — the two vocabularies
  disagree. `category` has no backend pattern so this does not 422, but it does break category
  filtering and grouping.
- **Suggested fix:** delete the fallback block and render the existing error state with a retry.

### FINDING R2-062 — Company dashboard invents an employee and two materials when the company has none
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — undisclosed fabricated data, including a salary figure, on the sidebar's
  "Dashboard"
- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/dashboard/page.tsx:321-338`
```js
const fallbackWorkforceEmployees = [{ id: "demo-employee-1", name: "Sample Crew Lead",
  designation: "Monthly", department: "Labour", employee_code: "EMP-001",
  basic_salary: 18000, hra: 2000, other_allowances: 500 }];
const fallbackMaterials = [{ id: "demo-material-1", name: "Cement", ... },
                           { id: "demo-material-2", name: "Sand", ... }];
const workforceSource  = workforceEmployees.length ? workforceEmployees : fallbackWorkforceEmployees;
const materialSource   = materialLibraries.length  ? materialLibraries  : fallbackMaterials;
```
- **The trigger is an *empty* result, not an error** — so **every new company sees this on day one**,
  and unlike R2-061 there is **no banner or disclosure of any kind**. A brand-new tenant is shown a
  crew lead on ₹18,000 basic + ₹2,000 HRA and a materials library containing Cement and Sand.
- **Same page as R2-017** (4 fabricated projects hiding the real one) and, per **R2-047**, this is
  the *only* dashboard reachable from the sidebar. Fix all three together.
- **Suggested fix:** render an honest empty state with a call to action ("Add your first employee").
  Nineteen other modules already do this correctly.

### FINDING R2-063 — Quality module writes a hardcoded remark and mislabels unresolved checklists
- **Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH — fabricated text persisted into quality audit records
- **Where — both copies:** `d/quality/page.tsx` and `p/[project_id]/quality/page.tsx`
- **Three separate defects:**
  1. **A hardcoded remark is saved against every checklist response** (`d:427`, `p:425`):
```js
const responses = Object.entries(inspectionResponses).map(([itemId, result]) => ({
  checklist_item_id: itemId,
  result,
  remarks: "Checked on site"          // <- not user input; written to every single response
}));
```
     There is no remarks field in the audit UI. Every inspection item in the database therefore
     carries the literal string **"Checked on site"** as if an inspector had typed it. On a quality
     record — which exists to evidence what was actually verified — this is fabricated evidence, and
     it will appear in any inspection export or dispute.
  2. **Unresolvable checklists are labelled with a real IS code** (`d:225`, `p:223`):
```js
checklist: foundCl ? foundCl.title : "IS 456 Concrete Pre-Pour",
```
     An inspection whose `checklist_id` does not match any loaded checklist is displayed as
     **"IS 456 Concrete Pre-Pour"** — a specific Indian Standard for concrete pre-pour. A steel or
     waterproofing inspection with a stale checklist reference is shown under a concrete standard.
     The correct fallback is the raw id or "Unknown checklist".
  3. **Dead fabricated const.** `CHECKLISTS` (`d:74-95`) defines two full IS-code checklists
     (`CL-01` IS 456:2000, `CL-02` IS 1786:2008) under a `// ─── Mock Data ───` header. It has
     **zero references** — the page loads real checklists from
     `/apis/v3/quality/checklists/{companyId}` at `:181`. Harmless today, but it is the source of
     the string in defect (2) and is exactly the kind of leftover that gets re-wired later.
- **Note for Round 2's record:** Quality was listed as clean in the Phase 10 sweep. Defect (1) is
  invisible from the UI — nothing is displayed, the string only reaches the database.
- **Suggested fix:** add a real remarks input (or send `null`), fix the fallback label, delete the
  dead const.

### FINDING R2-064 — BOQ import claims it is "using demo data" when it loads none
- **Severity:** LOW — misleading error message
- **Where:** `d/budgeting/boq/page.tsx:142-144`
```js
} catch {
  setImportMsg("Backend not reachable. — using demo data.");
}
```
- **Evidence:** nothing follows the message — no demo rows are set, no state changes. The user is
  told the page fell back to demo data when in fact the import simply failed and the BOQ is
  unchanged. (The stray `. — ` is a leftover from a removed sentence.)
- **Contrast:** the success path here is correct — it checks `res.ok && data.success` and surfaces
  `data.detail` on failure (`:135-140`). Only the network-error branch is wrong. Note the
  **project-level** BOQ import at `p/[project_id]/boq/page.tsx:250` does **not** check the response
  at all (R2-055), so the product's two BOQ import paths fail in two different ways.
- **Suggested fix:** say the import failed and the BOQ was not modified.

### FINDING R2-065 — Dead duplicate payroll calculator in the HR page
- **Severity:** LOW (dead code) — but worth deleting before someone wires it up
- **Where:** `d/hr/page.tsx:99-125`, `computePayslips`, under a `// ─── Mock Data ───` header
- **Evidence:** **zero call sites.** The page's payslips come from the server at `:592`
  (`data.payslips.map(...)`), which is correct. The function is a complete second implementation of
  pro-rated gross, basic, PF (capped at ₹1,800), ESI (0.75% employee / 3.25% employer), TDS and net.
- **Why it is worth flagging rather than ignoring:** it embeds the same assumption D2 is about —
  `const days = daysPresent[emp.id] ?? daysInMonth;` — **absent attendance silently means a full
  month**, identical to the server behaviour in **R2-033**. If this ever gets wired up it
  reintroduces that decision client-side, where it cannot be flagged. It is also the R2-010 pattern
  (calculators duplicated front and back with no contract test) applied to payroll.
- **Suggested fix:** delete it. If a client-side preview is wanted later, call the API.

## 🧪 DISCRIMINATOR / ALLOWLIST FIELDS — remaining patterns enumerated (R2-011 class)

R2-011 established the rule: **grepping literal assignments does not verify a constrained field —
every option list, const array and default that feeds it must be enumerated.** Round 2 re-verified 5
fields that way. This is the remaining set: all 21 `pattern=` constraints in the backend.

| Field | File | Pattern | Every frontend feed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deduction_type` | `billing.py:70` | TDS/Retention/Security Deposit/Advance Recovery/Material Recovery | `<select>`, 5 exact values | ✅ verified Round 2 |
| `party_type` | `library.py:24` | Client/Supplier/… | 9-option `<select>` | ❌ **R2-011 — 6 of 9 fail** |
| `payment_type` | `finance.py:30` | in/out/transfer | ternary → in/out | ✅ verified Round 2 |
| `payment_method` | `finance.py:32` | Cash/Bank Transfer/… | hardcoded `"Cash"` | ✅ verified Round 2 |
| `opening_balance_type` | `library.py:49` | pay/receive | defaults + toggles | ✅ verified Round 2 |
| `opening_balance_direction` | `library.py:42` | will_pay/will_receive | defaults + 2 selects | ✅ verified Round 2 |
| `category` (drawings) | `drawings.py:60` | 2D Layout/3D Layout/Production File | **none** (orphaned) | ✅ no risk — see R2-006 |
| `ownership_type` | `equipment.py:27` | `^(Owned\|Hired)$` | `<select>` at `equipment/page.tsx:835-837` → exactly `Owned`, `Hired` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `punch_type` | `hr.py:114` | `^(in\|out)$` | `mode.toLowerCase()` where `mode: "IN" \| "OUT"` (`attendance/page.tsx:456`, typed at `:418`) | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `approval_status` (drawings) | `drawings.py:70` | `^(approved\|rejected)$` | `newStatus === "locked" ? "approved" : "rejected"` (`drawings/page.tsx:298`) | ✅ **SAFE** — binary by construction |
| `result` (quality) | `quality.py:108` | `^(Pass\|Fail\|NA)$` | TS union `"Pass" \| "Fail" \| "NA"` (`quality/page.tsx:29`) | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `severity` (NCR) | `quality.py:123` | `^(Minor\|Major\|Critical)$` | TS union + default `"Major"` (`:154`, `:347`), select at `:997` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `status` (equipment maint.) | `equipment.py:92` | scheduled/completed/overdue | no frontend feed found | ✅ no risk |
| `status` (production) | `production.py:115` | draft/running/completed/cancelled | no frontend feed found | ✅ no risk |
| `payroll_month` | `hr.py:196` | `^\d{4}-\d{2}$` | `<input type="month">` → always `YYYY-MM` | ✅ **SAFE** |
| `grade`, `type` | `calculators.py:88, 370` | M5…M45 / pct_* | **none** — the console never calls these endpoints | ✅ no risk — see R2-010 |
| `fmt` ×3, `file_type` | `bi_export.py`, `google_drive.py` | csv/json, project/company | query params with matching defaults | ✅ **SAFE** |

**Conclusion: `party_type` (R2-011) remains the only broken pattern.** All 21 are now accounted for
by feed enumeration rather than by grepping assignments, closing the "remaining risk" caveat Round 2
left open at the end of R2-011.

**One inconsistency found while doing this, not a 422:** the equipment `category` field has no
backend pattern, and the two vocabularies in the frontend disagree — see R2-061.
