- **Fix:** require `membership.role == "admin"` on all three; constrain `role` with a `Literal` /
  `pattern=`; refuse to remove or demote the last admin.

### FINDING R2-143 — 🟠 HIGH: creating a chat group writes an FK-invalid member row from a client-supplied `created_by`, and the group row is committed first

- **Where:** `chat.py:110-122` (`create_group`), called from `d/chat/page.tsx:154-171`.
- The client sends `created_by: localStorage.getItem("user_id")` — proved above to be a **`users.id`**.
  The server does `db.add(group); db.commit()` and *then*, in a second transaction, inserts
  `ChatGroupMember(user_id=payload.created_by, role="admin")` into a column that is
  `ForeignKey("company_team.id")`. Unless that `users.id` coincidentally exists as a `company_team.id`,
  Postgres raises a foreign-key violation and the request 500s **after the group row is already
  committed** — leaving an orphan group with no members that, per R2-140, nobody can ever open.
- `payload.created_by` is `Optional` and **never validated against `current_user`**: a caller may
  name any UUID as the group admin, and if it is omitted entirely the group is created with **zero
  members**, permanently unusable.
- The frontend's fallback when `localStorage.user_id` is missing is the hardcoded literal
  `"e0000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"` (`page.tsx:151`, also `:40` for `companyId`) — a fabricated
  UUID sent to the server as an identity.
- **Status:** the 500 is predicted from the schema, not yet exercised — creating a group is a write to
  the founder's live company. **Pending consent.** The FK definition and the ID-space proof are
  certain; only the exact status code is not.
- **Fix:** ignore `created_by` from the payload entirely; derive the creator's `CompanyTeam` row
  server-side and insert it as the admin member **in the same transaction** as the group.

### FINDING R2-144 — 🟡 MEDIUM: voice notes and media attachments exist in the model, the schema and the read path, and cannot be produced by any UI control

- `ChatMessage` stores `media_url` and `voice_note_url` (`models.py:1646-1647`); both are accepted by
  `ChatMessageCreate` and returned by `ChatMessageResponse` (`chat.py:52-53`, `:64-65`); the message
  renderer only ever reads `msg.image_urls` (`d/chat/page.tsx:494-499`).
- The only attachment control in the composer is a text input labelled **"Image URL (optional)"**
  (`page.tsx:551`) whose value is split on commas and posted as `image_urls` (`page.tsx:226`). There
  is no file picker and no upload anywhere in the page.
- **Consequence:** a site chat for a construction product cannot attach a site photo taken on a
  phone; the user must already have a public URL. Same root cause as R2-068 (photo evidence stores a
  hardcoded stock URL) — there is no upload pipeline behind any of these controls.

### FINDING R2-145 — 🟡 MEDIUM: adding someone to a chat group requires typing their raw UUID

- `d/chat/page.tsx:810-820`: the Add Member form's only identity field is a free-text input for
  `user_id`, with the placeholder `e.g. e0000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`.
- The company team list is already available to the console (Settings → Team renders it), so the data
  for a picker exists. As shipped, the feature is unusable by its intended user, and a typo produces
  either a 500 (FK violation, see R2-143) or a silent no-op (`if (res.ok)` with no `else`,
  `page.tsx:189`).

### FINDING R2-146 — 🟡 MEDIUM: the company-level Chat route is a project chat that silently shows nothing when no project is active

- `d/chat/page.tsx:47-48` takes `projectId` from `useProject().activeProjectId`, and `fetchGroups`
  only runs `if (projectId)` (`page.tsx:120-124`). `GET /chat/groups/{project_id}` is the only list
  endpoint and is project-scoped by definition (`chat.py:124-127`).
- **Consequence:** with no active project the page issues **no request at all** and renders
  "No chats found." — identical to a project that genuinely has no groups. There is no company-wide
  chat despite the `/c/{cid}/d/chat` route, and no message telling the user to pick a project.
- Live: with a project active, the endpoint returned `200 []`, so the empty state was honest in this
  instance. The failure mode is the no-project case, and the absence of any distinction between
  "nothing here", "no project selected" and "the request failed".

### FINDING R2-147 — 🟡 MEDIUM: the message poll refetches the whole thread every 4 seconds and the group list never refreshes

- `d/chat/page.tsx:134-137`: `setInterval(() => fetchMessages(activeGroup.id), 4000)` pulls the
  **entire** message history each tick (`GET /chat/messages/{group_id}` has no `since`/pagination —
  `chat.py:159-181` returns every row ordered ascending). A long-lived site group grows this payload
  without bound, and each tick costs a DB connection — the same pool that R2-138 showed is only 30
  wide.
- The group list is fetched only on mount and after a mutation, so a group someone else creates never
  appears, and `member_count` is computed with a **per-group `COUNT(*)` in a Python loop**
  (`chat.py:128-133`) — N+1 on every group-list load.
- **Fix:** poll with an `after_id`/`since` cursor, cap the initial load, and compute `member_count`
  with a single `GROUP BY`.

## Company To-Do (`/c/{cid}/d/todo`)

Live: the page renders, `GET /apis/v3/todos/company/{cid}` succeeds, the company has no to-dos, and
the empty state is honest ("No tasks found. Click '+ New To Do' to add one."). It is also the
**first page in this audit with a real error branch** — `fetchTodos` throws on `!res.ok` and renders
"Could not load tasks from the server." (`d/todo/page.tsx:77`, `:210-213`). That is the R2-137 fix
pattern, already written, in a third file. The findings below are about what happens *after* the list
loads.

**The decisive comparison:** the project-scoped twin at `p/{pid}/todo/page.tsx` implements the same
screen **correctly** — it `PUT`s the status (`:64`), `DELETE`s (`:73`) and sends `repeat_type`
(`:177`). The company-level page does none of the three. Every finding below is a divergence from a
working sibling in the same repository, not a missing capability.

### FINDING R2-148 — 🔴 CRITICAL: on the company To-Do list, "complete" and "delete" only change React state; the server is never told

- **Where:** `frontend/src/app/c/[company_id]/d/todo/page.tsx:145-153`.
  ```
  const handleToggleTodo = (id: string) => { setTodos(prev => prev.map(...)); };
  const handleDeleteTodo = (id: string) => { setTodos(prev => prev.filter(t => t.id !== id)); };
  ```
  Neither function contains a `fetch`. They are wired to the row checkbox (`:294`) and the row's
  delete button (`:313`).
- **The endpoints exist and work:** `PUT /apis/v3/todos/{todo_id}` accepts `status`
  (`backend/app/routers/todos.py:133,152-153`) and `DELETE /apis/v3/todos/{todo_id}` deletes and
  writes a delete-log entry (`todos.py:163-180`). The project-level page calls both.
- **Consequence:** ticking a task off makes it vanish from the Pending filter and appear under
  Completed; deleting removes the row. **Both survive only until the next fetch.** Any navigation,
  refresh or the `useEffect` re-run on `[companyId, accessToken, projectMap, teamMap]` (`:139-142`)
  restores every "completed" and "deleted" item to pending. Nothing is written, and there is no
  error — the operation genuinely succeeded, locally.
- **Severity rationale:** this is worse than a dead button. A dead button teaches the user it is
  dead. This one gives positive confirmation, so a site supervisor closing out the day's checklist
  believes the work is recorded, and no other user ever sees it. It is the same failure shape as
  R2-105 (offline punch sync reporting success) and R2-090 (approvals showing success on 403).
- **Fix:** copy the two handlers from `p/[project_id]/todo/page.tsx:60-75` verbatim.

### FINDING R2-149 — 🟠 HIGH: the entire "Repeat Settings" modal is decorative — the value is never sent, and nothing in the backend ever expands a recurrence

- **Where:** `d/todo/page.tsx:402-540`. The modal offers Weekdays / Everyday / Monthdays radio
  buttons (`:443-460`), a weekday multi-select (`:462-480`), and an "Ends" date (`:517`). All of it
  writes to local state (`repeatType`, `selectedWeekdays`, `endsDate`). Both the Cancel button
  (`:529`) and the confirm button (`:536`) do exactly one thing: `setIsRepeatModalOpen(false)`.
- The create payload (`:158-166`) contains `company_id`, `title`, `due_date`, `type`,
  `assignee_ids` and optionally `project_id`. **There is no `repeat_type` key.** The server
  therefore stores the model default `"none"` (`models.py:2102`) on every to-do created here, while
  the closed modal keeps displaying "Every W" / "Daily task" (`:407`).
- The project-level page **does** send it (`p/[project_id]/todo/page.tsx:177`), so the field is
  reachable — just not from this screen.
- **Deeper problem, which affects both pages:** a repo-wide grep for `repeat_type` outside
  `routers/todos.py` returns exactly one hit — the column definition at `models.py:2102`. There is
  **no scheduler, no cron, no job and no read-time expansion** anywhere that turns a `repeat_type`
  into a second occurrence. Even where the value is stored correctly, a "daily" to-do is a single
  row with a label. The recurrence feature does not exist on either side; one page hides that fact
  better than the other.
- **Also:** `endsDate` is initialised to the hardcoded literal `"2026-12-05"` (`:55`) rather than
  derived from today, so the modal opens showing a fixed date that will silently become a past date.
- **Fix:** either send `repeat_type` and build the expansion job, or remove the modal. Shipping a
  configuration UI for a feature with no runtime is worse than not shipping the feature.

### FINDING R2-150 — 🟡 MEDIUM: `created_by` on a to-do is whatever the client says, and this client says nothing

- `TodoCreate.created_by` is accepted from the request body and written straight through
  (`todos.py:115`), while the authenticated `current_user` — already resolved on the same line as the
  dependency — is used only for the permission check.
- The company To-Do page never sends the field, so every to-do created from this screen has
  `created_by = NULL`. There is no "raised by" column in the UI and no way to reconstruct one.
- Same shape as R2-143 (`chat.create_group`) and the R2-132/134 three-way findings: the server
  accepts an identity from the caller instead of deriving it from the token. Worth fixing as one
  sweep — the caller-supplied-identity pattern now has three confirmed instances.

### DISPROVED — do not re-derive
- **"To-Do assignees use the wrong ID space like chat does."** They do not. `todo_assignees.assignee_id`
  is `ForeignKey("company_team.id")` (`models.py:2114`) and the picker is fed by
  `GET /apis/v3/crm/team-members/{company_id}`, which returns `TeamMemberResponse(id=t.id, …)` where
  `t` is a `CompanyTeam` row (`crm.py:371-381`). The spaces match. R2-140 is specific to chat.
- **"The company To-Do page swallows load failures like the rest of the console."** It does not —
  see the error banner above. It is one of the three files that get this right.

## Budget & Committed Costs (`/c/{cid}/d/budget`)

**Screen vs API, run live this session** — the rendered page and `GET /apis/v3/budget/committed/{pid}`
agree digit for digit:

| Screen | API field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| TOTAL BUDGET ₹0 | `total_budget` | 0 |
| TOTAL COMMITTED ₹198,380 | `total_committed` | 198380 |
| TOTAL ACTUAL ₹23,600 | `total_actual` | 23600 |
| Material committed ₹48,380 / actual ₹23,600 | `material_committed` / `material_actual` | 48380 / 23600 |
| Subcontractor committed ₹150,000 / actual ₹0 | `subcon_committed` / `subcon_actual` | 150000 / 0 |

**The page is an honest renderer.** Unlike Finance (R2-099) there is no client-side distortion here.
Every finding below is in the server's arithmetic, and the UI's fault is only that it presents
hardcoded constants in the same typeface as measured values.

### FINDING R2-151 — 🟠 HIGH: Labour and Equipment committed *and* actual are hardcoded `0.0`, and the UI renders them as measured ₹0 rows

- **Where:** `backend/app/routers/budget.py:93-97`.
  ```
  labour_committed = 0.0
  labour_actual = 0.0
  equipment_committed = 0.0
  equipment_actual = 0.0
  ```
  Four of the eight numbers the module exists to produce are literals. They flow into
  `total_committed` and `total_actual` (`budget.py:104-106`) and into the response unchanged.
- **What the UI does with them:** `d/budget/page.tsx` renders a four-row table with Labour and
  Equipment rows showing ₹0 budget, ₹0 committed, ₹0 actual, ₹0 variance, 0.0% utilization —
  visually identical to a project that genuinely has no labour or plant cost. Confirmed live on the
  screen text above.
- **Why it is wrong rather than merely incomplete:** the company has a finalized payroll run for
  2026-07 (seeded in Round 2 and still present) and the product ships an Equipment module with its
  own expense reporting. The data exists; this endpoint declines to query it. A cost controller
  reading this screen concludes labour spend is zero.
- **Fix:** compute `labour_actual` from finalized payroll runs scoped to the project (the same source
  `safety.py` uses for attendance) and `equipment_*` from equipment expenses; until then, return
  `null` and render "not tracked", never `0`. This is the same remedy pattern as D2 — see
  `safety.py`'s `manhours_source` flag, which is the reference implementation already in the repo.

### FINDING R2-152 — 🟠 HIGH: `GET /budget/committed/{project_id}` writes to the database and commits

- **Where:** `budget.py:66-74`. If no `ProjectBudget` row exists for the project, the **GET handler**
  constructs one, `db.add`s it and `db.commit()`s before continuing.
- **Consequences:**
  1. A read endpoint is non-idempotent and has a side effect, so it cannot be cached, retried safely,
     or served from a read replica.
  2. There is no permission check on the write — the route's only guard is `verify_project_access`
     (`budget.py:65`), while the endpoint that legitimately writes the same table,
     `POST /budgeting/allocation`, requires `budgeting:edit` (`budgeting.py:222`). **Anyone who can
     view a project silently creates its budget row**, bypassing the permission that governs that table.
  3. Two concurrent first-views race to insert the same `project_id`; whether that ends in a duplicate
     row or an `IntegrityError` 500 depends on a unique constraint that the model does not declare.
  4. Every first view costs a write transaction on the 30-connection pool that R2-138 showed is the
     platform's scarcest resource.
- **Fix:** treat a missing row as zeros in memory and return them. Do not persist on read.

### FINDING R2-153 — 🟠 HIGH: the budget's "actual" ignores two of the four expense invoice types, including the one named `equipment`

- `budget.py:14` imports `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES` from `app.constants` — and **never uses it**. The
  handler instead hardcodes two string literals: `Bill.invoice_type == "purchase"` for material
  (`:79-81`) and `Bill.invoice_type == "subcon"` for subcontractor (`:86-88`).
- `constants.py:14` defines `EXPENSE_INVOICE_TYPES = ("purchase", "subcon", "expense", "equipment")`.
  **`expense` and `equipment` bills are therefore counted in no category at all** — they are not
  material, not subcon, and the equipment bucket is the hardcoded `0.0` of R2-151. A bill of either
  type raises the company's real spend and moves nothing on this screen.
- Live evidence that the plumbing is otherwise right: the project's three bills are
  `purchase 23,600` and `sale 118,000`; the sale is correctly excluded and material actual is exactly
  23,600. The defect is latent in this dataset **because no `expense` or `equipment` bill exists yet**
  — it will surface silently the first time one is raised.
- This is the same unenumerated-`invoice_type` family as R2-011 and the Remediation Gap Map: the
  constant that would have prevented it is imported at the top of the very file that gets it wrong.
- **Fix:** bucket by the constant, and add a fallthrough so any `invoice_type` not mapped to a
  category is surfaced rather than dropped.

### FINDING R2-154 — 🟡 MEDIUM: committed cost counts every purchase order and work order regardless of state, and the variance display has no "budget not set" case

- **Committed:** `material_committed` sums all POs except `status in ("closed",)` (`budget.py:76-77`),
  so **draft, cancelled and rejected POs are committed cost**. `subcon_committed` sums
  `estimated_work_amount` over **every** work order with no status filter at all (`budget.py:83-84`).
  A cancelled ₹150,000 work order still reads as ₹150,000 committed.
- **Presentation:** with no budget allocated, `total_budget` is 0, so the page displays
  **COMMITTED VARIANCE ₹-198,380** and a red-negative variance on every row — which reads as a
  ₹198,380 overrun rather than "no budget has been set". Utilization is `0.0%` for Material despite
  ₹23,600 of actual spend, because `pct()` divides by a zero budget (`d/budget/page.tsx:91`).
  Nothing on the screen says "Set a budget to see variance", even though the `Set Budget` button is
  right there.
- **Fix:** filter committed by an enumerated live-status set; when `total_budget == 0`, suppress
  variance and utilization and show a set-budget prompt instead of a fabricated overrun.

### Verified good — do not re-audit
- `POST /apis/v3/budgeting/allocation` (`budgeting.py:212-236`) is correct: it resolves the project,
  checks company membership **and** `budgeting:edit`, upserts the single `ProjectBudget` row, and
  returns it. The Set Budget modal handles both branches, showing the server's `detail` on failure
  (`d/budget/page.tsx:78-86`) — one of the few `else` branches in the console (cf. R2-137).
- `d/budgeting/` contains only a `boq/` subdirectory, not a second budget page. There is no duplicate
  module; the two directory names are not a fork.

## Custom Fields (`/c/{cid}/d/custom-fields`)

The engine underneath is real: `upsert_values_for_entity` (`custom_fields.py:106-186`) normalises a
raw value into `value_text` / `value_number` / `value_date` / `value_json` according to the field's
declared `field_type`, and it is invoked from project creation (`projects.py:185`) and bill creation
(`billing.py:657`). The findings below are about the admin screen that manages it and about the two
endpoints that screen calls directly.

### FINDING R2-155 — 🟠 HIGH: the "Set Value" screen is write-only — values are posted, fetched, and thrown away without ever being rendered

- **Where:** `d/custom-fields/page.tsx:59-63`.
  ```
  const fetchValues = async () => {
    if (!selectedField) return;
    try {
      await fetch(`${getApiHost()}/apis/v3/custom-fields/values/${selectedField.entity_type}/${projectId}`, ...);
    } catch (e) { console.error("Failed to load values", e); }
  };
  ```
  The response is awaited and discarded — no `.json()`, no `setState`. There is no `values` state in
  the component and nothing in the JSX renders a stored value. `fetchValues` is nevertheless called
  on mount of a selection and after every successful save (`:75-78`, `:122`), so the request is real
  and its result is real; only the display is missing.
- **Consequence:** after "Value saved" appears, the screen shows exactly what it showed before. The
  user cannot confirm what was stored, cannot see the previous value they are overwriting, and cannot
  tell a successful save from a save onto the wrong entity. `set_value` is an **upsert**
  (`custom_fields.py:211-228`) — it silently replaces an existing value — so the one piece of
  information the user most needs before typing is the one the page refuses to fetch into view.
- **Fix:** parse the response into state and render it in the field list; the endpoint already
  returns everything needed.

### FINDING R2-156 — 🟠 HIGH: the field builder offers six entity types; only three surfaces in the product read custom fields, so four of the six are unfillable

- The create-field form's Entity Type select offers **project, task, bill, invoice, lead, vendor**
  (`d/custom-fields/page.tsx:192-199`).
- A repo-wide search for the component that renders custom fields on an entity — `CustomFieldsSection`
  — returns exactly three call sites: project create and project edit
  (`c/[company_id]/projects/page.tsx:708`, `:962`) and the project transaction/bill screen
  (`p/[project_id]/transaction/page.tsx:744`). On the server, `custom_fields` is accepted by exactly
  two payloads: `projects.py:185` and `billing.py:102`.
- **Consequence:** a field defined for **task, invoice, lead or vendor** appears in the admin list,
  can be marked *required*, and can never be filled in by anyone through normal use of the product,
  because no task, lead or vendor screen renders it. "Required" is not enforced anywhere either — no
  create path validates that required custom fields are present.
- **Compounding it:** the admin page's own list is hardcoded to `?entity_type=project`
  (`page.tsx:53`) while the create form defaults to `project` but lets the user pick another type.
  Create a `vendor` field and it vanishes from the list on the next fetch — the create succeeded, the
  screen shows nothing, and the only signal is the transient "Field created" toast.
- **Fix:** restrict the select to the entity types that are actually wired (project, bill), or wire
  the rest; and make the list's `entity_type` follow a filter the user controls, as
  `settings/page.tsx:437` already does with its `cfEntity` variable.

### FINDING R2-157 — 🔴 CRITICAL: `POST /custom-fields/values` never checks that the target entity belongs to the company being authorised against

- **Where:** `custom_fields.py:209-233`.
  ```
  def set_value(payload: CustomFieldValueCreate, ...):
      require_permission(db, current_user, payload.company_id, "settings:manage")
      existing = db.query(CustomFieldValue).filter(field_id, entity_type, entity_id).first()
      ...
      value = CustomFieldValue(**data); db.add(value); db.commit()
  ```
  The only authorisation is `require_permission` against **`payload.company_id`** — a value chosen by
  the caller. Nothing verifies that `entity_id` (an arbitrary UUID, typed by hand into a free-text
  "Entity ID" box at `page.tsx:240`) belongs to that company, and nothing verifies that `field_id`
  belongs to it either.
- **Consequences:**
  1. A user who legitimately administers company A can write custom-field values onto **any entity
     UUID in company B**, stamped with company A's `company_id`. The write succeeds and is
     indistinguishable from a legitimate one.
  2. Read-side amplification: `get_values` (`custom_fields.py:236-243`) queries by
     `entity_type + entity_id` **only — not by company** — and then performs its tenant check as
     `if values: get_company_membership(db, current_user, values[0].company_id)`. Two things follow.
     Only the **first** row's company is ever checked, so a set of rows spanning two companies is
     released to a member of whichever company happens to sort first. And a poisoned row from
     company A landing first will **403 company B's own users out of their own entity's values** —
     the injected row becomes a denial of service on a record its owner cannot see or delete.
  3. `if values:` means an empty result is returned with **no membership check at all**, so the
     endpoint is a probe for whether an arbitrary UUID has custom-field values.
- **Note on severity:** Round 3 recorded tenant isolation as "verified genuinely good — all endpoints
  guarded". That verdict was based on the presence of a guard, and this endpoint has one. It is the
  *object* of the guard that is wrong: the caller names the tenant instead of the record naming it.
  **That is a different check from the one Round 3 ran, and other endpoints accepting a
  `company_id` in the body should be re-examined the same way** (`chat.create_group` at
  `chat.py:110-112` has the identical shape).
- **Not exercised live.** Proving it requires writing a value onto a UUID outside the founder's
  company, which is out of the rules of engagement. The reasoning is from source and is not
  conditional on runtime state.
- **Fix:** resolve the entity from `entity_type` + `entity_id`, derive `company_id` from the record,
  and require permission against **that**; ignore `payload.company_id`. Filter `get_values` by the
  derived company and check membership before returning, including for the empty case.

### FINDING R2-158 — 🟠 HIGH: a `date` custom field cannot be given a date from this screen — the value is collected, marked required, and never sent

- The value modal renders a **required** `<input type="date">` bound to `valueForm.value_date` when
  the selected field's `field_type` is `date` (`d/custom-fields/page.tsx:254-258`).
- The request body built by `handleSetValue` (`:105-115`) contains `field_id`, `entity_type`,
  `entity_id`, `company_id`, `value_text` and conditionally `value_number`. **`value_date` is not in
  it.** The server's `CustomFieldValueCreate` accepts `value_date` (`custom_fields.py:54`) and the
  column exists, so the field is simply dropped in transit.
- **Consequence:** the browser blocks submission until a date is entered, then stores
  `value_text: ""` and no date. The toast says "Value saved". Every date custom field set from this
  screen is empty.
- The same handler carries a second defect: `if (!(body.value_number === 0 && valueForm.value_text)) body.value_number = valueForm.value_number;`
  (`:112-114`) — a number field whose legitimate value is `0` is omitted whenever any text was
  typed, and `value_number: 0` is sent for text-only fields, writing a numeric zero into every text
  value row.
- Note the contrast: the shared `CustomFieldsSection` component and `upsert_values_for_entity` handle
  all six types correctly by dispatching on `field_type` (`custom_fields.py:144-160`). This screen
  reimplements that dispatch by hand and gets it wrong.

### FINDING R2-159 — 🟡 MEDIUM: `field_type` and `entity_type` are unconstrained strings on both create paths

- `CustomFieldCreate.field_type` and `.entity_type` are bare `str` with no `pattern=` and no
  `Literal` (`custom_fields.py:16-22`) — the R2-136 class, now with a consequence: the normaliser
  dispatches on exact string equality (`== "number"`, `== "date"`, `== "multiselect"`,
  `== "checkbox"` at `custom_fields.py:144-160`) and **falls through to `value_text` for anything
  else**. A field created with `field_type: "Number"` or `"decimal"` through the API stores its
  values as text, and every downstream numeric use of it is wrong without any error.
- The two UI selects happen to emit correct values, so this is reachable only via the API today —
  which is exactly how the `invoice_type` outage (R2-011) began.

## Calculators — the 7 tabs not yet audited (formula review)

Round 2 covered disclosure of wastage (R2-004) and the fact that the console never calls the backend
(R2-010). This pass reads the **formulas** of Slab Steel, Two-Way Slab, RMC, Paint, Tile,
Waterproofing and House Cost, and compares them against `backend/app/routers/calculators.py`.

### FINDING R2-160 — 🟠 HIGH: the Concrete calculator's "Column" mode silently reuses the Steel Column calculator's inputs, so two tabs corrupt each other

- **Where:** `d/reports/calculators/page.tsx:229-231`.
  ```
  if (concreteForm === "column") {
    vol = (sizeA / 1000) * (sizeB / 1000) * (colHeight / 1000);
  }
  ```
  `sizeA`, `sizeB` and `colHeight` are the **Steel Column** tab's state (declared `:34-37`, bound to
  the Steel Column inputs at `:480`). The Concrete tab's Column form binds the *same* state
  (`:849-855`), so the two calculators share one set of variables.
- **Consequences:**
  1. Sizing a 450×300 column for steel, then switching to Concrete → Column, silently carries those
     numbers over. Changing them in either tab rewrites the other tab's answer, with no indication
     that a value entered on one screen has changed a result on another.
  2. In Column mode the Concrete tab's own Length/Width/Depth inputs (`concreteL/W/D`) are **ignored**
     — they remain on screen and editable, and typing in them changes nothing.
  3. The column volume takes no count input, so a 4-column pour must be computed one column at a
     time, while the RMC tab's column mode *does* have a count (`rmcColCount`, `:104`). Two column
     volume calculators on one screen, with different capabilities and different state.
- **Fix:** give the Concrete tab its own column dimension state, and honour the visible L/W/D inputs
  or hide them in that mode.

### FINDING R2-161 — 🟠 HIGH: every number in the House Construction Cost calculator is invented, and the output is presented as a rupee total

- **Where:** `page.tsx:344-384`. The result is built entirely from constants written into the
  component:
  | Constant | Value | Basis given |
  |---|---|---|
  | Base rate ₹/sqft | budget 1600 · standard 2200 · premium 3400 | none |
  | City multiplier | Mumbai 1.25 · Delhi 1.20 · Bengaluru 1.18 · Pune 1.15 · Hyderabad 1.10 · Jaipur 0.95 · Lucknow 0.90 | none |
  | Per-floor escalation | `1.0 + 0.12 * f` — every storey costs 12% more than the one below | none |
  | Compound wall | `length_ft × base_rate × 0.35` | none |
  | Trade split | Structure 40% · Finishing 25% · MEP 15% · Interior 12% · Misc 8% | none |
  - There is no source, no "indicative only" caption, no as-of date, and no way for the user to
    substitute their own rate — unlike every other calculator on the page, which takes its rates as
    inputs (`steelPrice`, `cementRate`, `brickPrice`, `rmcRate` …).
- **Why this one matters more than a wrong constant:** the output is a **₹ figure for a whole house**,
  rendered large with a trade breakdown and a contingency line. It is the most quotable number in the
  product and the only one with no user-supplied rate behind it. It is also exactly the class of
  fabricated metric that was scrubbed from the marketing site.
- **Fix:** make the base rate an input with the current constant as a labelled default, cite the
  basis of the city and floor multipliers or drop them, and caption the result as indicative.

### FINDING R2-162 — 🟡 MEDIUM: the House Cost currency selector is dead, and Riyadh is priced in US dollars

- `page.tsx:358`: `const effCurrency = cityData.cur || houseCurrency;`. Every entry in `CITY_MAP`
  (`:345-356`) defines `cur`, and `cityData` falls back to the `default` entry which also defines it.
  The right-hand side of `||` is therefore **unreachable** — the currency `<select>` rendered at
  `:1536` sets `houseCurrency`, which can never affect the output. A dead control of the same kind as
  R2-012.
- The city list maps **Riyadh, KSA → `USD`** (`:355`) with a 0.90 multiplier, so Saudi costs are
  quoted in dollars at a rate derived from an Indian ₹/sqft table. Dubai is priced in AED at a
  separate hardcoded rate (180/240/380 per sqft).
- **Fix:** delete the selector or let it override; price KSA in SAR.

### FINDING R2-163 — 🟠 HIGH: the console and the API compute a *different* house cost — R2-010's duplication has produced a live divergence

R2-010 recorded that the console never calls `/apis/v3/calculators` and that the math is implemented
twice. This is what the two implementations now disagree about for the same house:

| | Console (`page.tsx:344-384`) | API (`calculators.py:168-198`) |
|---|---|---|
| Contingency | **included** in the headline total (`totalCost = subtotal + contingency`, `:379-380`) | **excluded** — `total_project_cost` is pre-contingency, buffer returned separately (`:186-196`) |
| Trade splits computed on | the total **including** contingency (`:1934`) | the total **excluding** it (`:181-185`) |
| Default base rate | 1600 / 2200 / 3400 by quality tier | single `base_rate` field, default **2000** (`:161`) |
| City multiplier | 10 cities, 0.90–1.25 | **does not exist** |
| Commercial uplift | **does not exist** | `is_commercial` → `×1.10` (`:175-176`) |
| Default contingency | 10% (`:158`) | 12% (`:165`) |
- **Consequences:** the same inputs produce different answers depending on whether they arrive through
  the screen or the API — and any integration, export or future report built on the endpoint will
  disagree with what the user was shown. The console's splits also **double-count the contingency**:
  five percentages summing to 100% are applied to a total that already contains the buffer, so the
  buffer is silently redistributed across the trades and then shown again on its own line.
- **Fix:** delete one implementation. The backend one is the better base (it already has the
  commercial flag and keeps the buffer separate) but it needs the city/quality tables; the console
  should call it.

### FINDING R2-164 — 🟡 MEDIUM: Paint applies three undisclosed allowances and hardcodes opening sizes (extends R2-004)

- `page.tsx:305-309`: `litres = (area / coverage) * coats * 1.10`, `puttyKg = (area/100) * 2.25 * 1.10`,
  `primerL = (area / 175) * 1.05`. Three separate hidden multipliers, none of them exposed as a
  wastage input — the Paint tab has **no wastage field at all**, unlike Steel, Concrete, RMC, Bricks,
  Tile, Plaster and Waterproofing, all of which do.
- Openings are deducted at fixed rates — `doorsCount * 21.0` sqft and `windowsCount * 12.0` sqft
  (`:302`) — with no way to enter actual sizes.
- The backend agrees on all five constants (`calculators.py:260-273`), so this is a shared convention
  rather than a divergence — but it is still undisclosed on screen, which is precisely the R2-004
  defect. R2-004's table should gain Paint's putty and primer lines.

### Verified correct — do not re-audit
- **Slab Steel and Two-Way Slab bar geometry** (`page.tsx:191-221`). Both compute bar count along the
  perpendicular span and cut length along the bar's own span, plus development length at both ends:
  main bars `ceil(Ly/spacing)+1` at `(Lx + 2·Ld)`, distribution `ceil(Lx/spacing)+1` at `(Ly + 2·Ld)`.
  Dimensionally consistent and matching standard practice. Unit weight is the `D²/162` kg/m
  convention throughout, correctly applied.
- **Tile** (`:317-324`): grout converted mm→inch (`/25.4`) and added to both tile dimensions before
  converting to feet — the tile *module* rather than the tile face, which is right.
- **Waterproofing** (`:339-341`): the only calculator that exposes coverage, coats **and** wastage as
  inputs. No hidden constants.
- **RMC** (`:255-269`): per-shape volumes are dimensionally correct and trucks are `ceil(vol/mixer)`.
- **Bricks mortar volume** (`:277-292`): wall volume minus net brick solid volume, then ×1.33 dry
  factor, cement by 1440 kg/m³ ÷ 50 kg. Correct, and it uses the pre-wastage brick count for the
  deduction, which is the right choice.
- `/apis/v3/calculators/*` requires authentication (`calculators.py:8`); it is not an open endpoint.

## Mobile viewport (375×812, pane visible and compositing)

Method: viewport set to the `mobile` preset, then for each page a rendered screenshot **plus** a DOM
measurement of `documentElement.scrollWidth` against `innerWidth` and of every element whose
`scrollWidth` exceeds its `clientWidth`. Screenshots alone would not distinguish "scrolls inside its
own container" (fine) from "clipped by an ancestor with `overflow:hidden`" (broken) — that
distinction produced R2-166.

### FINDING R2-165 — 🟠 HIGH: Chat has no responsive layout at all; on a phone the message pane is 171 px wide

- **Measured live at 382 px viewport:** the conversation sidebar is **288 px** and the message pane
  gets **171 px** (the two overlap the viewport because the sidebar is `shrink-0`).
- **Where:** `d/chat/page.tsx:292` — `className="w-72 bg-card border-r border-border-custom flex
  flex-col shrink-0"`. A fixed `w-72` (288 px) that is explicitly forbidden from shrinking, on a
  375 px device.
- **A grep for Tailwind breakpoint prefixes (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`) across the entire 848-line chat page
  returns zero hits.** There is no small-screen branch anywhere in the file.
- **Rendered result** (screenshot taken): the empty-state text wraps to one or two words per line —
  "Chat / Group / (Beta / Version)" stacked vertically down a 171 px column. With a conversation
  open, the composer would be worse: the message input carries `min-w-[200px]` (`:545`) and the image
  URL box `w-44` (176 px) side by side in the same flex row (`:552`), i.e. 376 px of minimum content
  inside a 171 px pane.
- **Why it matters here specifically:** chat is the one module in this product whose primary device
  *is* the phone — it exists so site staff can post updates and MOM from the field. It is the least
  usable page on a phone in the console.
- **Fix:** collapse to a single pane below `md`, with the conversation list as a drawer; stack the
  composer inputs.

### FINDING R2-166 — 🟠 HIGH: on Attendance the mobile header is clipped by an `overflow:hidden` ancestor, so its right-hand controls cannot be reached at all

- **Measured:** the header band `border-b border-border-custom bg-background px-6 py-3 flex …` has
  `scrollWidth 494` against `clientWidth 375`, and its parent `flex-1 flex flex-col overflow-hidden`
  has the same 494 vs 375 with **`overflow-x: hidden`**.
- **Consequence:** 119 px of the header is not merely off-screen, it is **unreachable** — the parent
  refuses to scroll and the band itself is `overflow: visible`, so there is no scroll container to
  drag. The screenshot shows a button truncated mid-word at the right edge ("La…"). The page-level
  `documentElement.scrollWidth` equals `innerWidth`, so nothing about the page suggests content is
  missing; a phone user simply never sees that control exists.
- This is the failure mode a screenshot-only check would have called "looks a bit tight". It is also
  the opposite of the Budget page, which was measured on the same viewport and is **correct**: its
  wide table sits in an `overflow-x: auto` container (`scrollWidth 577` / `clientWidth 320`) and
  scrolls, with no page-level overflow.
- **Fix:** let the header wrap (`flex-wrap`) below `md`, or give it its own `overflow-x-auto`.

### FINDING R2-167 — 🟠 HIGH: the Attendance page opens on a hardcoded date — 30 June 2026 — and will drift further every day

- **Where:** `d/attendance/page.tsx:148` — `const [date, setDate] = useState("2026-06-30");`
- **Live:** the date picker read `2026-06-30` against a browser clock of `2026-07-26`. **26 days
  stale**, and the gap grows without bound.
- `date` feeds the log fetch `GET /apis/v3/hr/attendance/{project_id}/{date}` (`:320`, re-run on
  `[projectId, date]` at `:334`), so **Worker Attendance Log always opens on a day that is not
  today**. For any company that started using the product after that date, the default view is
  permanently empty, which reads as "nobody punched in".
- It compounds R2-105 (punches are never POSTed) and R2-137 (a failed fetch and an empty day render
  identically): three independent reasons for this log to look empty, none of them visible to the
  user.
- The date is **not** used when recording a punch, so it does not misdate attendance — only the read
  view is affected. That bound was checked: `date` appears in exactly one fetch.
- **Fix:** `useState(new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10))`. Then grep for the same pattern — a
  literal date string in a `useState` is mechanically findable and this is unlikely to be the only one.

### Re-tested live on mobile, still unfixed
- **R2-106** — the production Attendance screen still renders **"Simulate GPS lock (On-Site)" checked
  by default**, next to a "Geofence: Active" badge. Confirmed by screenshot this session.
- **R2-105** — "Sync Offline Queue (0)" is still present and still labelled as a sync.

### Verified good on mobile — do not re-audit
- **Budget** (`/d/budget`): no page-level horizontal overflow; KPI cards reflow to a 2×2 grid; the
  wide comparison table scrolls inside its own `overflow-x-auto` container. This is the pattern the
  other pages should copy.
- **Custom Fields** (`/d/custom-fields`): header, description, primary action and empty state all
  reflow correctly at 375 px.
- On both pages, exactly one interactive control measured under 32 px in either dimension (out of 23
  on Budget) — tap-target sizing is not a systemic problem.

### FINDING R2-168 — 🟠 HIGH: the hardcoded-date defect is systemic — five frozen dates across four screens, including the payroll month

R2-167 predicted that a literal date in a `useState` would not be the only one. A mechanical sweep of
`frontend/src` for `useState("YYYY-MM-DD")` and `useState("YYYY-MM")` returns **five** hits, all
still frozen in the past relative to today (2026-07-26):

| File | Line | Frozen value | Days stale | What it drives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `d/attendance/page.tsx` | 148 | `2026-06-30` | 26 | attendance log fetch (R2-167) |
| `p/[project_id]/attendance/page.tsx` | 144 | `2026-06-30` | 26 | same screen, project route |
| `d/hr/page.tsx` | 234 | `2026-06-26` | 30 | `GET /hr/attendance/{pid}/{selectedDate}` (`:293`) **and the visible heading** "Daily Attendance — 2026-06-26" (`:751`) |
| `d/hr/page.tsx` | 235 | `2026-06` | ~1 month | `payrollMonth` — the month the payroll screen operates on |
| `d/todo/page.tsx` | 55 | `2026-12-05` | future | recurrence "Ends" date (R2-149) |

- **The HR one is the worst of the set:** the screen *prints the stale date in its own heading*
  ("Daily Attendance — 2026-06-26"), so the UI states the date it is showing and is simply wrong
  about which day the user wanted. And `payrollMonth` defaulting to `2026-06` means the payroll
  screen opens on the **previous month** — on a screen where picking the wrong month is a payroll
  error, not a display error.
- **Shared root cause:** these are all seed values left from development. The fix is one line each
  (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, and `.slice(0,7)` for the month), and the grep above is
  the complete list — this class is now **bounded at five**, like the two classes bounded in Round 3.
- Recommend a lint rule (`no-magic-date`) or a shared `todayISO()` helper, because the same seed
  values will be reintroduced by the next screen built from a copy of one of these.

## Write-tests — chat and RBAC (founder authorised writes in the QA company)

All records below use the founder's `ZZ QA` convention. Cleanup is disclosed at the end.

### ✅ R2-140, R2-141, R2-143 — all three now VERIFIED LIVE, not inferred

Sequence run against the production API with the owner's own token, in the owner's own company:

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `POST /chat/groups` **with** `created_by = localStorage.user_id` (`7f6c0bcf…`, a `users.id`) | **request died — `TypeError: Failed to fetch` after 1.56 s**, and **no group row exists afterwards** |
| 2 | `POST /chat/groups` **without** `created_by` | **201** — `{id: a0beb919…, created_by: null, member_count: 0}` |
| 3 | `GET /chat/messages/{gid}` as the company **owner** | **403 `{"detail":"Not a member of this chat group"}`** |
| 4 | `GET /chat/groups/{gid}/members` as the owner | **403 `{"detail":"Not a member of this chat group"}`** |
| 5 | `DELETE /chat/groups/{gid}` | **405 `{"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}`** |
| 6 | `POST /chat/groups/{gid}/members` adding **myself** as admin | **403 `{"detail":"Not a member of this chat group"}`** |

- **R2-140 confirmed exactly as predicted.** The company owner — `priority_type: partner`,
  `permissions: {all: true}` — is refused read access to a chat group in their own company, because
  the membership filter compares a `users.id` against a `company_team.id` column.
  The two IDs were both captured this session and are different values for the same person:
  `users.id = 7f6c0bcf-fb15-4de1-b1ad-9acbfc02c7a1`,
  `company_team.id = e9db5738-4b36-4a81-8ded-86d52cc8e2c5` (from `GET /crm/team-members/{cid}`).
- **New, worse than filed — the group is in a permanent deadlock (row 6).** `add_member` is itself
  guarded by `verify_group_membership` (`chat.py:230`), so **adding the first member requires already
  being a member.** A group created without `created_by` can never acquire one. Combined with
  R2-143, *both* creation paths produce an unusable group: with `created_by` the request fails, and
  without it the group is born empty and can never be joined. **There is no sequence of API calls
  that produces a working chat group.** The feature is not degraded, it is inoperable.
- **R2-141 confirmed:** 405 on delete, exactly as read from the route table.
- **R2-143 confirmed, with one correction to what was filed.** The predicted FK violation happens,
  but it happens on the **group insert itself**, not on the member insert: `chat_groups.created_by`
  is *also* `ForeignKey("company_team.id")` (`models.py:1633`), and `create_group` builds the row with
  `ChatGroup(**payload.model_dump())` (`chat.py:112`). So the first commit fails and the whole request
  rolls back. **There is no orphan group row** — the "group row is committed first" wording in
  R2-143 is wrong and should read: *the request fails outright and nothing is created*. The
  user-visible result is the same (the modal closes having done nothing, per `if (res.ok)` with no
  `else`), and the caller-supplied-identity defect is unchanged.
- **Secondary observation worth its own note:** the 500 reached the browser as **`TypeError: Failed
  to fetch`**, not as a status code — an unhandled server exception returns a response without CORS
  headers, so the browser refuses it and the client cannot distinguish a server crash from the
  network being down. That is why R2-137's missing `else` branches would not have helped here even
  if they existed: `res` never arrives. Any error-handling work should include a global exception
  handler that returns a CORS-bearing 500 (this also covers R2-139).

### FINDING R2-169 — 🔴 CRITICAL: R2-073's precondition is confirmed — the API accepts and stores an empty permission set

- `POST /apis/v3/settings/roles/{company_id}` with body `{"role_name": "ZZ QA Empty Role",
  "permissions": {}}` returned **200** and persisted `"permissions": {}` verbatim.
- `validate_permissions` (`permissions.py:101-118`) iterates the submitted keys and rejects unknown
  ones — an empty dict has no keys to reject, so it passes and returns `{}`.
- `require_permission` then treats that stored `{}` as "un-migrated tenant" and **returns early,
  granting everything** (`auth.py:103-105`).
- The chain is now proved at every step except the final 403-vs-200 on a real request, which still
  requires a **second, non-owner member** — the owner is `priority_type: partner` and passes the
  guard before the permissions are ever consulted (`auth.py:92-94`), so no owner-driven test can
  exercise it. That remains the one blocked item.
- **This is the D7 decision.** Recommended answer: empty means empty. Keep a one-time migration
  fallback keyed on a column (`permissions_migrated_at IS NULL`), not on the emptiness of the dict.

### FINDING R2-170 — 🟠 HIGH: three permissions the server requires cannot be granted by any means — confirmed mechanically and live

Computing the canonical key set from `permissions.py` (18 `MODULES` × view/edit, `:approve` only for
the 6 `WORKFLOW_MODULES`, plus 4 global keys) and diffing it against every key passed to
`require_permission` across all routers gives exactly three orphans:

| Required key | Endpoint it guards | What becomes impossible |
|---|---|---|
| `attendance:approve` | `hr.py:503` | approving a submitted timesheet |
| `drawings:approve` | `drawings.py:237` | approving a drawing revision |
| `reports:approve` | `reports.py:201` | approving a report |

- **Confirmed live:** `PUT /settings/roles/{rid}/permissions` with `{"indent:approve": true}` and
  `{"po:approve": true}` both returned **400 `Unknown permission key`**, while
  `{"billing:approve": true}` (a real workflow module) returned 200. The taxonomy is enforced exactly
  as computed.
- **Consequence:** for any role with a non-empty permission set, those three approvals are permanently
  403 — the key required to pass cannot be written into the role. Taken with R2-169 the system has
  only two reachable states: a role with **no** permissions configured (which can do *everything*, via
  fail-open) or a role with permissions configured (which can never do these three). There is no
  configuration that grants exactly these.
- **Fix:** add `attendance`, `drawings` and `reports` to `WORKFLOW_MODULES` — a one-line change that
  makes all three keys grantable, and the whole of R2-074/R2-112 with it.

### FINDING R2-171 — 🔴 CRITICAL: two seeded roles hold nine permission keys that no longer exist in the taxonomy, and those roles can no longer be saved at all

- Read live from `GET /settings/roles/{cid}`: **Manager** holds **50** keys and **Project partner**
  holds **49**, including `crm:approve`, `safety:approve`, `quality:approve`, `reports:approve`,
  `drawings:approve`, `planning:approve`, `projects:approve`, `equipment:approve`,
  `attendance:approve`, `production:approve` — **ten `:approve` keys for modules that are not in
  `WORKFLOW_MODULES`**, i.e. keys `validate_permissions` now rejects.
- **Proved live:** reading Manager's permissions and `PUT`ting them back **unchanged** returns
  **400 `Unknown permission key: 'crm:approve'`**. The role cannot be re-saved even with no edit
  applied. **Manager and Project partner are permanently un-editable through the API** — and
  therefore through the Roles & Access matrix, which uses this endpoint.
- **Two ways this bites, and they pull in opposite directions:**
  1. **Locked out of editing.** An admin who opens Manager, changes one checkbox and presses Save
     gets a 400 naming a key they never touched and cannot see. (Per R2-073 the safe response — press
     Cancel — is also the only working one.)
  2. **Or worse, silently downgraded.** If the matrix editor submits only the keys it knows how to
     render, the ten unknown keys are **dropped**, and Manager silently loses its approve rights on
     the next save of any unrelated checkbox. Which of the two happens depends on how the matrix
     builds its payload — **this needs checking before anyone edits a role in production**, and it is
     the reason R2-073's "do not press Save" instruction should stay in force.
  3. Meanwhile at runtime those keys **do** work: `has_permission` is a plain dict lookup
     (`permissions.py:78-82`), so a Manager today really can approve attendance and drawings — using
     keys that the system will refuse to write ever again. Enforcement and configuration disagree
     about what the permission model contains.
- **Root cause:** the seed presets (`DEFAULT_ROLE_PRESETS`) were written against a wider taxonomy
  than `permissions.py` now defines, and nothing validates the presets against
  `ALL_PERMISSION_KEYS` at seed time or in a test.
- **Fix:** a startup/migration check that validates every stored role against the canonical set and
  reports drift; add the missing modules to `WORKFLOW_MODULES` (which resolves most of the drift at a
  stroke, per R2-170); and add a test that asserts `validate_permissions(preset)` succeeds for every
  preset.

### Auditor disclosure — records created and cleaned up
- **`ZZ QA Empty Role`** (`4dd1689b…`) — created, used for the permission probes, **deleted** (204).
  `GET /settings/roles` now returns the original 11 roles: Owner, Admin, Client, Accountant,
  Sub Contractor, Associate HR, Project partner, Site Engineer, Manager, Supervisor, Viewer.
- **`ZZ QA Audit Chat B`** (`a0beb919-1c9d-4e25-8314-3fdd587b1ab0`) — created, and **cannot be
  deleted by the auditor because the delete route does not exist (R2-141)**. It is invisible in the
  UI's message pane (403, R2-140) but will appear in the chat sidebar list. Removing it needs a
  direct DB delete or the `is_archived` flag; it is inert either way.
- Manager's permissions were read and re-submitted unchanged; the request **400'd, so nothing was
  written**. No role's permissions were modified.
- The failed `POST /chat/groups` rolled back completely; verified by listing groups afterwards.

### ⚠️ CORRECTION TO R2-073 — the "Clear All grants full access" claim is DISPROVED; the fail-open is real but not reachable that way

R2-073 was carried as the **#1 CRITICAL** and as the reason for the standing instruction "do not press
Save in Roles & Access". Tested directly this session, and it does not behave as filed.

**What was tested.** A throwaway role was created, then given an all-`false` permission set — the
exact payload the matrix editor produces after "Clear All" — and read back:
```
PUT /settings/roles/{rid}/permissions  {"permissions": {"projects:view": false, "projects:edit": false, … }}
→ 200 {"billing:edit":false,"billing:view":false,"finance:edit":false,…}   (10 keys, all false)
```
**The stored dict is non-empty.** `require_permission`'s fail-open is `if not role_perms: return`
(`auth.py:103-105`) — a dict with ten `False` values is **truthy**, so the guard does not trigger;
execution falls through to `has_permission`, which returns `False` for every key, and the role is
correctly denied everything.

**Why the original reading was wrong.** The matrix editor never sends a sparse dict. `buildInitialDraft`
seeds the draft with **every** key in the frontend taxonomy (`RolePermissionsModal.tsx:29-35`),
`setAll(false)` writes `false` into every one of them (`:66-72`), and `save` posts the whole draft
(`:80-84`). "Clear All" therefore produces ~40 explicit `false`s, not `{}`. There is no UI path that
submits an empty permission object.

**What remains true, and is still CRITICAL — see R2-169.** The fail-open itself is real and is
reachable: `POST /settings/roles/{cid}` with `"permissions": {}` is accepted and stored as `{}`
(verified, 200), and any role in that state grants **everything**. That is an API-reachable state and
also the state of any role that predates the permissions migration. **D7 still needs answering** and
the fail-open should still be removed — but it is a latent-state defect, not a
"one click in the UI grants full access" defect.

**Practical effect on the standing instruction:** pressing Save in Roles & Access does not grant full
access. It is still not safe to press, for a different reason — **R2-171**: the modal drops the ten
out-of-taxonomy keys Manager and Project partner hold, so saving those two roles *silently removes*
approve rights. Keep the "press Cancel" rule, cite R2-171 as its reason.

**Method note for the next session.** This was disproved by exercising the exact payload the UI sends
rather than by reasoning about what "empty" means. Round 3's summary line — "role editor's Clear All
grants full access" — was the most severe claim in the audit and it survived a round unchallenged
because nobody had a safe way to test it. The test was safe all along: a throwaway role, never
assigned to anyone, deleted afterwards.

### FINDING R2-172 — 🔴 CRITICAL: the permissions modal silently strips any stored key it does not recognise, so saving Manager or Project partner revokes ten approve rights without saying so

- `buildInitialDraft` (`RolePermissionsModal.tsx:29-35`) builds the draft by iterating the
  **frontend's** `ALL_PERMISSION_KEYS` (`lib/rbac.ts:90-97`) and reading each key out of the stored
  permissions. Keys present in storage but absent from that list are **not copied into the draft**,
  and `save` sends only the draft (`:84`).
- Manager holds 50 keys and Project partner 49, of which **ten** (`crm:approve`, `safety:approve`,
  `quality:approve`, `reports:approve`, `drawings:approve`, `planning:approve`, `projects:approve`,
  `equipment:approve`, `attendance:approve`, `production:approve`) are outside both taxonomies —
  read live this session, see R2-171.
- **Therefore:** an admin who opens Manager, ticks one unrelated checkbox and saves sends a payload
  containing none of those ten. The server validates it happily (every remaining key is canonical),
  returns **200 "Permissions saved"**, and Manager loses ten approval rights. Nothing in the UI ever
  displayed those rights, so nothing appears to change. This is a **silent privilege revocation with
  a success toast**.
- It also resolves the open question in R2-171: of the two possible behaviours, this is the one that
  happens. The direct-API path 400s (proved: re-saving Manager's own permissions verbatim returns
  `400 Unknown permission key: 'crm:approve'`); the **UI path succeeds and drops them**. The two
  paths disagree about the same operation.
- **Fix:** merge unknown stored keys back into the payload untouched (or surface them in the matrix
  as read-only rows flagged "not in current taxonomy"), and fix the taxonomy drift at the root by
  adding the missing modules to `WORKFLOW_MODULES` (R2-170).

**Cleanup:** `ZZ QA ClearAll Role` (`4cdd0571…`) deleted (204). The company's 11 original roles are
intact and unmodified; no existing role's permissions were written at any point.

## Closing Round 2's open UNVERIFIED item — the project Transaction page

Round 2's handoff recorded, deliberately unfiled, that `/c/{cid}/p/{pid}/transaction` rendered
`Loading…` with `TOTAL IN ₹0` / `MARGIN ₹0` late in a degraded session, and asked a later session to
re-open it **with the pane visible** before concluding anything. Done, this session.

**Result: half the observation was throttling, half is a real bug.**
- The three bills **do** render (₹1,18,000 sale, two ₹11,800 purchases) and **MARGIN shows
  ₹80,000.00**, not ₹0. That part of Round 2's observation was a hidden-pane artifact, correctly not
  filed.
- **`TOTAL IN ₹0.00`, `TOTAL OUT ₹0.00` and `PROJECT BALANCE ₹0.00` are real and reproduce with the
  pane visible** — while the server reports ₹90,000 received on this project. New finding below.

### Re-tested from Round 2's dismissal list (pane visible)
- **Theme toggle — genuinely works.** Clicking it moved `documentElement` from no theme class to
  `light-theme`, `body` background from `rgb(17,17,19)` to `rgb(243,244,246)`, and wrote
  `localStorage.theme`. Toggled back to dark; the founder's setting is as it was. Round 2's
  dismissal stands.

### FINDING R2-173 — 🔴 CRITICAL: the project Transaction page reports ₹0 received on a project the server says has ₹90,000 in

- **Screen vs API, same project, same minute:**
  | | Screen | `GET /apis/v3/finance/transactions/{cid}` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Total In | **₹0.00** | **`in_total: 90000.0`** |
  | Project Balance (In − Out) | **₹0.00** | in 90,000 / out 0 |
  | Payment rows | none | `Payment In … 50000` (Approved) and a second part-payment, both carrying `project_id: a1376092…` |
  - The sale invoice on the same screen is labelled **"Partially Paid"**, so the page is
    simultaneously displaying evidence that money arrived and a ₹0 total.
- **Cause** (`p/[project_id]/transaction/page.tsx:181-207`): the summary is computed **only from
  `bills`**. `totalIn` accumulates only when a *bill* has `invoice_type` of `payment_in` or
  `i_received`; actual payment records are a different table and are never fetched by this page.
  Since payments are recorded as payments (not as settlement-type bills), the counter can only ever
  be zero for normal use — the ₹0 is structural, not a data gap.
- **Same family as R2-099** (Finance showing ₹0 against a live ₹1,18,000) and it is the second
  confirmed instance of the pattern: *a financial summary computed client-side from one collection
  while the server already exposes the correct aggregate*. `finance/transactions/{cid}` returns
  `in_total`, `out_total`, `total_invoice`, `unpaid_invoice`, `total_expense` and `unpaid_expense`
  ready-made; the page ignores all six and recomputes two of them wrongly.
- **Secondary defect on the same cards:** `margin` sums `subtotal` (pre-tax) while the ledger rows
  beneath show `total_payable` (post-tax) — ₹80,000 margin from ₹1,00,000 − ₹20,000 sits directly
  above rows reading ₹1,18,000 and ₹11,800. Two tax bases on one screen, neither labelled.
- **Fix:** call `finance/transactions/{cid}` (filtered by project) and render its aggregates, or fetch
  payments alongside bills. Label the margin basis.

### FINDING R2-174 — 🟡 MEDIUM: every party on the Transaction ledger reads as the logged-in user's login name, and the server is the one saying it

- All three bills display **`upadhyayprateek574`** in the Party column — the founder's own account
  name, not a client or vendor. Confirmed to originate server-side: `finance/transactions/{cid}`
  returns `"party": "upadhyayprateek574"` for the sale invoice.
- Note the same response returns `"party": "Walk-in Party"` for the payment rows, so the fallback
  differs by record type within a single endpoint.
- This is the R2-131 party-name family (R2-052, R2-082, R2-087, Labour/Subcon "Unknown") observed on
  a new surface, and it strengthens the case for R2-131's single shared helper: there are now at
  least three distinct wrong answers in production for "who is the counterparty" — the user's login,
  "Walk-in Party", and "Unknown".

## File uploads — tested live against production

Two files were uploaded to the QA project and both round-trips inspected. **The upload pipeline is
real and mostly well built** — which itself corrects an assumption carried since R2-068 ("there is no
upload pipeline behind any of these controls"). There *is* one; the photo-evidence controls simply do
not use it.

**Verified good — do not re-audit**
- `POST /apis/v3/files/upload` → **201**, with a 50 MB cap enforced before the body is buffered
  (`files.py:19,147-151`), an empty-file guard, and inline tenant verification because `project_id`
  arrives as multipart form data rather than in the path (`files.py:137-142` — the comment explains
  exactly why `Depends(verify_project_access)` could not be used, which is correct reasoning).
- Production **is** using object storage, not the DB fallback: `GET /apis/v3/files/file/{id}`
  returned an **opaque redirect** (307 → a Supabase signed URL), not a body. Signed URLs expire in
  **1 hour** (`supabase_storage.py:112`). Private buckets, service-role key server-side only.
- The DB-blob fallback path sanitises `Content-Disposition` against CR/LF/quote injection
  (`files.py:227-229`) — a deliberate, correct defence.
- Download is tenant-checked by resolving the file's project and verifying company membership, with
  the reason commented (`files.py:200-209`).

### FINDING R2-175 — 🟠 HIGH: there is no way to delete an uploaded file, at any level

- `files.py` registers **five** routes — `POST /folders`, `GET /folders`, `GET /files`,
  `POST /upload`, `GET /file/{file_id}`. **There is no `DELETE` for a file or a folder**, and no
  archive flag on `ProjectFile` (`models.py:2127`).
- **Consequence:** every upload is permanent for the life of the tenant. A file uploaded to the wrong
  project, a superseded drawing, a document uploaded with the wrong client's data in it — none can be
  removed through the product. For a construction ERP holding client contracts and drawings, "no
  retraction path" is also a data-protection problem: a deletion request cannot be honoured without
  direct DB and bucket access.
- Same shape as **R2-141** (chat groups cannot be deleted) and it lands the same way in the UI: the
  files page offers no delete control, so nothing looks broken.
- **Direct evidence:** the auditor's own two probe files cannot be cleaned up — see the disclosure
  below. Being unable to undo a write I was authorised to make *is* the finding.
- **Fix:** add `DELETE /files/file/{id}` (removing the storage object and the row, and writing a
  delete-log entry the way the rest of the codebase does), plus a folder delete that refuses when
  non-empty.

### FINDING R2-176 — 🟡 MEDIUM: any file type is accepted, and the `download=1` flag is silently ignored for stored files

- **No content-type or extension allowlist.** Confirmed live: a file named `probe.exe` with
  `Content-Type: application/x-msdownload` uploaded successfully (**201**). `content_type` is taken
  from the client's own multipart header and stored verbatim (`files.py:154`); nothing validates or
  sniffs it.
- **`download` does nothing on the object-storage path.** `GET /files/file/{id}?download=1` returned
  the same 307 redirect as without it — the parameter is only consulted in the DB-blob branch
  (`files.py:224`), which production no longer uses. So the "Download" and "Preview" buttons on the
  files page (`p/[project_id]/files/page.tsx:137,141`) resolve to the same behaviour, and whether a
  file renders in the browser or downloads is decided by the content type the **uploader** chose.
- **Consequence:** an uploaded `text/html` file is served from the Supabase storage domain and will
  render. That domain is not the app origin, so this is not a session-stealing XSS, but it is a
  credible phishing surface hosted on the customer's own infrastructure, reachable by anyone holding
  a 1-hour signed link. Combined with the `.exe` acceptance, the files module will happily distribute
  executables to a construction site's staff.
- **Fix:** allowlist the content types the product actually needs (documents, images, CAD, archives),
  sniff rather than trust the client header, and pass `?download` through to the signed URL as a
  `response-content-disposition` override — Supabase supports it.

### Auditor disclosure — two files that cannot be removed
`ZZ-QA-upload-probe.txt` (`d0f701ac-7573-4f38-85ce-97e77d006bc3`, 24 bytes, text/plain) and
`probe.exe` (`faf4940b-bfa6-4d67-aae6-be3f7fdaf2ca`, **7 bytes, contents `MZ fake`** — not an
executable, a string chosen so the upload would be honest about what it was testing). Both are in the
QA project's file root. **Neither can be deleted through the API (R2-175);** removal needs a DB row
delete plus the `project-files/{project_id}/{file_id}` object in Supabase Storage.

## Edit and delete coverage — systematic sweep of all 43 routers

Method: counted `@router.<verb>` decorators per router, then reconciled every frontend `DELETE` call
site against the backend route table.

### FINDING R2-177 — 🟠 HIGH: 26 routers create records and can never delete them, and the core transactional documents have no general edit either

**Routers with `POST` but zero `DELETE`** (26 of 43). Excluding the ones where it is correct
(`calculators` — pure compute; `auth`, `admin_migrations`, `public_leads`, `profile`,
`google_sheets`, `face_recognition` — not user records), the business-record routers with **no
delete at all** are:

`billing` · `procurement` · `budgeting` · `equipment` · `quality` · `safety` · `assets` · `dpr` ·
`labour` · `production` · `rfq` · `three_way` · `wastage` · `statutory` · `subcon_attendance` ·
`subcon_performance` · `custom_fields` · `files` · `reports`

That covers **bills, purchase orders, indents, GRNs, work packages, equipment records, inspections,
NCRs, daily progress reports, wastage entries, RFQs, asset records, custom field definitions and
uploaded files**.

**And there is no general edit either.** The mutation verbs on those routers are narrow state
transitions, not updates:
| Router | Only non-POST mutation |
|---|---|
| `billing` | `PATCH /bills/{id}/match` (`billing.py:721`) — links a three-way match, nothing else |
| `procurement` | `PATCH /inventory/{id}` (`procurement.py:879`) — stock only; **no PO or indent edit** |
| `equipment` | `PATCH /deployments/{id}/return` (`equipment.py:184`) |
| `quality` | `PATCH /inspections/{id}/respond`, `/ncr/{id}/review`, `/ncr/{id}/close` |

- **Consequence:** a purchase order raised with the wrong vendor, quantity or rate is permanent and
  uncorrectable. So is a mistyped equipment reading, an inspection filed against the wrong tower, a
  DPR for the wrong date. The user's only recourse is to create a second, contradicting record — and
  since committed cost sums **every** PO regardless of status (R2-154), the erroneous one keeps
  counting forever.
- **Where immutability is defensible, the counter-instrument must exist.** For bills it is arguably
  correct — and billing does ship debit notes and credit notes, which is the right pattern. It is not
  defensible for indents, GRNs, equipment, inspections, DPRs, custom field definitions or files, none
  of which have a void/reverse/supersede path either.
- **This also explains the Delete Logs module.** `log_deletion` is called from the handful of routers
  that *can* delete; with 26 routers unable to produce an event, the audit log is near-empty by
  construction — which, with R2-116 (the page never renders a row) and R2-138 (it exhausts the DB
  pool trying), means the compliance feature has three independent reasons to show nothing.
- **Fix:** decide per entity between soft-delete (`is_archived`/`voided_at`, already the pattern on
  `chat_groups.is_archived`) and a reversing document, then implement one of the two for each of the
  19 routers above. Every deletion path that does exist already calls `log_deletion`, so the audit
  trail comes for free.

### Verified — the frontend does not offer deletes that do not exist (one known exception)

All 17 `DELETE` call sites in the console were reconciled against the route table:
project parties, library items, timesheets, todos (both `todos/{id}` and `planning/tasks/todos/{id}`),
holidays, leave templates, approval rules, salary templates, towers, MOM, delete-logs, chat members,
and the three integration disconnects — **every one resolves to a real backend route.**

**The single exception is `DELETE /chat/groups/{id}` (R2-141), already filed and confirmed live as
405.** So the "UI offers an action the API cannot perform" class is now **bounded at one instance**.
The gap is not phantom controls; it is the absence of controls.

## Settings → Multi Level Approval

Live: `GET /apis/v3/settings/approval-rules/{cid}` returns **`[]`** — the company has configured no
rules, so nothing on this screen is currently gating anything. The findings are about what happens
when someone does configure one.

### FINDING R2-178 — 🔴 CRITICAL: the approval-rules screen offers 15 categories; only 2 are consulted by any code, and the other 13 configure nothing

- **The engine exists and is properly built.** `app/approvals.py` provides `find_matching_rule`,
  `match_approver`, `levels_approved`, `user_already_acted` and `record_action`, with a per-level
  sign-off audit trail (`ApprovalAction`, `models.py:1382-1397`).
- **It is wired into exactly two flows.** A repo-wide search for `find_matching_rule` outside its own
  module returns two call sites:
  | Call site | Feature type |
  |---|---|
  | `finance.py:1116` | `PAYMENT_REQUEST_FEATURE_TYPE = "Payment Request"` (`finance.py:1043`) |
  | `procurement.py:428` | `PO_FEATURE_TYPE = "Purchase Order"` (`procurement.py:354`) |
- **The UI offers fifteen** (`settings/page.tsx:476-481`): Asset Transfer, Design Version, Equipment
  Expense, GRN Material, Inspection Form Response, Leave Application, Material Issue, Material
  Purchase, Material Transfer, Material Used, Other Expense, Payment Entries, Payment Request,
  Purchase Order, RFQ.
- **Therefore thirteen of the fifteen are inert.** An admin can build a three-level approval chain for
  GRN Material or Leave Application, name approvers, set amount bands, save it, and see it listed
  back — and **no code path will ever read it**. Material will be received, leave will be granted and
  expenses will be booked with no approval, while the settings screen states the opposite.
- **Severity:** this is a control that a company adopts the product *for*. Unlike a dead button, it
  fails silently, in the direction of permitting things, and only becomes visible during an audit of
  something that already happened. It belongs with R2-105 and R2-148 in the "reports success, does
  nothing" family, but with a compliance blast radius.
- **Fix:** either wire the remaining thirteen (the engine is generic — each needs a `find_matching_rule`
  call at its create/approve boundary, as `procurement.py:428` demonstrates in about ten lines), or
  cut `APPROVAL_CATEGORIES` down to the two that work. Do not ship the list as-is.

### FINDING R2-179 — 🟠 HIGH: enforcement is bound to the UI's category label by exact string match, with the fragility documented in a comment instead of fixed

- Both wired call sites carry the same warning verbatim: *"must match the Settings > Multi Level
  Approval category label exactly"* (`finance.py:1043`, `procurement.py:354`). The link between a
  stored rule and the code that enforces it is the human-readable string `"Purchase Order"`, typed in
  one place in Python and another in TypeScript.
- **Consequences:** renaming a category label in `settings/page.tsx` — a change that looks purely
  cosmetic — **silently detaches enforcement** from every rule already stored under the old label.
  Existing rules keep displaying under the renamed category and stop being applied. The same happens
  for any locale change, trailing space, or case difference.
- `ApprovalRule.feature_type` is an unconstrained `String` with no `pattern=` and no enumeration
  (R2-136 family), so the API accepts any value and the settings screen will happily list a rule for
  a category that no longer exists.
- **Fix:** define the categories once as a shared enum keyed by a stable slug (`purchase_order`), send
  the slug over the wire, and render the label from a lookup. Add a startup assertion that every
  `feature_type` in the database matches a known slug — the same drift check R2-171 needs for
  permission keys, which is the second instance of this exact class today.

## Round 2's hidden-pane dismissals — re-tested against the server

Round 3's instruction was to re-check these before trusting them, because one of the six
("Finance ₹0") turned out to be a real bug (R2-099). Four of the remaining five are now re-tested
**against the API, not the UI**. All four dismissals **stand**.

| Round 2 observation | Re-test | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Theme toggle "does nothing" | clicked live: `documentElement` gained `light-theme`, body background `rgb(17,17,19)` → `rgb(243,244,246)`, `localStorage.theme` written; toggled back | **dismissal stands — works** |
| `POST /library/parties` "hangs" | **200 in 2.3 s**, party created with `party_id_custom: "PID-7"`, then deleted cleanly (`{"success": true}`) | **dismissal stands — throttling** |
| Task progress "not saving" | `PUT /planning/tasks/{id}` `{progress: 76}` → **200**, read back **76**; restored to **75**, read back **75** | **dismissal stands — saves correctly** |
| Project Transaction page `TOTAL IN ₹0` / `MARGIN ₹0` | re-opened with the pane visible | **half wrong** — margin renders ₹80,000, but the ₹0 totals are real: **R2-173** |

Not re-tested: `+ Add Transaction` and `Save Employee` — both create financial/HR records in the
founder's company and neither could be verified without writing one. They remain dismissed on Round
2's evidence only.

### FINDING R2-180 — 🟠 HIGH: every write endpoint accepts unknown fields, ignores them, and returns 200 — a client field-name typo is a silent no-op with a success response

- **Found by making the mistake.** `PUT /planning/tasks/{id}` with `{"progress_percentage": 76}` —
  the wrong name for a field actually called `progress` — returned **200 with the full task body**,
  and the stored value **stayed 75**. Repeating the test deliberately with
  `{"progresss": 99, "nonsense_field": "x"}` also returned **200**, and the value was again unchanged.
- **Cause:** the Pydantic request models are plain `BaseModel`s, so `model_config` defaults to
  `extra="ignore"`. Unknown keys are dropped before the handler sees them, and because these update
  handlers apply fields conditionally (`if payload.x is not None`), an empty-after-filtering payload
  is a valid no-op that still commits and returns the refreshed row.
- **Why it matters beyond typos:** this is the server-side twin of R2-137. The client cannot tell a
  successful write from a discarded one — `res.ok` is true either way, and even a component that
  checks the response body gets a well-formed object back. It converts every future rename or schema
  drift into a silent data-loss bug rather than an error. It is also exactly how a partially-migrated
  frontend would behave after a field rename: everything "saves", nothing changes.
- **Where this compounds findings already filed:** R2-149 (the To-Do repeat payload omits
  `repeat_type`), R2-158 (`value_date` never sent) and R2-143 (`created_by` in the wrong ID space)
  all sit on top of this — in each case the server had the opportunity to reject a payload it could
  not honour and instead returned success.
- **Fix:** set `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` on the request models (FastAPI then returns
  a 422 naming the offending key), and have update handlers 422 on a payload that resolves to zero
  applied fields. Doing this is also the cheapest possible regression test for the entire API surface.

### Cleanup
`ZZ QA Verify Party` (`22ff28a8-4d41-45e7-b1e2-98c5fc2afcfd`) created and deleted (200
`{"success": true}`). The QA task's `progress` is back at its original **75**. No other records
touched by this section.

## Second-identity testing (founder created a second tenant)

The founder signed up a second account, which created its own company —
**`1776c887-5552-4611-aad5-f4899aad0f87` "Test Claude B2 Construction"**, user
`26cc8626-cac8-4891-a4c6-c2cb5c184fdd`, role Owner, `priority_type: partner`. Tenant A remains
`d3724ec3-…` "AK Construction".

### ✅ Tenant isolation — re-verified with a real second identity, and it holds

Every probe below was issued **with tenant B's token against tenant A's resources**:

| Endpoint (A's ids) | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /planning/projects?company_id={A}` | **403** "You do not have access to this company" |
| `GET /billing/bills?project_id={A_project}` | **403** "You do not have access to this project" |
| `GET /finance/transactions/{A}` | **403** |
| `GET /settings/roles/{A}` | **403** |
| `GET /chat/groups/{A_project}` | **403** |
| `POST /custom-fields/fields` with `company_id: {A}` | **403** "User is not a member of the requested company" |
| `GET /custom-fields/fields/{A}?entity_type=project` | **403** |

Round 3's "tenant isolation verified good" verdict is therefore **confirmed by a live second
identity**, not just by reading guards — with one exception, immediately below.

### ✅ R2-157 — the read-side leak is now DEMONSTRATED, not inferred

`GET /custom-fields/values/project/{A_project}` **with tenant B's token returned `200 []`.**

Every other A-scoped endpoint 403'd for this caller; this one answered. That is exactly the code path
filed in R2-157: `get_values` (`custom_fields.py:236-243`) queries by `entity_type + entity_id` with
**no company filter**, then guards with `if values: get_company_membership(db, current_user,
values[0].company_id)` — so an **empty** result skips the tenant check entirely and returns 200.

- **What this proves today:** an authenticated user of any tenant can probe arbitrary UUIDs of any
  other tenant and distinguish "has custom-field values" from "does not", with no membership.
- **What is still inferred, not proven:** that a **non-empty** result would be handed to the wrong
  tenant. Proving it needs a custom-field value to exist on A's project and then a re-probe from B.
  That attempt was **not completed** — see the limitation note below — so R2-157's disclosure leg
  stands on the source reading plus this 200, and its write leg stands on source alone.
